# Kurx — Decision Log

Every entry: **what was ambiguous / blocked → what we chose → why (simplest option satisfying the spec)**.

> **This log is append-only, so it contains superseded decisions by design.** An entry records what was
> decided *on its date*; later entries revise it. Where that has happened the older entry carries an
> explicit ⚠️ **SUPERSEDED / partly superseded** marker naming its replacement — never assume the highest
> D-number on a topic is the only one that matters, and never assume an old entry is still in force.
>
> **Three numbers name two unrelated decisions each — always read both.** Concurrent sessions writing
> this log collided on `D-105`, `D-114` and `D-299`, and the log is append-only so they are not
> renumbered (100+ citations across code and docs point at them). A `grep` for one of these returns two
> different decisions; neither supersedes the other.
>
> | Number | First entry | Second entry |
> |---|---|---|
> | **D-105** | Local toolchain standardised — one Flutter SDK, one Android SDK | Event Chat Phase 2A — lifecycle correctness wiring |
> | **D-114** | Authentication workstream frozen with three open defects (AM0–AM10 handover) | Phase 5 — Presence, typing and read receipts: backend |
> | **D-299** | Two gates that had drifted: the category filter, and the online event that could never publish | Production-readiness audit fixes |
>
> Repeats of `D-101`–`D-104` are **not** collisions: those are lettered sub-decisions (`D-101a`,
> `D-102a`, …) and a plain digit match catches them. `D-266` legitimately carries 11 milestone
> headings (M1–M8 plus addenda). Before claiming a new number, take the highest that exists
> (`grep -oE '^## D-[0-9]+' docs/DECISIONS.md | sort -t- -k2 -n | tail -1`) rather than the last line
> in the file — and re-check it immediately after writing, because another session may have taken it.
>
> **Dated entries below cite documents that no longer exist** — `docs/history/**`, `REMAINING_WORK.md`,
> `BACKEND_ARCHITECTURE_COMPLETION.md`, `PLATFORM_AUDIT_M8.md`, `EVENT_CREATION_V2.md` and others were
> deleted on 2026-08-08 once the code they described had shipped or been replaced. Those citations are
> **provenance**, not live pointers: they record what the decision was made against on its date. Recover
> any of them with `git log --diff-filter=D -- docs/`.
>
> **The current architecture, if you read nothing else:**
>
> | Concern | Current decision |
> |---|---|
> | Who owns an event | **[D-268](#d-268--the-user-owns-the-event-representation-is-an-attribute-and-there-is-no-personal-organization-2026-08-04)** — the User. `events.created_by`. Organizations never own events, and there is no "personal organization" in the domain. |
> | Navigation | **[D-267](#)** — user-first and event-first. Workspace lists your own events; Create Event needs no organization; Representing is a step inside the form. |
> | Authorization | **[D-269](#)** — `IEventAuthority`, one service, one ordered level, one permission table. No service implements its own. |
> | What an event supports | **D-266 M2** — the Capability Engine. It performs **no** authorization, and the event authority performs **no** capability resolution. |
> | Representation & verification | **[D-074](#)** / **[D-075](#)** — organizations are institutions a user *represents*, granted by admin approval. |
>
> Narrative version: [`docs/architecture/event-creation.md`](architecture/event-creation.md).

## D-001 · Clean machine had zero toolchains, no sudo, no Docker
The build machine had no dotnet/node/flutter/docker/brew and no passwordless sudo.
**Chose:** sudo-free installs — .NET 10 SDK via `dotnet-install.sh` → `~/.dotnet`; Node 22 LTS tarball → `~/tools/node`; Flutter stable zip → `~/development/flutter`; PostgreSQL 16 arm64 binaries (zonky embedded-postgres jar) → `~/tools/pg`; Redis built from source → `~/tools/redis`. Docker Desktop cannot be installed headlessly without sudo, so **local dev runs Postgres/Redis natively**; `infra/docker-compose.yml` is still provided per spec for machines that have Docker.
**Why:** unblocks every verification step without admin access; compose file keeps the spec's clean-machine story intact.

## D-002 · Repo directory name
The workspace directory is `~/kurx` (the earlier `~/kuex` was deleted by the user mid-session). All paths in docs assume repo root `kurx/`.

## D-003 · Dev database
Local Postgres cluster lives at `~/tools/pg-data/kurx`, port **5432**, superuser `kurx`, password `kurx`, databases `kurx` (app) and `kurx_test` (tests). Same credentials mirrored in docker-compose so `.env` values work in both setups.

## D-004 · Money type
`long` (Int64) paise everywhere in C#; `bigint` in Postgres. Column names end `_paise`.

## D-005 · Rate limiting
Used **.NET built-in rate limiter** (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting`, ships since .NET 7) instead of AspNetCoreRateLimit — spec allows either; built-in has no extra dependency. OTP-specific limits (3/phone/10min, 10/IP/hour) are enforced in `OtpService` against Postgres (survives restarts), not just the middleware, so tests can assert them deterministically.

## D-006 · IDs
All entity ids are `uuid` (Guid v4, generated app-side). Simplest uniform choice; matches `tickets.code uuid` requirement.

## D-007 · T1 payout parameters (spec gives ranges)
Spec says T1 = cap ₹25k–50k, first advance delayed 4–7 days, reserve 10–15% ~7 days. **Chose defaults:** cap ₹50,000 (5,000,000 paise, configurable in `payout_schedules.cap_paise`), first-advance delay 5 days, reserve 12% for 7 days, weekly runs. T2 = 75% advance, 8% reserve. T3 = 100%, instant, 2% reserve. All stored per-org in `payout_schedules` so ops can tune without code changes.

## D-008 · OTP hashing
OTP codes and refresh tokens are stored hashed (SHA-256). Dev provider prints the raw OTP through the console WhatsApp sender.

## D-009 · JWT signing
HMAC-SHA256 with `JWT_SECRET` env var (dev default in `.env.example` marked NOT FOR PROD). Access 1h, refresh 30d rotated on use; reuse of a rotated refresh token revokes the whole chain.

## D-010 · Slugs
Event/org slugs auto-generated from title (lowercase, dashes), uniquified with a short random suffix on collision. Slug is immutable after publish.

## D-011 · ImageSharp version
SixLabors.ImageSharp 4.0 fails the build without a commercial license key (`$(SixLaborsLicenseKey)`).
**Chose:** pin **3.1.12** (Six Labors Split License — free for OSS/small business, no build-time gate). Revisit only if a 4.x-only feature is needed.

## D-012 · First-login provisioning
OTP verify creates the user row with empty `Name`; the client shows onboarding when `/v1/me` returns `needs_onboarding: true` (i.e. name still empty). OTP policy: 6 digits, 5-minute expiry, max 5 verify attempts per code; limits from D-005 enforced in `AuthService` against Postgres. 10-digit phones are normalized with a `91` prefix. **Superseded on this point by D-089:** `NormalizePhone` no longer infers India from length. A leading `+` is honoured as the caller's stated country; only a number with no `+` at all is still read in the legacy `IN` region, which keeps pre-E.164 clients working without re-homing foreign numbers.

## D-013 · Package pinning
EF Core pinned to **8.0.11** across the solution to match `Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL 8.0.11` (Design at 8.0.16 caused MSB3277 version conflicts). `dotnet-ef` global tool 8.0.28 works but needs `DOTNET_ROOT=$HOME/.dotnet` exported (sudo-free SDK install, D-001).

## D-014 · Refresh-token reuse response
"Revoke the whole chain" (D-009) is implemented as: reuse of an already-rotated refresh token revokes **all** active refresh tokens of that user. Simpler than per-chain lineage tracking and strictly safer.

## D-015 · Org role matrix, member provisioning, org slugs
Spec names roles Owner/Manager/Staff/Finance without a permission matrix.
**Chose:** Owner = full control (sole role that changes roles, removes anyone, adds Manager/Finance/Owner); Manager = edit org profile + add/remove Staff; Finance = KYC/payout endpoints; Staff = read-only; any member may view the org and its member list; anyone may leave, and the last Owner can neither leave nor be demoted (an org always keeps ≥1 Owner). Adding a member by an unknown phone provisions the user row (mirrors D-012 first-login provisioning) so invitees simply log in via OTP later. Org slugs are generated per D-010 and immutable from creation — renaming the org never changes the slug.
**Why:** smallest matrix that keeps money/KYC behind Owner+Finance and org administration behind Owner.

## D-016 · Bank KYC flow and T1 advance percent
KYC providers are mock (synchronous) in dev; D-007 left the T1 advance percent implicit.
**Chose:** penny-drop approval immediately creates the Razorpay Route linked account and sets `payout_account_status=Active` + `bank_last4`; the full account number is **never persisted** (`kyc_records.payload_json` stores masked last4 + provider detail only). A rejection records the attempt but never regresses an already-Active org (failed bank change keeps the old account). PAN match is recorded for review and does not gate payouts by itself. The payout schedule row is seeded at org creation with **tier 1, advance 50%, cap ₹50,000, reserve 12%** (completes D-007).
**Why:** synchronous mock keeps the slice testable offline; storing only last4 avoids holding bank PII we never need.

## D-017 · Phase 1 foundation hardening (secrets, errors, validation, auth, health, logging, SignalR, CI)
Phase 1 asked for production-grade error handling, validation, auth, health checks, logging, and SignalR security without redesigning the existing Clean Architecture. Several implementation choices weren't spelled out:
- **Connection-string strength check**: `SecretValidation.RequireProductionConnectionString` rejects a Production connection string containing the committed `Password=kurx`, mirroring the existing `JWT_SECRET` guard (D-any). Only checks for the known-weak default, not entropy, since a connection string isn't a random secret.
- **Error format**: all error responses — validation failures, expected business errors (403/404/409/...), and unhandled exceptions — are RFC7807 `ProblemDetails`, with the existing string error codes preserved as an `error` extension field (so prior `{error:"..."}` consumers, including tests, keep working unchanged) plus a `correlationId` extension.
- **Validation**: FluentValidation via a generic `IEndpointFilter` (`WithValidation<T>()`) rather than `FluentValidation.AspNetCore` (that package targets MVC, not minimal APIs).
- **KurxAdmin policy**: added as a static ASP.NET Core policy even though no admin-only endpoint exists yet, since `TokenService` already issues the `kurx_admin` claim — the policy just finishes wiring an already-half-built piece. Per-org role checks stay in `OrgService` (D-015) rather than moving to static policies, since the required role varies per org per user and must be looked up per request.
- **SignalR**: `AddSignalR()`/`MapHub()` had never been called at all (hubs were unreachable). Added `[Authorize]` to both hubs, JWT accepted via `?access_token=` query string for `/hubs/*` (browsers can't set headers on WS/SSE), and a membership check on every group join — `SalesHub.JoinOrg` checks org membership directly, `ScanHub.JoinEvent` resolves the event's `OrgId` first.
- **Health checks**: Postgres always; Redis only if `REDIS_CONNECTION` is configured; local-disk storage (writability probe) only when `STORAGE_PROVIDER=localdisk`. Deliberately did **not** add email/SMS checks — only console/mock dev senders exist, so there is no real external dependency to probe yet.
- **Web route protection**: `web/lib/session.ts`'s httpOnly-cookie session helpers already existed but were dead code (`(app)/layout.tsx` had no auth check; `OtpPanel` wrote tokens to `localStorage`). Wired `requireSession()` into the layout and switched `OtpPanel` to the `saveSession` server action instead of adding new session infrastructure.
- **Found in passing**: `web/lib/site.ts`'s `apiBaseUrl` read `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` with a stale `localhost:5050` fallback (real API port is `5080`), and `.env.example` documented a different, non-matching variable name (`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE`) for the web app. Fixed the fallback port and added the correctly-named var to `.env.example`.
**Why:** smallest changes that satisfy each requirement without rewriting working code or blocking Production startup on business features (payments/notifications) that are intentionally still unbuilt.

## D-018 · Phase 2 supersedes the unfinished pre-existing EventService
Before Phase 2, `Kurx.Domain.Entities.Event`/`EventCategory`, `TicketType`/`FormField`, and a full `IEventService`/`EventService` already existed in the repo — but were never registered in DI, never mapped to any endpoint, had zero tests, and their own code comments referenced decision entries ("D-018", "D-022") that didn't exist in this file. Their status enum (`Draft/Live/Completed/Cancelled`) and mandatory ticket-type-to-publish gate don't match the content-management workflow Phase 2 asks for, and conflict with "no Tickets in this phase."
**Chose:** treat this as unfinished scaffolding, not shipped behavior, and complete/align it rather than build a second parallel event system: extended `Event`/`EventCategory` with the new fields, replaced `EventStatus` with `Draft/InReview/Published/Closed/Archived` (`EventStatusWorkflow` is the single source of truth for valid transitions), decoupled publish from ticket types entirely, and rewrote `IEventService`/`EventService` to match. `TicketType`/`FormField` entities and their FK to `Event` are left in the schema untouched for the ticketing phase; only the service methods that manipulated them (which nothing called) were removed from the interface.
- **Authorization**: Owner/Manager may manage their own org's events (same tier as org-profile edits, D-015); a platform admin (`kurx_admin` claim / `KurxAdmin` policy from Phase 1) may manage any org's events. Passed down as `bool isAdmin` alongside `userId` rather than threading `ClaimsPrincipal` into the service layer.
- **Draft visibility**: a non-Published event is only visible via `GetAsync`/`GetBySlugAsync` to an org member or admin; everyone else gets `not_found` (never `403`, so a guessed id can't even confirm a draft exists).
- **Visibility semantics**: `Public` appears in search/upcoming/trending/featured/latest/related. `Unlisted` and `Private` are both excluded from every discovery surface and reachable only by direct id/slug — they behave identically for now; giving `Private` an additional org-membership gate on the direct-link read is deferred (noted here rather than silently skipped).
- **Trending**: no orders/analytics exist yet, so "trending" is genuinely `ViewCount` (incremented once per public detail fetch of a Published event) sorted descending — an honest signal, not fabricated data.
- **Venue**: an event either points at a saved `Venue` (`VenueId` set — its Name/Address/City/Lat/Lng are copied onto the event as a snapshot) or carries ad-hoc venue text/coordinates directly. `City` is denormalized onto `Event` either way so search-by-city doesn't need a join.
**Why:** smallest correct path given Phase 2's explicit "don't redesign the architecture, don't rewrite working code" — nothing was actually working here, so completing it in place avoids a confusing second event system while still respecting the constraint's spirit.

## D-019 · Phase 10 Flutter mobile app — scope, stack, and backend contract
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-08). Flutter application code still gated on the Stage 4 approval; the scaffold begins only after that gate.** Scope and stack are one architectural call, recorded together.

Phase 10 (`.claude/phases/phase10.md`) names an attendee + scanning Flutter app plus a full production-readiness pass as its deliverables, but most of that backend does not exist yet (roadmap "Not built yet": orders, payments, tickets/QR, check-in, notifications, real providers). This decision fixes what the mobile app actually builds against the **source-verified** backend surface, so we never invent APIs, DTOs, or business rules.

**Backend contract (verified in source, not docs):**
- **Auth flow** (`backend/Kurx.Api/Endpoints/AuthEndpoints.cs`, `backend/Kurx.Application/Abstractions/IAuthService.cs`): WhatsApp OTP — `POST /v1/auth/otp/request {phone}` → `{ok:true}` or ProblemDetails (429 `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds`, 400); `POST /v1/auth/otp/verify {phone,code}` → token response or 401; `POST /v1/auth/refresh {refreshToken}` → token response or 401; `POST /v1/auth/logout {refreshToken}` → `{ok:true}`; `GET /v1/me` (Bearer) → `{id,phone,name,username,email,needs_onboarding}`.
- **Token response is snake_case**: `access_token, access_expires_at, refresh_token, refresh_expires_at, user_id, is_new_user`. JWT = HMAC-SHA256, access 1h, refresh 30d rotated; reuse revokes all sessions (D-009/D-014). Bearer token in the `Authorization` header (`backend/Kurx.Api/Program.cs`).
- **Request-body JSON casing**: request records are PascalCase (`Phone`, `Code`, `RefreshToken`) but ASP.NET Core binds case-insensitively, and the published contract (`docs/api/README.md`) is camelCase — the mobile client sends **camelCase request bodies** and parses **snake_case response bodies**.
- **Public discovery** (`backend/Kurx.Api/Endpoints/EventEndpoints.cs`, unauthenticated): `GET /v1/events` (search `q,categoryId,orgId,city,dateFrom,dateTo,sort,page,pageSize`) → `{items:[summary],total}`; `/v1/events/upcoming|trending|featured|latest?limit` → `[summary]`; `/v1/events/{slug}` → full detail (view-counted); `/v1/events/{slug}/related?limit` → `[summary]`. Summary fields (snake_case): `id, org_id, parent_event_id, title, slug, subtitle, banner_key, starts_at, ends_at, status, visibility, venue_name, city`.
- **Public ticket types** (`backend/Kurx.Api/Endpoints/TicketTypeEndpoints.cs`): `GET /v1/events/{eventId}/ticket-types` → on-sale types for a published event (`price_paise` is `long` paise, D-004). **Read-only — no order/purchase endpoint exists anywhere in `backend/Kurx.Api/Endpoints/`.**
- **Errors** (`ProblemResults.cs`, `ExceptionHandling/GlobalExceptionHandler.cs`, `Program.cs`): RFC7807 `application/problem+json` with a stable `error` code, `correlationId` (mirrors `X-Correlation-Id`), and an `errors` field on `validation_failed`.
- **Realtime** (`Program.cs`): SignalR `ScanHub` at `/hubs/scan` and `SalesHub` at `/hubs/sales` exist and are auth+membership-gated (token via `?access_token=`), but **`ScanHub` exposes only group join/leave — there is no scan-validation / check-in endpoint or service** (`backend/Kurx.Api/Hubs/ScanHub.cs`).

**In scope (this phase, incremental):** attendee-facing read + auth flows only — OTP login, secure token storage, token refresh/logout, `/v1/me` + onboarding detection, and public event discovery (list/search/detail/related, read-only ticket-type display).

**Excluded scope:** payments, ticket purchase/orders, ticket/QR generation, check-in/QR scanning, wallet, push notifications (FCM), analytics, organizer dashboard, and the production-readiness capstone — every one depends on backend that Phases 3–8 have not built (confirmed absent in `backend/Kurx.Api/Endpoints/`). Phase 10 stays **open**; only attendee read/auth slices close.

**Supported flows (buildable today):** (1) OTP login → token storage → `/v1/me`; (2) event browse — upcoming/trending/featured/latest, search, detail, related; (3) read-only ticket-type listing on an event detail.

**Unsupported flows (backend absent — do not build):** purchase/checkout, my-tickets/QR, organizer check-in scanning, notifications, wallet, analytics.

**Stack (this decision — becomes a standing convention only once written into `.claude/memory/mobile-conventions.md` in Stage 3):**
- **Flutter** stable channel (installed sudo-free per D-001), **Dart** stable (`>=3.4 <4.0`).
- **Riverpod** — state management + DI (no separate service locator).
- **GoRouter** — declarative navigation with auth-driven redirect guards.
- **Dio** — the single HTTP client: connect/receive timeouts, a bounded retry policy, a `Bearer` auth interceptor, a `401`→`/v1/auth/refresh`→retry-once interceptor, and RFC7807 ProblemDetails parsing into one `ApiError` model matching exactly what `ProblemResults.cs`/`GlobalExceptionHandler.cs` emit (never a second error shape).
- **Freezed + json_serializable** — immutable DTOs/models via codegen; DTOs mirror the verified snake_case responses and are mapped to domain entities.
- **flutter_secure_storage** — tokens only (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore); never `SharedPreferences`, plaintext, or a log line.
- **Hive** — local cache for **non-secret** data only (e.g. cached event lists for offline/first-paint); **never** tokens or PII.
- **Material 3** — light + dark, localization-ready, `en_IN`-first, ₹ money at the display edge.
- **Architecture — feature-first Clean Architecture.** Per feature: `presentation/{widgets,pages,providers}` · `domain/{entities,repositories,usecases}` · `data/{datasources,models,repositories,services}`; plus shared `core/{network,theme,router,storage,utils}`, `common/`, `shared/`.

**Implementation constraints:** never invent APIs/DTOs/fields — every request/response DTO mirrors a verified endpoint above; camelCase out, snake_case in; money is `long` paise formatted at the edge (D-004); tokens live only in `flutter_secure_storage`, never plaintext/SharedPreferences/Hive, never logged, never exposed; base URL from build config (`KURX_API_BASE`, default `http://localhost:5080`) with no stale fallback (the D-017 bug class); consume the existing JWT + ProblemDetails, never a new response shape. First vertical slice = OTP login → token storage → event list, verified live against the running API.

**Why:** the mobile app must track shipped backend reality, not Phase 10's aspirational deliverable list; fixing the verified contract now prevents inventing endpoints and keeps each slice closeable while the payment/ticketing/check-in backend is still unbuilt. The Clean-Architecture layering (domain/usecases per feature) is heavier than the read-only first slice strictly needs — chosen deliberately for the app's growth path (the "scalable" requirement) so DTOs, domain, and UI stay decoupled as ticketing/payments/check-in land in later slices; individual slices still obey CLAUDE.md #5 (no premature abstraction *within* a layer).

## D-020 · Phase 3 ticket-type pricing, inventory, group, and form-field rules
**Status: ACCEPTED — shipped in commit 6b5a2e1** (`TicketTypeService`/`ITicketTypeService`, `TicketTypeEndpoints`, `TicketTypeBodyValidator`/`FormFieldBodyValidator`, 11 integration tests).

Phase 3's spec named "ticket types (pricing tiers, quantity limits, sale windows)" and "FormField-based custom registration forms" without pinning the concrete pricing/inventory/group/validation semantics. These were resolved as follows (validated at the boundary by FluentValidation *and* re-checked in the service, so a bad call fails the same way regardless of entry point):
**Chose:**
- **Pricing unit / registration mode**: enums `PricingUnit { PerTicket, PerGroup }` and `RegistrationMode { Individual, Group }`, parsed case-insensitively; unknown values → `invalid_pricing_unit` / `invalid_registration_mode`. Price is `long` paise (D-004), `≥ 0` (free allowed); `< 0` → `invalid_price`.
- **Group sizing**: `Group` mode requires both `GroupMin` and `GroupMax` with `min ≤ max` (`group_size_required` / `invalid_group_size`); `Individual` mode nulls out group sizes on write so stale bounds can't linger. Actual group *pricing* math (per-group vs per-ticket at checkout) is deferred to the order flow — the ticket type only stores the unit.
- **Inventory**: `Quantity > 0` on create (`invalid_quantity`); `Available = max(0, Quantity − Sold)` is derived, never stored. The shipped `Sold` counter is the inventory source of truth for two guards — **delete is rejected when `Sold > 0`** (`tickets_already_sold`) and **an update may not set `Quantity` below `Sold`** (`quantity_below_sold`) — so a type that has issued tickets can neither vanish nor be oversold. (No order flow increments `Sold` yet; the guards are in place for when D-021's order flow lands.)
- **Sale window**: `SaleEnds > SaleStarts` (`invalid_sale_dates`). `PerUserLimit` defaults to 5 when supplied `≤ 0`.
- **Visibility**: the public list (`GET /v1/events/{eventId}/ticket-types`) returns types only for `Published` events and only within the active window (`SaleStarts ≤ now ≤ SaleEnds`); the org-facing list returns all types regardless of window. Archived events reject ticket-type writes (`event_archived`).
- **Form fields**: `key` is snake_case (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`) and unique within a ticket type (`duplicate_key` on add and on key-changing update); `Type ∈ {Text,Number,Select,Checkbox,Date,File}`, `Scope ∈ {PerRegistration,PerParticipant}` (`invalid_type` / `invalid_scope`). Scope drives where answers live later (order-level vs participant-level), matching the `AnswersJson` split already modelled on `Order`/`GroupMember`/`Ticket`.
- **Authorization**: Owner/Manager (or `KurxAdmin`) manage; any other caller gets `forbidden`, unknown ids `not_found` — same tier as event edits (D-018).
**Why:** the smallest rule set that makes ticket inventory safe before any money moves (can't delete or undersize a type that already issued tickets) and keeps pricing/group/form semantics unambiguous, while deliberately leaving purchase-time pricing math and `Sold` mutation to the order flow so ticket-type config ships and is testable independently of payments.

## D-021 · Disposition of the unwired Order/Group/Payment scaffolding (Phase 3/4 prerequisite)
**Status: ACCEPTED — free-registration path implemented in `OrderService` (`backend/Kurx.Infrastructure/Orders/OrderService.cs`), 10 integration tests (`Kurx.Tests/OrderTests.cs`).**

**Resolution of the open questions below, as implemented:**
- **`OrderItem` is real, not vestigial.** `Ticket.OrderItemId` is a non-nullable FK to `OrderItem`, so every `Order` gets exactly one `OrderItem` row (`Qty` = tickets issued — 1 for individual mode, the target group size for group mode; `UnitPricePaise` = `TicketType.PricePaise`). `Order.TicketTypeId`/`Order.AmountPaise` remain the order-level summary fields `OrderView` reads directly.
- **Free-only for this pass.** _[Superseded by D-049 — paid checkout is now implemented; the `payment_not_supported_yet` rejection below no longer applies.]_ `CreateOrderAsync` rejects any `TicketType.PricePaise > 0` with `payment_not_supported_yet` before touching any other state, rather than creating a `Pending` order with no way to ever complete — `IPaymentGateway`/`Payment`/`Refund` capture and webhooks remain a later phase built on the same `Order.Status` model, unchanged by this pass.
- **Group capacity is reserved incrementally, not all at once.** The leader takes one slot at `CreateOrderAsync` (`TicketType.Sold += 1`); each `JoinGroupAsync` call via the group's `JoinCode` takes one more, up to the `OrderItem.Qty` target set at creation (validated against `TicketType.GroupMin`/`GroupMax`). Once member count reaches the target, further joins fail with `group_full`. This avoids ever creating an unclaimed/nameless `Ticket`.
- **HMAC ticket signing reuses `TokenService.SignTicketCode`** (`backend/Kurx.Infrastructure/Auth/TokenService.cs`), the same method `GateEntryService`/`TicketTransferService` already use to verify tickets — `OrderService` had to sign with the identical method or every freshly-issued ticket would fail gate verification. (Note: this method actually signs with the JWT signing key, not the separately-configured but currently-unread `TICKET_HMAC_SECRET`; that pre-existing naming mismatch is unchanged by this pass since fixing it would require re-signing already-issued tickets — flagged here, not silently touched.)
**Original findings (for context) below.**

Before building Phase 3's registration/capture flow, investigated the pre-existing order scaffolding, per CLAUDE.md #2 (read before you build; finish what exists, don't duplicate it) — the same check that produced D-018 for the old EventService.
**Findings:**
- **What exists:** `IOrderService` (`CreateOrderAsync`/`JoinGroupAsync`/`MyTicketsAsync`/`MyGroupsAsync`/`GetGroupAsync`/`ResendTicketAsync`) and the full domain model `Order`/`OrderItem`/`Payment`/`Refund`/`Group`/`GroupMember`/`Ticket` (`backend/Kurx.Domain/Entities/Orders.cs`). All seven are mapped as `DbSet`s in `KurxDbContext` and their tables are created by the **Initial migration** (`20260706132659_Initial`) — so the schema is already live in dev/test DBs.
- **What's missing:** there is **no `OrderService` implementation**, `IOrderService` is **registered nowhere** in `DependencyInjection.cs`, **no order/registration endpoint** is mapped in `Program.cs`, and there are **zero tests**. Purely interface + model + schema — thinner even than D-018's EventService (which had a full, if misaligned, implementation).
- **Stale references (the D-018 disease again):** the `IOrderService` XML comment cites *"docs/DECISIONS.md D-017"* for group pricing/roster semantics, but D-017 is Phase 1 foundation hardening (SignalR/health/validation) — a **wrong reference to a decision that was never written**. The same comment's "free-registration path (Phase 1)" / "capture/webhook lands in Phase 2" use an internal numbering that predates the current roadmap's Phase 3 (registration) / Phase 4 (payments) split.
- **Consistency vs conflict — the key difference from D-018:** this model does **not** conflict with the shipped `TicketType`/`FormField` (D-020). `Order.TicketTypeId` FKs the shipped ticket type; the `AnswersJson` split across `Order` (per_registration) and `GroupMember`/`Ticket` (per_participant) matches the shipped `FormFieldScope`; `CreateOrderInput.GroupSize` matches `RegistrationMode.Group` + `GroupMin/GroupMax`; and `TicketType.Sold` is exactly the inventory counter an order flow would increment (guarded by D-020). D-018's EventService had to be superseded because it contradicted Phase 2; here the model is aligned and merely unfinished.
- **One open modelling question:** `Order` carries a direct `TicketTypeId` **and** an `OrderItem` table (`OrderId`,`TicketTypeId`,`Qty`,`UnitPricePaise`) exists, yet `IOrderService`/`OrderView` treat an order as a single ticket type. `OrderItem` looks vestigial — implementing requires a decision: single-ticket-type-per-order (drop/ignore `OrderItem`) vs a multi-item cart.
- **Out of scope for the order flow:** `Ticket.HmacSig` + `TICKET_HMAC_SECRET` (still "not read by any code path" per `.env.example`) is QR signing for check-in (Phase 5), not registration. *[Superseded by **D-216** (2026-08-01): that `.env.example` claim was wrong by the time check-in shipped — the secret is read by `TokenService.SignTicketCode` and is now mandatory in Production.]*
**Recommendation (Chose):** **finish in place, do not supersede.** When Phase 3's registration flow is built: implement `OrderService` for the free-registration path (validate ticket type + sale window + `PerUserLimit`, capture per_registration/per_participant answers against the ticket type's `FormField`s, increment `Sold` transactionally, issue `Ticket`s; `Group`/`JoinGroup` for group mode), register it in `DependencyInjection.cs`, map the endpoints in `Program.cs`, and cover it with integration tests against the real `kurx_test` DB. Resolve the `OrderItem`-vs-single-ticket question as its own line in that decision, and fix the stale `D-017`/phase-number references in the `IOrderService` comment as part of the same change. Paid checkout, `Payment` capture, and webhooks extend the same model in Phase 4.
**Why:** nothing conflicts — the schema is already migrated and the model matches shipped ticketing — so a rewrite (the D-018 path) would only duplicate a correct model; the actual debt is the missing implementation, one redundancy decision, and two stale comment references. Recorded as PROPOSED so the finish-vs-supersede call and the single-item-vs-cart shape are approved before code is written, not discovered mid-build.

## D-022 · Username audit trail — two separate tables
**Status: ACCEPTED — shipped in AddV2Schema migration.**

The existing `username_history` tracks **released** usernames for the 30-day reclaim hold (does a released username have a hold on it?). A second table, `username_change_log`, tracks the full **chronological history** of every username change for a user (old → new → timestamp) for audit purposes, completely independent of whether the name is currently held or available. The two tables serve different queries: reclaim hold check → `username_history`; audit trail → `username_change_log`.
**Why:** merging both concerns into one table requires either a nullable `new_username` (awkward) or a discriminator column — a simpler split keeps each query trivially indexed and each row semantically unambiguous.

## D-023 · `design_templates.EventId` for event-scoped certificate templates
**Status: ACCEPTED — shipped in AddV2Schema migration.**

Added a nullable `event_id` to `design_templates` so a template can be scoped to one specific event rather than being org-wide (`org_id` set, `event_id` null) or system-wide (both null). This enables an org to create a one-off certificate design for a single event without polluting their org-level template library.
**Scoping precedence:** event-scoped (`event_id` set) → org-wide (`org_id` set, `event_id` null) → system-wide (both null).
**Why:** practical need for per-event branding without a new entity type; the nullable column adds zero complexity to the existing template lookup.

## D-024 · Registration forms as a 4-table system decoupled from ticket types
**Status: ACCEPTED — schema shipped in AddV2Schema migration. Service/endpoints not yet wired.**

`registration_forms → registration_fields → registration_responses → registration_response_values`. Distinct from the existing `form_fields` table (which is **ticket-type-scoped** and drives the `AnswersJson` capture flow). The new system is **event-level**: one event can have multiple named forms (with an `is_default` flag), and forms can be reused across ticket types or used standalone for surveys and waitlists.
The `preset_taxonomy` column on `registration_forms` maps to an `event_categories` slug so the same category-based field presets that power `field_presets` can seed a new form automatically.
`registration_response_values` stores both a `value_text` (scalar answers) and a `value_json` (complex answers: multi-select, file metadata) — keeping the schema open to any field type without schema changes.
**Why:** ticket-type-scoped `FormField`s don't support event-wide surveys, post-event feedback, or waitlist info collection; a separate system avoids adding polymorphism to the existing form-field/order-answers model while reusing the same field-type vocabulary.

## D-025 · Soft deletes via `DeletedAt` nullable timestamp
**Status: ACCEPTED — shipped in AddV2Schema migration.**

Added `deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL` (null = active) to: `events`, `organizations`, `venues`, `speakers`, `sponsors`, `ticket_types`, `event_reviews`. Partial indexes `WHERE "DeletedAt" IS NULL` keep active-record queries as fast as hard-delete indexes. Deleted records remain queryable for audit, refund processing, and financial reconciliation — entities with financial history must never be hard-deleted.
**Column quoting:** Postgres requires `"DeletedAt"` in `HasFilter` strings (PascalCase stored by EF; only lowercase column names are unquoted by default). Pattern in C#: `HasFilter("\"DeletedAt\" IS NULL")`.
**Why:** hard deletes on orgs/events that have payment history destroy audit trails and break ledger FK references; soft delete is the minimal change that satisfies both the "remove from discovery" use case and the financial audit requirement.

## D-026 · Location columns on `events` for India-scale discovery and GST
**Status: ACCEPTED — shipped in AddV2Schema migration.**

Added `Country text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'IN'`, `State text NULL`, `District text NULL`, `PostalCode text NULL` to `events`. `City` already existed (denormalized for search); these four fields add finer-grained jurisdiction data for:
- **Discovery filtering**: search by Country/State/City compound index (`ix_events_country_state_city`).
- **GST jurisdiction**: district + postal code identify the supply place for B2C invoicing under Indian GST.
- **`Country` is required** (non-null, defaults to `IN`) so new events created before GST jurisdiction is added still have a valid country. State/District/PostalCode are nullable because not every event has a physical address (virtual events).
**Why:** `City` alone is insufficient for GST compliance; adding four nullable columns is less disruptive than a separate `event_locations` table for what is ultimately an address fragment.

## D-027 · Org invitations — GitHub-style flow with time-limited token
**Status: ACCEPTED — schema shipped in AddV2Schema migration. Service/endpoints not yet wired.**

Added `org_invitations` table. This is **distinct from** the existing "add member by phone" flow in `OrgService.AddMemberAsync` which immediately creates the membership row (and provisions a user if the phone is unknown). The invitation flow:
1. Owner/Manager creates an invitation row (`status = Pending`) and the system sends a tokenized link.
2. The invitee follows the link, authenticates via OTP if needed, and explicitly accepts or declines.
3. On accept: membership row created with the specified role; invitation marked `Accepted`.
4. Token expires in 7 days (`expires_at = created_at + 7d`); any claim after that → `Expired`.
5. Token is single-use: claiming it sets `accepted_at` and any subsequent use is rejected.
6. Owner/Manager can revoke a pending invitation at any time → `Revoked`.

The `invited_user_id` column is null until the invitee is identified (existing account matched by phone or new account created via OTP); `invited_phone` is the targeting field.
**Why:** the immediate-add flow is convenient for a known collaborator; the invitation flow is necessary for external parties who need to consent before appearing as a member of an org. Both flows will coexist.

## D-028 · Organization wallet — cached balance, never SUM on the hot path
**Status: ACCEPTED — schema and WalletService shipped.**

`organization_wallet` is a denormalized cache of the org's financial position across all ledger states. It is updated **atomically in the same transaction** as every `ledger_entries` insert; the balance is never recalculated by summing `ledger_entries` at read time. `last_ledger_entry_id` points to the entry that last updated the cache and can be used to detect staleness or replay if a transaction fails mid-way.

Columns: `collected_paise`, `available_paise`, `advanced_paise`, `reserved_paise`, `settled_paise`, `lifetime_earned_paise`, `lifetime_withdrawn_paise`.

`WalletService.GetWalletAsync` reads this single row; `GetLedgerAsync` pages `ledger_entries` for the audit trail. Financial access gated to `OrgRole.Owner | OrgRole.Finance` (D-015).
**Why:** summing a ledger on the hot read path doesn't scale as events grow; a cached row is always O(1). The tradeoff is that the cache update must be part of the same DB transaction as the ledger insert — `CollectedToAvailableLedgerJob` and any future payout/settlement code must respect this invariant.

## D-029 · Hangfire wired with 3 recurring jobs
**Status: ACCEPTED — shipped.**

Hangfire PostgreSQL storage registered in `DependencyInjection.AddKurxInfrastructure`. Dashboard at `/hangfire` (dev-only, no auth required for local debugging). Three recurring jobs:

| Job class | CRON | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ExpireSeatHoldsJob` | `* * * * *` (minutely) | Transitions `SeatHold.Status = Active → Expired` when `ExpiresAt < now`; decrements `TicketType.Sold` |
| `ExpireWaitlistOffersJob` | `*/5 * * * *` (every 5 min) | Transitions `WaitlistEntry.Status = Notified → Expired` when `OfferExpiresAt < now` |
| `CollectedToAvailableLedgerJob` | `0 0 * * *` (daily midnight UTC) | Transitions `LedgerState.Collected → Available` for events whose `EndsAt + 7d settlement window` has passed; updates `OrganizationWallet` cache atomically |

All three job classes are `AddScoped` (Hangfire's built-in DI activator resolves them per execution). Job registrations run at startup in `Program.cs` via `IRecurringJobManager.AddOrUpdate`.
**Why:** these three jobs cover the three time-driven state machines that cannot be event-driven (seat hold expiry, waitlist offer expiry, and ledger settlement). All others (payment capture webhook, refund) are external-event-driven and don't need a polling job.

## D-030 · Org soft-deletion policy
**Status: ACCEPTED — shipped in Phase 2 (`OrgService.DeleteAsync`).**

`DELETE /v1/orgs/{orgId}` is an **Owner-only** operation that sets `organizations.DeletedAt = NOW()` (soft delete per D-025). The endpoint is **blocked when the org has any event in `Published` or `Closed` status** (`has_active_events` → HTTP 409): published events have live attendees and financial obligations; closed events may have outstanding settlements that reference the org. `Draft`, `InReview`, and `Archived` events do not block deletion.

After soft-deletion:
- `ListMineAsync` excludes the org (`WHERE "DeletedAt" IS NULL`).
- `GetAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `GetKycAsync`, and all member endpoints return `not_found` (D-018 — deleted resource must not leak existence).
- The org row, its `organization_wallet`, `ledger_entries`, `kyc_records`, and `withdrawals` are **never hard-deleted** — financial tables use `RESTRICT` so the FK graph prevents orphan destruction regardless.
- Membership rows are left intact for audit; they become unreachable through active queries because the parent org is excluded.

An `org.delete` audit log entry is written with the org's name and slug before the save.

**Why:** soft delete is the only approach compatible with financial audit trail requirements (D-025). The `Published/Closed` guard is the minimal safety gate — it prevents an org disappearing while ticket buyers have a valid relationship with it. `Draft`/`InReview`/`Archived` events have no active attendee relationships.

## D-031 · Wallet withdrawal concurrency — SELECT FOR UPDATE + pending deduction
**Status: ACCEPTED — shipped in Phase 2 (`WalletService.InitiateWithdrawalAsync`).**

Two concurrent withdrawal requests for the same org must not collectively exceed `available_paise`. The prevention mechanism is two-layered:

1. **Postgres row-level lock**: `InitiateWithdrawalAsync` opens an explicit transaction and immediately executes `SELECT 1 FROM organization_wallet WHERE "OrgId" = $1 FOR UPDATE`. This acquires an exclusive row lock — any second concurrent request for the same org blocks at this statement until the first commits or rolls back, serializing all withdrawal attempts per org.

2. **Pending-withdrawal deduction**: after acquiring the lock, the service sums the `amount_paise` of all withdrawals with `Status IN ('requested', 'processing')` for the org and subtracts that from `available_paise` before the balance check. This prevents a burst of requests — each individually observing a fresh `available_paise` value — from collectively issuing withdrawals that exceed the balance before any single request is persisted.

A withdrawal is also gated on `organizations.PayoutAccountStatus = Active` (checked before the lock acquisition; `payout_not_active` → HTTP 400). Amount must be `> 0` (enforced by `WithdrawInputValidator` before the service is reached; `validation_failed` → HTTP 400).

**Raw SQL uses `ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync`** (not `ExecuteSqlAsync`) to guarantee the `orgId` is a bind parameter and cannot be interpolated as raw SQL (SQL injection safety — the two overloads are easily confused).

**Why:** application-level locks (e.g. `MemoryCache`) don't survive process restarts or multi-instance deployments; a Redis distributed lock adds a dependency. `SELECT FOR UPDATE` is the simplest correct mechanism for a Postgres-backed monolith — it serializes the critical section at the DB level with zero extra infrastructure.

## D-032 · Removal of the Flutter mobile mock data layer
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-10).**

The Phase 1 "UI-first" mobile build (TASKS.md) shipped a `MockConfig`/`FakeEventsRepository`/`FakeAuthRepository` swap seam plus, beyond that seam, several controllers (tickets, profile/username, notifications) that fabricated data locally with no repository swap point at all — a fake booking flow (synthesized gate/seat/QR, no payment), a hardcoded username-taken list, and a seeded notification feed. This predates D-019, which subsequently fixed mobile's scope to the **verified** backend surface and explicitly excludes payments/orders/tickets/QR/notifications from this phase. The mock layer had drifted out of sync with that accepted scope and needed to be removed rather than left presenting fabricated functionality as real.
**Chose:**
- **Deleted** `core/config/mock_config.dart`, `features/events/data/datasources/mock/mock_catalog.dart`, `features/events/data/repositories/fake_events_repository.dart`, `features/auth/data/repositories/fake_auth_repository.dart`. `eventsRepositoryProvider`/`authRepositoryProvider` construct only the real `Dio`-backed repository (no branch).
- **Read-only local features left alone**: bookmarks (`BookmarksController`) are genuinely local, saved-event selections with no server round-trip ever faked — not part of the mock layer, no backend endpoint expected for it.
- **Real-backed piece wired to the real source**: `ProfileController` now sources `name`/`phone`/`username` from `currentUserProvider` (real `GET /v1/me`, already fetched on login) instead of a hardcoded fallback identity ("Aarav Sharma"). The fabricated `joinedAt` ("member since") field was dropped from `ProfileState` and the profile header — `/v1/me` has no such field and one should not be invented.
- **Actions with no backend now throw `UnimplementedError`, not fabricate data**: `TicketsController.book()` (no order/payment endpoint), `ProfileController.isUsernameAvailable()`/`claimUsername()` (no username endpoint). Each carries a `TODO(D-019)` pointing at the missing backend. Calling UI (`booking_sheet.dart`, `username_claim_page.dart`) catches `UnimplementedError` and shows a "not available yet" toast instead of crashing.
- **`NotificationsController`** now returns an empty list instead of six seeded fake notifications — there is no notifications backend (D-019); the existing empty-state UI already handles this correctly.
- Removed the `--dart-define=USE_MOCK` references from `PROGRESS.md`/`TASKS.md` (struck through, annotated with this decision) — no code path ever reads that flag going forward.
**Unimplemented gaps this leaves (tracked, not built — do not invent):** ticket purchase/orders, username claim/availability, in-app notifications. All three require backend work out of scope for the current mobile phase (D-019's excluded-scope list).
**Why:** the mock layer had outgrown its original "swap seam" purpose and started shipping fabricated functionality (fake tickets, fake availability checks, fake notifications) that contradicted D-019's accepted scope; removing it and being honest about what's unimplemented (rather than silently faking it) keeps the app's behavior truthful about what the backend actually supports.

## D-033 · Event taxonomy seeding + slug uniqueness strategy
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-10).**

The platform needed its standard event taxonomy loaded into `event_categories` (the `EventCategory`
tree, `CategoryLevel: Audience → Category → Type`): **3 audiences → 13 categories → 145 types**. Seven
type names recur across audiences (Marathon, Workshop, Seminar, Networking Event, Career Fair, Volunteer
Event, Startup Meetup — each under both Student and Public), which collide with the table's
**single-column globally-unique `Slug` index** (`KurxDbContext`, `event_categories`). The ambiguous call:
make slugs unique-per-parent (needs a schema change — drop the global unique index, add a composite
`(ParentId, Slug)` one, and rework `CategoryService.UniqueSlugAsync`) vs keep them globally unique and
disambiguate the collisions.
**Chose:** **globally-unique slugs, no schema change.** A type whose kebab slug recurs across audiences is
prefixed with its audience stem (`student-marathon` / `public-marathon`, `student-workshop` /
`public-workshop`, …); all other 131 types keep the bare kebab slug (`hackathon`, `wedding`). Prefixing is
symmetric — when a name collides, *every* occurrence is prefixed, so no arbitrary "first one wins the bare
slug." Implemented in `Kurx.Infrastructure.Events.EventTaxonomySeeder` (mirrors `SystemTemplateSeeder`:
static `SeedAsync(db, ct)`, idempotent match-on-slug, wired into `Program.cs` startup after migrations).
`Sort` = 0-based sibling order as listed; `Level`/`ParentId` link each tier; `IsVisible = true`. Slugify
reuses `CategoryService`'s exact ASCII-kebab rule so seeded and admin-created slugs are consistent.
**Why:** the existing unique constraint is already global, and `CategoryService` (admin-created categories)
already assumes global-uniqueness with a random-suffix fallback — keeping that invariant means **zero
schema/migration churn and zero change to existing code paths** (CLAUDE.md §5, "don't touch what isn't
asked"). Audience-prefixing only the 14 colliding rows keeps the other 131 slugs clean and human-readable
for URLs/lookups (`FieldPreset.CategoryOrTypeSlug`), while staying fully deterministic and collision-free —
verified live against `kurx_test` (3/13/145, unique slugs, correct parent links, idempotent on re-run).

## D-034 · Rate limiter ran before authentication — every request was bucketed as anonymous
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-11). Found and fixed while adding integration tests for D-021.**

`Program.cs`'s middleware pipeline called `app.UseRateLimiter()` before `app.UseAuthentication()`. The `GlobalLimiter` partitions requests by `ctx.User.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)` — but with authentication not yet run, `ctx.User` was still the default unauthenticated principal for every request, so the claim lookup always returned null. Every request, including ones carrying a valid Bearer token, fell into the anonymous-IP partition (60 req/min shared per IP) instead of the intended per-user partition (300 req/min, 3000 for `kurx_admin`). Confirmed by running the pre-existing `TicketTypeTests` in isolation (no code changed in that file) — it also failed with `429 rate_limited`, proving the bug predates this change and wasn't introduced by the new `OrderTests`.

**Chose:** reorder to `UseAuthentication()` → `UseRateLimiter()` → `UseAuthorization()`, matching the standard ASP.NET Core rate-limiting guidance (limiter needs `ctx.User` populated to partition correctly; authorization can safely run after since a 403 from an authenticated-but-unauthorized caller should still count against their own quota, not the anonymous one).

**Why:** a test suite with enough authenticated calls per class (bulk send, group joins, multi-step setup) could exhaust the 60/min anonymous bucket well before any real per-user limit — a false 429 with no relation to actual abuse. In production this meant a single active organizer or attendee could be throttled based on how many *other, unrelated* anonymous requests shared their IP (e.g. behind a shared NAT or corporate proxy), while the intended generous 300/min per-authenticated-user allowance was never actually reached by anyone. One-line fix, no behavior change for genuinely anonymous traffic (still 60/min per IP), no schema/API impact.

## D-035 · Real certificate rendering (Phase 7) — QuestPDF-only, system templates, manual trigger
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-11).** `ICertificateRenderer` (`CertificateRendererStub` → `CertificateRenderer`, `backend/Kurx.Infrastructure/Providers/DocumentProviders.cs`) now renders a real PDF + PNG via QuestPDF (already an installed, unused dependency) instead of returning the QR PNG bytes disguised as a PDF. New `ICertificateService`/`CertificateService` (`backend/Kurx.Infrastructure/Events/CertificateService.cs`) orchestrates generation; new `DesignTemplateSeeder` seeds system templates (`design_templates` was previously empty — no seeder touched it).

**Chose:**
- **PDF and PNG both come from QuestPDF directly** (`document.GeneratePdf()` / `document.GenerateImages(...)`) — `IDocumentRasterizer`/`Docnet.Core` are **not** used for the system-template path; `DocumentRasterizerStub` stays a stub, needed only if/when arbitrary uploaded-PDF custom templates are built.
- **Two system layouts, selected by `DesignTemplate.BaseLayout`**: `classic-certificate` (centered, coloured border) and `modern-certificate` (left-aligned, coloured header band) — both parameterized by `AccentColor` so org/event-scoped templates (D-023 precedence: event → org → system) can restyle without a new layout. Custom (`TemplateMode.Custom`, org-uploaded) backgrounds are **not implemented** in this pass — deferred, not silently dropped.
- **`DesignTemplateSeeder`** seeds 3 system rows (2 Certificate layouts + 1 Invite placeholder for future use) idempotently on startup, mirroring `SystemTemplateSeeder`'s match-on-name pattern.
- **Trigger is a manual organizer endpoint**, `POST /v1/events/{eventId}/certificates/generate` (Owner/Manager/`KurxAdmin`, `"heavy"` rate-limited), not an automatic Hangfire job — smaller, testable slice; a recurring job can wrap the same `ICertificateService.GenerateForEventAsync` later without changing this method's contract.
- **Eligibility**: if `Event.CertificatesEnabled` (existing, previously-unused column), only `TicketState.CheckedIn` tickets qualify; otherwise any non-`Void` ticket does. Guest tickets (`Ticket.UserId == null`) are skipped — a certificate always belongs to a user.
- **Idempotent**: re-running skips any ticket that already has a `Certificate` row (checked via `(EventId, TicketId)`, which is already a unique index).
- **`GET /v1/certificates/{code}` now returns `pdf_url`** (a presigned `IStorage.PresignGetAsync` URL), replacing the previously-raw `pdf_key` storage key — the frontend needs a fetchable URL, not an internal key. This is a breaking response-shape change to a field that was never actually populated by any code path before this pass, so no real consumer existed to break.
- **Real ticket QR**: `GET /v1/tickets/{code}/qr.png` returns a real scannable PNG via the already-real `IQrCodeGenerator`, fixing the static-icon/decorative-mock QR the web (`/tickets`) and mobile (`QrView`) clients currently show. Frontend wiring to consume this endpoint is a follow-up, not included in this backend pass.
**Why:** the smallest change that turns the certificate feature from "stub returning fake bytes" into "real, verifiable PDFs" without touching the still-unbuilt custom-editor/PDF-upload path (Docnet.Core) or inventing new schema — `DesignTemplate.PlacementsJson`'s field-placement model is intentionally *not* used yet (the two hardcoded layouts don't read it) since no editor writes it; wiring `PlacementsJson`-driven rendering is future work once a template editor exists to produce it.

## D-036 · Two-product registration model — guest checkout for Events, mandatory accounts for Competitions
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-11).** Three audit reports this session — since deleted (2026-08-08; in git history) (`PRODUCT_BUSINESS_RULES_AUDIT.md`, `PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_EVENTS_VS_COMPETITIONS.md`, `PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE_DELTA_INVITATION_RULES.md`) — established the product split — invitation-only/free public events never require a Kurx account, paid events and all competitions always do — and converged on the minimal schema below to implement it inside the existing `Order`/`Ticket`/`Group`/`EventInvitation` model, without a parallel system.

**Chose:**
- **`Order.UserId` is now nullable.** A guest (unauthenticated) order carries `GuestName`/`GuestPhone`/`GuestEmail` plus a `GuestAccessToken` (12-char, same generator shape as `InvitationService`'s `InviteToken` — a bearer credential embedded in a link, not typed manually, so it uses that token's alphabet/length rather than the 6-char `JoinCode` one). `GET/POST /v1/orders/guest/{accessToken}` (view/resend) are the guest's only way to reach their own order — possession of the token substitutes for a session, the same pattern every other random-token field in this codebase already uses.
- **`RequiresAccount` is computed, never stored**: `TicketType.IsCompetition || TicketType.PricePaise > 0`, evaluated once in `OrderService.CreateOrderAsync`. A stored boolean would just be a cache of these two columns that could drift out of sync with them — not persisting it is the simpler and more correct choice.
- **Guest checkout is scoped to `RegistrationMode.Individual` only.** `Group`-mode tickets (both plain group bookings and competition teams) still require an authenticated leader, exactly as before D-036 — the product rules never described anonymous group formation, and it would add an unbounded-identity dedup problem with no concrete spec to build against.
- **`TicketType.IsCompetition`** (bool) is the single new flag driving both the account requirement and competition-team routing — deliberately not named `IsCompetitionTeam` (the earlier working title) since a competition can be `RegistrationMode.Individual` (a solo coding contest) and still need the same account/history/certificate treatment.
- **Competition team formation is invite-only, never open-code.** `JoinGroupAsync` (the public `JoinCode` path) rejects with `competition_requires_invitation` when `TicketType.IsCompetition`. The only way to join such a team is `POST /v1/groups/invitations/{token}/accept`, sourced from a new `EventInvitation.GroupId`-scoped invite the captain sends via `POST /v1/events/{eventId}/invitations` (extended to accept a Kurx `Username` — resolved server-side to that account's phone/name — or a raw phone, and authorized by the group's `LeaderUserId`, not just org managers). Acceptance additionally verifies the accepting user's own phone matches the invitation's `Phone` when one was set — the same targeted-redemption rule `TicketTransferService.ClaimAsync` already enforces on transfer claims, applied here for consistency and to stop a leaked token being redeemed by an unintended account.
- **No `GroupMember.Status` (`Pending`/`Joined`) field was added**, despite being proposed in the second audit report for a captain-approval workflow — it turned out to be unnecessary. A `GroupMember` row is only ever created at the moment an invitation is *accepted*, so there is no intermediate "pending member" row to track; `EventInvitation.RsvpStatus` (already `None|Accepted|Declined`) fully carries that state. This is one fewer new field than the reports estimated, discovered while implementing rather than planning.
- **Chat auto-join is wired for the first time**: `ChatService.AddMemberByEventAsync`/`EnsureRoomExistsAsync` existed, fully correct, with zero callers anywhere in the codebase before this pass. `OrderService` now calls them on every authenticated ticket issuance (individual purchase, group leader, group join, competition invite acceptance) — never for guest orders, since `ChatMember.UserId` is non-nullable and a guest has none.
- **`Certificate.Kind`** (new `CertificateKind` enum: `Participation, Winner, RunnerUp, Finalist, Volunteer, Organizer, Judge, Speaker, Sponsor, Appreciation, Completion`) is added to the schema now but `CertificateService.GenerateForEventAsync` only ever assigns `Participation` — Winner/RunnerUp/Finalist need a Judging module that doesn't exist; Volunteer/Judge/Speaker/Organizer need `EventAssignment`-sourced eligibility, also unwired. Not faked.
- **Certificate revocation is visible, not hidden** — `Certificate.IsRevoked`/`RevokedReason`/`RevokedAt`, and `GET /v1/certificates/{code}` returns `200` with `is_revoked: true` for a revoked certificate rather than `404`. This is the deliberate *opposite* of D-018's hide-drafts pattern: D-018 hides unpublished business info that shouldn't be guessable; a revoked certificate's public falsifiability is the entire point of the verify endpoint existing.
- **`Event.ShortCode`** (unique 6-char, same alphabet as `JoinCode`/`VerifyCode`) is a voice/SMS-friendly reference distinct from the slug, generated and locked at creation exactly like `Slug` already is.
**Why:** every new field extends an existing entity or reuses an existing generator/authorization pattern already proven elsewhere in this codebase (D-031's style of targeted verification, `TicketTransferService`'s phone-match-on-claim, the platform-wide random-token convention) — nothing here introduces a new architectural primitive, a duplicate identifier, or a parallel registration system. Free/invitation-only Events and account-mandatory Competitions now share one `Order`/`Ticket`/`Group` engine, branching only on `IsCompetition` and `PricePaise`.

## D-037 · Mandatory username onboarding + phone number change
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-11).** Finalized identity model: every user must set a unique public `Username` (alongside `Name`) before using the app, phone numbers can be changed on an existing account, and the pre-existing 30-day username reclaim hold (`UsernameHistory`, D-022) is now actually enforced rather than only recorded.

**Chose:**
- **`needs_onboarding` now requires both fields**: `user.Name == "" || user.Username is null` (was Name-only, D-012). `Username` stays **nullable in the database** — no destructive migration — enforced only in the application layer, so existing rows with no username simply route back through onboarding on next use rather than failing a NOT NULL constraint retroactively.
- **New `GET /v1/usernames/availability?username=`** (unauthenticated — availability isn't sensitive) returns exactly one of `available/unavailable/reserved/invalid`. `unavailable` collapses three distinct backend checks (active-user conflict, org-slug conflict, inside the 30-day reclaim hold) into one status, matching the four states the product spec named; callers needing to distinguish further would need a second, more detailed endpoint, not built here. Mobile/web now call this instead of probing via `PATCH /v1/me/profile`.
- **Reclaim hold is now enforced, not just recorded**: `PATCH /v1/me/profile`'s uniqueness check and the new availability endpoint both query `UsernameHistory` for a row with the same username and `ReleasedAt` within the last 30 days. Per D-022's own stated intent ("reclaimable 30 days after this"), nobody — including the original releasing owner — can reclaim during the hold window; this had never actually been checked anywhere before this pass.
- **Phone change** (`POST /v1/me/phone/verify`, authenticated, body `{Phone, Code}`) reuses the existing `POST /v1/auth/otp/request` unchanged to send the code to the new number, then verifies and reassigns `User.Phone` to the calling user's existing row — `User.Id` and every relationship are untouched. **Does not revoke other sessions**: only the phone number changes, and D-009's reuse-revocation model targets token theft, not routine phone updates, so forcing re-login everywhere would be surprising for a non-compromise event.
- **OTP login race condition fixed**: `AuthService.VerifyOtpAsync` previously had no guard against two concurrent requests for the same brand-new phone both passing the "does this user exist" check before either committed, which would throw an unhandled 23505 unique-constraint violation on `Users.Phone` for the loser. Now catches that specific `DbUpdateException`, clears the failed change tracker, re-fetches the winning row, and issues tokens for it — mirroring `EventService.CreateAsync`'s existing slug-collision catch pattern. The same pattern protects the new phone-change endpoint against two callers racing for the same new number.
- **Captain team-invitations already resolved by Username with phone fallback** (built during D-036) — no change needed; this remains the primary username-based public-identity use case beyond profile URLs and search.
- **Email is unchanged and *not* newly enforced unique** — `Users.Email` has no DB-level unique index today (confirmed by inspection) despite being described as unique; Email isn't editable by any endpoint, so no code path can create a duplicate today, but the constraint itself doesn't exist. Documented here rather than silently added, since adding a real unique index was not requested and risks failing against any pre-existing duplicate/null data.
**Why:** every change either tightens an already-documented-but-unenforced invariant (the reclaim hold), extends an existing entity without a destructive migration (nullable `Username`), or reuses an already-proven pattern elsewhere in the codebase (the 23505-catch retry, the guest/competition token-possession-as-auth idea) — no new architectural primitive, consistent with D-036's own closing rationale.

## D-038 · Case-insensitive email uniqueness + phone-change revokes all other sessions
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-11). Supersedes D-037's "Email is unchanged and not newly enforced unique" bullet** — email is now uniquely enforced, case-insensitively.

**Chose:**
- **Case-insensitive unique index via raw SQL, not EF Core's fluent `HasIndex`**: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "IX_users_Email_Lower" ON users (lower("Email")) WHERE "Email" IS NOT NULL`, added in the `AddEmailUniqueIndex` migration. EF Core's fluent API can express a *filtered* index (`.HasFilter(...)`, used everywhere else in this codebase) but not an *expression* index over `lower(...)` — so this one is raw SQL, with a one-line comment in `KurxDbContext.cs` pointing here so a future reader doesn't wonder why `User.Email` has no fluent `HasIndex` call. `Test@x.com`/`test@x.com`/`TEST@x.com` now collide as the same identity, matching `Username`'s existing lowercase-normalized convention.
- **Duplicate detection fails loudly, not silently, and does not auto-mutate data**: the migration's `Up()` runs a `DO $$ ... RAISE EXCEPTION ...` guard before creating the index, counting case-insensitive duplicate emails and aborting with an exact count and a pointer to this decision if any exist. It does **not** attempt to auto-resolve duplicates (pick a canonical row, null the others) — that's a data decision requiring human judgment, and doing it silently inside a migration is itself the riskier "silent" behavior the request asked to avoid. **Verified against the live `kurx` database at implementation time: 0 users exist, so 0 duplicates — this migration applies cleanly today.** If it ever does fire in the future: identify the colliding rows (`SELECT * FROM users WHERE lower("Email") = '<dup>'`), decide the canonical account (oldest `CreatedAt`, or user-confirmed), and null `Email` on the others — safe today since no code path reads or depends on `Email` yet — then re-run the migration.
- **`Users.Email` still has no application-layer write path** (confirmed by inspection — no endpoint sets it). "Store using lowercase" therefore has nothing to normalize yet; the DB-level functional index is what actually enforces case-insensitivity today, and will keep doing so regardless of how a future email-set endpoint writes the column. When that endpoint is built, it should still normalize to lowercase before storing (matching `Username`'s convention) as defense-in-depth, not as the sole enforcement mechanism.
- **Phone change now revokes every other active session**: `AuthService.VerifyPhoneChangeAsync` bulk-revokes all of the user's active `RefreshToken` rows (the exact `ExecuteUpdateAsync` shape `RefreshAsync`'s reuse-detection path already uses) immediately after the phone number is saved, audit-logs `auth.phone_changed`, then issues a fresh access/refresh pair via the existing `IssueTokensAsync` helper. `POST /v1/me/phone/verify` now returns the standard token response (reusing `ToTokenResponse`, the same helper `otp/verify`/`refresh` already use) instead of a bare `{id, phone}`. No client currently calls this endpoint, so the response-shape change breaks nothing.
- **Access tokens still can't be revoked early** — inherent to the existing stateless-JWT architecture (only refresh tokens are DB-tracked). A stolen device's live access token (≤1h) remains valid until natural expiry after a phone change; its refresh token stops working immediately. This is the same guarantee D-009/D-014 already provide for token-theft detection, applied to a new trigger — not a new gap.
- **Emergent interaction with D-014, confirmed correct via testing**: deliberately reusing the now-revoked pre-change refresh token after a phone change triggers the *existing* reuse-detection sweep (`RefreshAsync`), which revokes every currently-active token for that user again — including a freshly-issued one, if checked afterward. This isn't a bug; it's D-014's theft-assumption behavior firing exactly as designed. Tests check the freshly-issued token first for this reason.
- **Global anonymous-IP rate limit made test-configurable** (`RATE_LIMIT_ANON_PER_MIN`, `Program.cs`), mirroring the existing `RATE_LIMIT_OTP_PER_MIN` override pattern exactly. Found while adding tests for this decision: `AuthTests.cs`'s total anonymous-endpoint call volume (~74 calls across 18 tests, one shared fake IP, sub-20-second run) crossed the hardcoded 60/min global anonymous bucket — a risk D-034 already flagged as accepted but which this file's growth has now actually hit. Production default is unchanged (60/min when unset); `KurxApiFactory.cs` sets a generous test-only value, same as it already does for the OTP-specific limiter.
**Why:** case-insensitive matching is what "the same email address" actually means for every real mail provider, so enforcing it any other way would be a correctness bug wearing a uniqueness constraint's clothes; failing the migration loudly (not auto-merging) keeps a genuinely risky data decision in human hands; and the session-revocation change closes the exact "stolen device stays logged in after I take my number back" gap the request described, using only mechanisms this codebase already trusts (D-009/D-014's revocation model), not a new one.

## D-039 · Trust & verification substrate — two polymorphic tables (re-architecture M0)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13). First module of the production re-architecture** (design docs `KURX_REARCHITECTURE_MASTER_PLAN.md` and `KURX_MODULE_DESIGN_DOSSIER.md`, deleted 2026-08-08; in git history), which separates five previously-conflated concepts — **Authentication ≠ Identity Verification ≠ Organization Verification ≠ Membership Verification ≠ Event Approval** — each with its own state machine. All three verification types, plus event approval (M8), fraud (M13), and the admin console (M12), share **one evidence table and one review table** rather than three bespoke review systems.

**Chose:**
- **`verification_documents`** (evidence) and **`verification_reviews`** (append-only decisions), both **polymorphic** via `SubjectType ∈ {UserIdentity, Organization, Membership, Event}` + `SubjectId`. `SubjectId` carries **no hard FK** — it points at different tables (`users`/`organizations`/`memberships`/`events`), so referential integrity is enforced by the writing service, not a DB constraint. This is the one deliberate exception to the codebase's otherwise-strict FK discipline, justified by the polymorphism.
- **`DocType`/`ReasonCode` are open strings** (subject-specific and extensible per org type — same rationale as `EventAssignment.Role`'s 14-values-plus-Custom), while `SubjectType`/`Status`/`Decision` are **enums stored as text** (global `OnModelCreating` convention).
- **Evidence files live in private storage**; only `StorageKey` + `Sha256` (forgery/duplicate detection, M13) + `ExtractedJson` (OCR/provider fields) are persisted. **Profile bio is never an input to verification** — evidence is always an explicit document or an explicit review row. This makes the "bio is never proof" invariant structural.
- **`UploadedBy`/`ReviewerId` are real `User` FKs** (`RESTRICT`); `ReviewerId` is nullable — a null reviewer denotes a system/automated decision.
- Additive migration `AddVerificationSubstrate`; fully reversible `Down`; **no existing table touched**.

**Why:** one substrate keeps every verification subsystem consistent and auditable — M12's console reads `verification_reviews` across all subject types with one query — and avoids three parallel review systems that would drift. M3/M5/M6 each add only their subject-specific state table on top of this. Built **first (M0)** because every later trust module depends on it.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` 106/106 (added `VerificationSubstrateTests` round-tripping both tables, the polymorphic subject, the jsonb payload, the enum-as-text mapping, and a null system-reviewer against real `kurx_test`).

## D-040 · Platform roles read live per request, not from the token (re-architecture M2)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** Replaces the single `User.IsKurxAdmin` boolean + static `kurx_admin` token claim with a `platform_roles` table read **live per request**, giving least-privilege reviewer/finance/support separation for the admin console (M12) and instant revocation.

**Chose:**
- **`platform_roles`** (`UserId`, `Role ∈ {SuperAdmin, VerificationReviewer, FinanceOps, Support, ReadOnlyAuditor}`, `GrantedBy?`, `GrantedAt`, `ExpiresAt?`), unique `(UserId, Role)`. `IPlatformRoleService` reads/writes it. SuperAdmin implies every other platform capability.
- **Authority is never in the JWT.** `PlatformRoleClaimsTransformation` (`IClaimsTransformation`, in the Api layer to keep Infrastructure free of ASP.NET auth types) runs on every authenticated request: it **strips** any `platform_role`/`kurx_admin` claim the presented token carries (defeating a forged claim), then **re-adds** the user's current roles from the DB — one `platform_role` claim per role, plus a live `kurx_admin` claim for SuperAdmin. Because roles are re-read each request, a grant/revoke is effective on the **next** request, not after token expiry. Verified by a test that revokes with the *same still-valid token* and gets `403`.
- **Zero endpoint churn.** The nine per-endpoint `IsAdmin(principal)` helpers keep checking `kurx_admin` — now a live DB-sourced claim, not a token claim. Policies (`SuperAdmin`/`VerificationReviewer`/`FinanceOps`/`Support`) read `platform_role`; the existing `KurxAdmin` policy now maps to the live SuperAdmin claim.
- **Rate limiter admin tier dropped (throttle only).** The limiter runs before authorization, so the live `kurx_admin` claim isn't present there yet — every authenticated user now buckets at 300/min. This is a throttling change, never an authorization one; the admin console gets dedicated limits in M12. `TokenService` no longer mints `kurx_admin`.
- **Backfill:** the `AddPlatformRoles` migration inserts a `SuperAdmin` grant for every existing `users.IsKurxAdmin = true` user (`GrantedBy` null = system). `IsKurxAdmin` is left in place for now and dropped in M1 (D-041) once nothing reads it.
- **No caching yet:** the lookup is a single index seek on `(UserId)` returning ≤5 rows (0 for almost everyone), consistent with the existing live-authz reads (`OrgService.RoleAsync`). A short-TTL cache is a documented future perf item, deferred to avoid premature invalidation complexity.

**Why:** baking admin/reviewer/finance authority into a 1-hour token means a compromised or removed privileged user keeps that power until the token expires — unacceptable for the powerful roles the admin console needs. Live reads close that window; `IClaimsTransformation` delivers it with zero churn to existing authorization sites and makes forged claims structurally impossible.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` 110/110 (added `PlatformRoleTests`: forged-claim rejected, real grant allowed, revocation effective next request on the same token, reviewer ≠ SuperAdmin; the pre-existing platform-admin event test now uses a real granted SuperAdmin instead of a forged claim).

## D-041 · Identity & account authority boundary — drop IsKurxAdmin, profile is authority-zero (re-architecture M1)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** Completes the separation of *account/handle* from *trust*: the `User` row is an account plus a self-declared display profile with **zero authority**, and the last authorization bit is removed from it.

**Chose:**
- **Dropped `users.IsKurxAdmin`.** After M2 (D-040) nothing in live code read it — platform authority is `platform_roles`, and the M2 `AddPlatformRoles` backfill already turned every `IsKurxAdmin = true` user into a `SuperAdmin` grant. The `DropIsKurxAdmin` migration is ordered *after* `AddPlatformRoles`, so on a fresh database the backfill preserves the grants before the column is dropped (verified: full chain applies clean on `kurx_test`). `Down` re-adds the column (default false). No admin information is lost — it moved to `platform_roles`.
- **Profile fields are authority-zero, documented structurally.** `Headline`, `Bio`, `EducationJson`, `Skills`, `LinksJson` are self-declared display data, never read by any authorization or verification decision. The `User` XML doc states this ("bio is never proof"); trust facts live only in `platform_roles` (M2), `user_identity_verifications` (M3), and `membership_claims` (M6).
- **`EducationJson` retained for now**, explicitly labelled a self-declared/**unverified** affiliation (that is exactly how the public profile already surfaces it — a display string, consumed by nothing that gates access). It is migrated into evidence-backed `membership_claims` and the column dropped in M6 (D-044), not now — dropping it before M6 exists to receive the data would lose it. **[SUPERSEDED by D-220, 2026-08-01: this migration never happened and will not — a `MembershipClaim` needs an existing org, an enum role, evidence documents and reviewer approval, none of which a free-text string supplies. The column is retained permanently as self-declared data. The D-number cited here is also wrong: D-044 is org verification (M5); M6 is D-045.]**
- **No `/v1/me` trust summary yet.** The dossier's "`/v1/me` returns a verification/trust summary" is deferred to M3/M7, when there is real verification state to summarize; adding a hardcoded "unverified" placeholder now would be speculative. No client contract changed — `is_kurx_admin` was never exposed by `/v1/me` or the profile response.

**Why:** removing the dead boolean eliminates the last "authority baked into the user row" and makes "the profile is display-only" a structural fact rather than a convention, which is the precondition for every later trust module reading evidence tables instead of profile text. Sequenced right after M2 so the drop is safe (grants already migrated).
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` 110/110 (unchanged — the drop is transparent to behavior; the migration chain including the M2 backfill applies clean on a freshly-reset `kurx_test`).

## D-042 · Person identity verification (re-architecture M3)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** Adds KYC of a *person* — entirely distinct from organization bank verification (M9). New `user_identity_verifications` aggregate (1:1 with `User`) with a graduated ID0–ID4 ladder.

**Chose:**
