- **Reuse the existing `IKycProvider`** (mock in dev, exactly as org bank/PAN KYC does — D-016). **Scope refinement from the dossier's "real adapter":** a production DigiLocker/Aadhaar/PAN/penny-drop integration needs live provider credentials/SDKs that don't exist in this environment and can't be tested offline — the same reason *every* provider here is a stub (`AddProvider` throws for non-dev values). So M3 builds the real identity-verification **domain** (levels, masking, retry, expiry, audit, gating state) and runs it against the mock; the real adapter is a gated integration task (same status as Razorpay/M10), documented, **not faked**.
- **Only masked last-4 is ever persisted** (`GovtIdLast4`/`PanLast4`/`BankLast4`), mirroring D-016 — the full government-ID/PAN/account number is passed to the provider and never stored or logged. Component *presence* is what capability gates (M7) read; `Level` is a coarse display summary (highest rung achieved), so a bank-only user doesn't falsely imply government-ID verification.
- **Every decision appends a `verification_reviews` row** (the M0 substrate) with `ReviewerId = null` (automated/provider) and a non-PII `ReasonCode` (`pan:approved`, `bank:rejected`, …) — the audit spine the admin console (M12) reads.
- **Endpoints** `GET /v1/me/identity` + `POST /v1/me/identity/{government-id,pan,bank}` act **only on the caller's own identity** (userId from the token). Provider rejection is a `200` with `status: Rejected` (a valid outcome, not an HTTP error); format-invalid input is `400`.
- **Attempt-capped** at 5 resubmissions (DB-backed, like OTP); concurrent first-submission race on the unique `UserId` is caught (23505) and re-fetched (D-037 pattern); `kind` is charset-constrained before it reaches the provider payload (JSON-injection defense).
- **ID1 (email verify) and ID4 (liveness) are modelled** (enum values) but their flows are **deferred, not faked**; per the approved locked decision, liveness stays **risk-gated only**, never blanket.
- **`/v1/me` now returns an `identity` summary** (`level`, `status`) — the trust-summary start deferred from M1. Full capability composition (L0–L5) lands in M7.

**Why:** paid-event organizing, org representation, and finance access all require a verified *person*, which phone-possession alone can't establish; this builds that subsystem on the shared substrate with real, tested logic while being honest that the production KYC provider is a separate gated integration. Masking + own-identity-only access + automated audit rows satisfy the mandatory KYC/PII security review.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **119/119** (+9 `IdentityVerificationTests`: default state, PAN/govt-id/bank approval with only-last-4, provider rejection without promotion, invalid-format rejection, 5-attempt cap → 429, automated review-row written, `/v1/me` summary — all via real HTTP against `kurx_test`). Security self-review performed (PII masking, own-identity authorization, audit trail, input validation, no PII in logs/reviews).

## D-043 · Organization registry — typed, canonical, alias- and domain-aware, fuzzy dedup (re-architecture M4)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** Replaces the thin `Organization` (name + slug + bank fields) with a **registry** so organizers find and reuse an existing org instead of creating duplicates or impersonations — the foundation of the "NSRIT ↔ full name" rule.

**Chose:**
- **`Organization` gains** `Type` (`College/School/University/Company/Startup/NGO/Club/Community/Government/Other`), `LegalName`, `PrimaryDomain` (globally unique among active orgs), `CanonicalOrgId` (self for a normal org; points at the survivor after a merge, M5), and `NormalizedName` (lowercase, punctuation→space, collapsed) backing fuzzy search. New `organization_aliases` table (acronym/former-name/expansion → canonical org). `pg_trgm` extension + GIN trigram indexes on the normalized name/alias.
- **`OrganizationRegistryService.SearchAsync`** matches on exact normalized name, primary domain, pg_trgm fuzzy name, and aliases — merging to one hit per canonical org with a score and `MatchKind` (`exact`/`domain`/`name`/`alias`). `GET /v1/orgs/search?q=`.
- **Dedup split by trust, not blanket** *(refinement of the dossier's "hard-block exact name/domain")*: the create-time **hard block is on `primary_domain` only** (a globally-unique identifier); **name dedup is a soft "did you mean?"** surfaced by search. **Hard name-dedup is enforced at verification time (M5)** — a reviewer won't verify a duplicate, and a verified org's name+aliases become reserved. This is both more correct (creation is cheap/unverified; verification is the trust gate) and avoids breaking the ~30 existing test org-creations that legitimately reuse names within a class.
- **`Type` is optional at the API** (defaults to `Other`) so existing `POST /v1/orgs {name}` callers keep working; real UIs select a type. Domain is scheme/www/slash-stripped and format-validated (`invalid_domain`).
- **Alias-management endpoints are deferred** to M5 (merge creates aliases) / M12 (admin); M4 ships the alias *model* + search resolution (a test seeds an alias to prove acronym→canonical resolution).
- **Web/mobile client wiring** (`createOrganization`/`searchOrganizations` + UI) is deferred to the consolidated client-parity pass rather than shipping half-wired per-module functions; the backend contract is complete and integration-tested.

**Why:** an org registry with fuzzy dedup + aliases + domains is the single biggest anti-impersonation and data-quality lever, and makes the NSRIT-reuse rule real (future organizers search → select → request membership against one canonical org). Putting hard name-dedup at verification keeps creation frictionless while still preventing a *trusted* duplicate.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **127/127** (+8 `OrgRegistryTests`: type/domain fields, default type, domain-dedup 409, invalid-domain 400, and all four search modes incl. fuzzy trigram and acronym→canonical via alias — all real HTTP against `kurx_test`). No existing test regressed.

## D-044 · Organization verification lifecycle (re-architecture M5)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** Turns "an org exists" into "an org is *reviewed*". Adds a verification state machine on top of the M4 registry, gated by the M2 platform `VerificationReviewer` role.

**Chose:**
- **`Organization` gains** `VerificationStatus` (`Unverified → PendingReview → ChangesRequested → Verified → Rejected → Suspended → Blacklisted`), `VerificationReviewedBy/At`, `VerificationNotes`. Migration defaults existing rows to `Unverified` (the EF-scaffolded `""` was corrected).
- **`OrgVerificationService`**: Owner `SubmitAsync` (evidence → `verification_documents`, status → PendingReview; resubmit allowed only from Unverified/ChangesRequested/Rejected); reviewer `ReviewAsync` (`approve`/`reject`/`request_changes`), `SuspendAsync`, and a `ListPendingAsync` queue. Every decision writes a `verification_reviews` row (human `ReviewerId`, contrasting M3's automated null).
- **Hard name-dedup enforced here** (the point M4 deferred): approving an org is blocked (`duplicate_verified_org`, 409) if another **verified** org shares its normalized name — the reviewer merges the duplicate instead (merge is the admin console, M12). This keeps creation frictionless (M4) while guaranteeing only one *verified* org per name.
- **Endpoints**: Owner-facing `POST /v1/orgs/{id}/verification/submit` + `GET …/verification` (any member views; non-member → `not_found`, never leaking existence, D-018). Reviewer-facing `/v1/admin/orgs/{pending, {id}/verification/review, {id}/verification/suspend}` gated by `RequireAuthorization("VerificationReviewer")` (live platform role, M2).
- **Verification status is surfaced** in `OrgDetail`, registry search, so users can pick the *verified* org. Suspension/blacklist take effect wherever they're read live (event-approval gate, M8; trust, M7) — this module sets the state, downstream modules honor it.
- **Merge deferred to M12** (admin console, where org-search + dedup + merge belong together) rather than a complex FK-repoint now.
- **Evidence upload** accepts storage keys (uploaded via the existing `IStorage` presign, like media); a dedicated verification-doc presign endpoint is future work.

**Why:** org verification is the trust gate that makes representation and paid organizing meaningful; enforcing name-dedup at *approval* (not creation) is both correct and keeps the create path open. Reviewer separation (not SuperAdmin) is least-privilege for the coming console.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **136/136** (+9 `OrgVerificationTests`: submit→pending, invalid-evidence 400, non-member→404, non-reviewer→403, approve→verified, duplicate-verified→409, request-changes→resubmit→approve, suspend, audit-row + search shows verified — all real HTTP against `kurx_test`).

## D-045 · Membership-affiliation verification (re-architecture M6)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** A user's claim to *represent* an org becomes an evidence-backed, reviewed record — never inferred from profile bio.

**Chose:**
- **`MembershipClaim`** (user, org, `ClaimedRole` ∈ Student/Faculty/Employee/Alumni/Founder/Director/Coordinator/Volunteer/ClubPresident/EventLead/Other, status, `FastTrack`, `ValidUntil`, reviewer/notes). Evidence in `verification_documents` (subject = Membership, id = claim id). `Membership` gains `IsVerified`/`SourceClaimId`/`ValidUntil`.
- **Reviewed only from the claim + its documents** — profile bio is structurally excluded (M1 made the profile authority-zero; this module reads only the claim tables). "Bio is never proof" holds by construction.
- **On approval**, the user's operational membership is marked verified — creating a **read-only `Staff` seat** if none. **Organizer rights (Manager/Owner) stay an explicit org-Owner act** (D-015): affiliation-verified ("I'm a student here") is separate from operational authority ("you may publish/spend under our name"). This is the security boundary; it also means the **NSRIT-reuse rule** works (the *org* isn't re-verified — only the person's claim is — but the org still gates who acts on its behalf).
- **`AddMemberAsync` kept as immediate operational add** *(refinement of the dossier's "invite-gated")*: operational membership is the org's own workspace RBAC, legitimately immediate for the Owner; gating it on consent would break ~10 test sites for no trust gain. The consent-based `org_invitations` flow (D-027) remains available and unfinished-by-design (kept, deferred).
- **Fast-track hint**: a claim whose submitter's email domain matches the org's `primary_domain` is flagged `FastTrack` (surfaced first in the reviewer queue). Still reviewed, never auto-approved; email-verification (ID1) would strengthen it but isn't required. Bio is never a signal.
- **Endpoints**: `POST /v1/orgs/{id}/membership-claims`, `GET /v1/me/membership-claims`; reviewer `/v1/admin/membership-claims/{pending, {id}/review}` (VerificationReviewer, live-read). One active claim per (user, org) at a time.
- **Deferred**: request-changes/appeal workflow and the public-profile "verified affiliations" display → M12 / client-parity (the backend claim + `Membership.IsVerified` is what M7 reads).

**Why:** representation is a claim that must be proven, and proving it from evidence (not bio) while keeping *operational authority* under the org's explicit control is what makes the trust model both usable for genuine students and resistant to impersonation.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **143/143** (+7 `MembershipVerificationTests`: submit→pending, invalid role/evidence, duplicate→409, email-domain fast-track, non-reviewer→403, approve→verified Staff + audit, reject→no membership — all real HTTP against `kurx_test`).

## D-046 · Trust capability matrix (re-architecture M7)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** Composes the verification subsystems (M3 identity, M5 org, M6 membership) into **capability flags read live per request**, with L0–L5 as a presentation label — the keystone the event-approval gate (M8) and payouts (M10) read instead of re-deriving rules.

**Chose:**
- **`ITrustService`** with `GetUserCapabilitiesAsync` (`CanOrganizeFree`, `CanOrganizePaid`, `CanReceivePayout`, `IdentityVerified`, `BankVerified`, `Level`) and `GetOrgCapabilitiesAsync` (`CanRepresentOrg`, `IsOrgVerifiedRep`, `IsOrgVerified`). No schema — derived live from the verification tables, so a revocation/suspension is effective next request.
- **Capabilities are truth; the L0–L5 label is derived** (the locked decision). `CanOrganizeFree = any account` (free/private events need no KYC — the brief); `CanOrganizePaid = government-ID/PAN + bank + fraud-clear`; `CanReceivePayout = bank`; `CanRepresentOrg = an approved membership claim (Membership.IsVerified)`; `IsOrgVerifiedRep = that + org Verified`. Gates read the **component flags** (`*_last4` presence, `IsVerified`), not the coarse identity `Level` (avoids "bank-only reads as ID-verified", D-042).
- **Fraud (M13) is a documented no-op for now** (`fraudClear = true`); when M13 lands it only *tightens* `CanOrganizePaid`, never loosens it — so building it now is forward-safe.
- **L-labels**: user-context `/v1/me` reports L1 (account) or L2 (paid organizer); L3+ need org context (`/v1/orgs/{id}/my-capabilities`). L4 (verified org) / L5 (trusted partner) are org-level and land with the payout-tier "clean event" signal (M10+), not fabricated now.
- **Surfaced** on `/v1/me` (`trust` object) and `GET /v1/orgs/{id}/my-capabilities`.

**Why:** a single place that answers "may this user do X?" from live verification state keeps every gate consistent and testable, and makes the trust story legible to clients (badges) without ever trusting a token or a stored score.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **148/148** (+5 `TrustTests`: free-not-paid L1, identity+bank→paid L2, identity-only→not-paid, verified-rep of a verified org, operational-member≠verified-rep — all real HTTP against `kurx_test`).

## D-047 · Event approval + payment gate (re-architecture M8)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** Makes publishing a *paid* event conditional on verification, while keeping free events immediate — the money-safety gate the whole platform hangs on.

**Chose:**
- **Free events publish directly** (org Owner/Manager, `Draft → Published`), immediate, no review — matching the brief's "free private events: no KYC, immediate publishing."
- **Paid events (any priced ticket type) can never self-publish.** They must go `Draft → InReview` (`submit_review`, **gated** on the organizer's `CanOrganizePaid` — identity + bank + fraud-clear, M7 — **and** the owning org being Verified, M5) → a platform **VerificationReviewer** `publish`es (`InReview → Published`). A direct paid publish returns `paid_event_requires_review` (409); an unverified organizer's submit returns `organizer_not_verified_for_paid` / `org_not_verified` (403).
- **Reused the existing `EventStatus` states** (`Draft/InReview/Published/Closed/Archived`) rather than widening the enum to the dossier's `Submitted/UnderReview/Approved/…` *(refinement)*: the dossier's review states map cleanly onto the existing `InReview`, so the gate is delivered with **zero enum change, zero migration, and no breakage** to the existing free-event transition tests. The richer named states are cosmetic and can be added later without changing the gate.
- **`payments_enabled` is computed live, never stored** (`GET /v1/orgs/{org}/events/{id}/payment-readiness` → `{is_paid, payments_enabled, blocking_reasons}`): `paid && Published && organizer CanOrganizePaid && org Verified`, read fresh so a suspension (M5) or fraud flag (M13) stops payments on the next request. M10 reuses this exact computation at charge time.
- **Platform reviewers may publish/reject paid events under review without org membership**; `EventService` gained an `isReviewer` parameter and an `ITrustService` dependency (the gate reads capabilities, never re-derives rules).
- Whether the organizer must additionally be a *verified rep* (vs. just the operational Owner who created the event) is intentionally **not** required — the Owner operating their own verified org, themselves identity+bank verified, is sufficient; requiring a redundant membership claim from the Owner would add friction with no security gain.

**Why:** a paid event moves real money, so it must clear identity + bank + org verification and a human review before it can sell — but free/community events must stay frictionless. Computing `payments_enabled` live (not storing it) is what makes suspension and fraud response effective immediately.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **152/152** (+4 `EventApprovalTests`: free publishes directly, paid can't self-publish → 409, paid submit blocked when unverified → 403, full flow verify→submit→reviewer-publish + live readiness — all real HTTP against `kurx_test`). No migration; existing free-event transition tests unaffected.

## D-048 · KYC term split — org bank verification vs person identity (re-architecture M9)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13). Destructive step (table rename) — implemented data-preserving after explicit approval.** "KYC" was overloaded onto two unrelated things; the new architecture reserves "KYC" for *person* identity (M3, `/v1/me/identity`).

**Chose:**
- **Renamed `kyc_records` → `org_bank_verifications`** and the entity `KycRecord` → `OrgBankVerification`. This is the org's financial verification (penny-drop / PAN-match against its payout account, D-016), reached via `/v1/orgs/{orgId}/kyc/*` — **routes and response shapes are unchanged** (the rename is transparent to EF and to clients).
- **Data-preserving rename, not DROP+CREATE.** EF scaffolded a `DropTable`+`CreateTable` (which would destroy rows); I replaced it with `RenameTable` + `RenameIndex` + `ALTER TABLE … RENAME CONSTRAINT` for the PK/FK. Fully reversible `Down`. Verified the whole chain applies clean on a freshly-reset `kurx_test`.
- **Deleted the dead parallel KYC** — `IKycService`, `KycService`, `KycEndpoints`: a never-mapped second surface that duplicated the org bank/PAN routes and threw `AmbiguousMatchException` at request time (it was commented out of `Program.cs`). Removing it eliminates a live landmine and the duplication.
- **Kept `KycKind`/`KycStatus` enums** (they describe the *kind*/*state* of the bank check — PennyDrop/PanMatch/Digilocker, Pending/Approved/Rejected) and the `KycView`/`KycRecordView`/`KycOutcome` view records, to bound churn; only the entity/table/service were renamed. `IKycProvider` (the provider interface, reused by both org bank verification and person KYC) is unchanged.

**Why:** one word meaning two different verifications guarantees confusion and mis-gating; giving the org-financial check its own name (`org_bank_verifications`) and deleting the broken duplicate makes the split explicit and removes a request-time crash surface — with zero data loss and zero client-visible change.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **152/152** (unchanged — routes/behavior identical; the rename + the existing `OrgTests` bank/PAN cases apply clean on a freshly-reset `kurx_test`).

## D-049 · Paid checkout + ledger write-path (re-architecture M10)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13). Money module — security-reviewed.** Turns "no paid event can sell" into a complete capture → ledger → wallet pipe, on the existing (audited-compatible, D-028/D-031) ledger.

**Chose:**
- **Paid ticket type → a real Pending order.** Supersedes D-021's `payment_not_supported_yet`. `CreateOrderAsync` (paid branch) creates a `Pending` order + an `OrderItem` + a **`SeatHold`** (10-min, reclaimed by `ExpireSeatHoldsJob`, D-029) + increments `Sold`, and calls `IPaymentGateway.CreateOrderAsync` (mock) for the gateway order id. **Tickets are NOT issued yet.** Gated **live** (M8): the event's organizer must have `CanOrganizePaid` and the org must be `Verified`, else `payments_not_enabled` — so a suspended org (M5) can no longer sell, effective on the next order.
- **Razorpay webhook (`POST /v1/webhooks/razorpay`, signature-verified via `IPaymentGateway.VerifyWebhookSignature`) → `ConfirmPaymentAsync`**: **idempotent** (a re-delivered webhook for an already-Paid order is a no-op), records the `Payment`, consumes the seat hold, issues the ticket, and writes **`LedgerEntry(Collected)` + updates the `OrganizationWallet` cache in the same transaction** (the D-028 invariant — never SUM the ledger on the hot path). **The amount is server-authoritative** (`order.AmountPaise`, never a value from the webhook body), so a forged/replayed webhook can't inflate a payout.
- **The money pipe is now complete:** capture → `Collected` → (`CollectedToAvailableLedgerJob`, D-029) → `Available` → withdrawal (D-031). This module built the previously-missing *entry* to the ledger.
- **Real Razorpay adapter deferred** (`RazorpayPaymentGateway`/`IRouteClient` with real HMAC + full webhook envelope + route transfers) — same provider-boundary reality as M3's KYC: not buildable/testable without live keys, so the mock backs the flow and the real adapter is a gated integration task. The webhook body here is the minimal `{order_id, payment_id}` the real adapter would normalise to.
- **Scope bounds (documented, not faked):** paid tickets are **Individual-only** for now (`paid_group_not_supported_yet` — paid group pricing/who-pays is its own product decision); **refunds** (the `Refund` entity exists) are future.
- **`TICKET_HMAC_SECRET` now signs ticket QR codes** (`TokenService.SignTicketCode`), decoupled from the JWT key (fixes the D-021 note; falls back to the JWT secret if unset). Transparent — sign+verify both use the same method, and no real tickets predate this.

**Why:** the ledger/wallet were correct but unfed; this connects real money in without touching that audited bookkeeping, and makes the whole thing safe by keeping the amount server-authoritative, the capture idempotent, and the sell-gate live so verification/suspension actually controls the money.
**Security review:** webhook signature-checked (403 on fail; real HMAC in the deferred adapter); amount server-authoritative; idempotent capture; ledger+wallet atomic; live payment gate; inventory reserved via seat holds; no card data stored (gateway-side). The real-adapter integration will get its own review.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **156/156** (+4 `PaidOrderTests`: Pending order + gateway order, webhook capture → ticket + Collected ledger + wallet cache, idempotent double-webhook, and org-suspension blocks new orders live; plus the updated `OrderTests` paid-gate case — all real HTTP against `kurx_test`). No migration.

## D-050 · Forms convergence — one registration-form system (re-architecture M11). Supersedes D-024.
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13). Destructive drop (unused tables) — approved.** The codebase had two form systems; only one was ever wired.

**Chose:**
- **Retired the event-scoped `registration_forms` / `registration_fields` / `registration_responses` / `registration_response_values` 4-table builder** (D-024). It was **schema-only** — no service, no endpoints, no data, no tests (confirmed: only its entities/enum/DbContext config referenced it) — and duplicated the vocabulary of the **ticket-scoped `FormField`** (D-020), which is the *wired* system that drives per-registration/per-participant `AnswersJson` capture (and paid registration, M10).
- **`FormField` is now the single registration-form system.** Deleted the four entities, the `RegistrationFieldType` enum, and their DbSets/config; the `DropRegistrationForms` migration drops the four tables (dependency-ordered; reversible `Down`; 0 rows today).
- The one genuinely-additive idea D-024 carried — **event-wide standalone surveys/waitlist forms not tied to a ticket type** — is **deferred, not lost**: it can be re-introduced cleanly on `FormField` (or a focused, actually-wired design) if/when a feature schedules it, rather than kept as permanent dead schema.

**Why:** two overlapping systems where one is dead is a maintenance and correctness hazard (which one is authoritative?); collapsing to the proven, wired `FormField` removes the ambiguity and 4 unused tables with zero behavior change. Retiring at the *contract* phase (after confirming no consumer) is the safe half of expand→migrate→contract.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **156/156** (unchanged — the tables were never exercised; the drop applies clean on a freshly-reset `kurx_test`). 72 → 68 tables.

## D-051 · Admin verification console — backend (re-architecture M12)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** The review *queues* and *actions* already existed (org M5, membership M6, both reviewer-gated). M12 adds the genuinely-new admin capabilities on top of them.

**Chose:**
- **Org merge (`POST /v1/admin/orgs/merge`)** — completes the piece M5 deferred. Repoints the duplicate's memberships (dropping a seat where the user is already in the canonical org), membership claims, and aliases; records the **duplicate's name as an alias of the canonical org** (so its name still resolves); and soft-deletes the duplicate with `CanonicalOrgId` → survivor. **Bounded to a FRESH duplicate**: blocked (`cannot_merge_has_events` / `_ledger` / `_funds`) if it has any events or financial history — those reference the org id and need manual ops, never a silent repoint. All in one transaction.
- **Blacklist (`POST …/verification/blacklist`)** — a terminal org block (`OrgVerificationStatus.Blacklisted`, the state M5 already defined), for impersonation/fraud.
- **Cross-subject verification history (`GET /v1/admin/verifications/{subjectType}/{subjectId}/history`)** — the read side of the console: every `verification_reviews` decision + `verification_documents` entry for any subject (identity/organization/membership/event), straight off the M0 substrate. Storage keys are not listed (a presigned URL is fetched per-document when opened).
- **Appeals via resubmission** — a rejected org may re-submit (M5 allows `submit` from `Rejected`) and a rejected membership may file a fresh claim (M6); a dedicated first-class appeals queue is deferred rather than duplicating that.
- **The `admin/` Next.js UI is Pending Stitch UI** — deferred to the consolidated client-parity pass, consistent with how every client surface (web/mobile) has been handled across M4–M11. The admin *backend* is complete and integration-tested; the console UI is generated + wired later.
- All admin endpoints gated by the **`VerificationReviewer`** platform role (live-read, M2).

**Why:** merge is the one missing lever to actually *resolve* the duplicates the registry surfaces (M4) and the verification gate blocks (M5); keeping it bounded to fresh duplicates makes it safe to expose to reviewers; and one history endpoint over the shared substrate gives the console a complete, uniform audit trail without per-subject bespoke reads.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **161/161** (+5 `AdminConsoleTests`: merge repoints members + records alias, merge blocked when the duplicate has events, blacklist, verification history, non-reviewer → 403 — all real HTTP against `kurx_test`). No migration.

## D-052 · Fraud prevention (re-architecture M13 — final module)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-13).** Closes the loop: makes the M7 `fraudClear` gate real, so verification alone no longer implies trust — a flagged actor loses privileged capabilities live.

**Chose:**
- **`blacklist_entries`** — hard blocks on a known-bad identifier (`Phone`/`Email`/`Device`/`OrgName`/`DocHash`), stored **normalized** (phone E.164, email lowercased, org name via the M4 normalizer) with a unique `(kind, value)` index so lookups are exact and case/format-insensitive.
- **`fraud_signals`** — polymorphic (same subjects as the M0 substrate) risk signals (`Device`/`Ip`/`Velocity`/`DuplicateAccount`/`DocHash`/`DisposableContact`/`GeoMismatch`/`Manual`); a subject's **risk score is the sum of its signal scores**.
- **`IFraudService`** — blocklist add/list/remove, record-signal, risk-score, and **`IsUserClearAsync`**: a user is clear iff their phone/email aren't blacklisted **and** their risk score is below `HighRiskThreshold` (100).
- **Tightened M7's `fraudClear`** from a `const true` to a **live** `IsUserClearAsync` read. So a blacklisted or high-risk user's `CanOrganizePaid` becomes false, which cascades into the **event-publish gate (M8)** and **payment gate (M10)** — effective on the next request. As promised in D-046, M13 only *tightened* the gate, never loosened it.
- **Enforced the blocklist at org creation** — a blacklisted org name can't be (re)created (`org_blacklisted`), the anti-impersonation counterpart to M12's blacklist/merge.
- **`RiskFlag` (org/event-scoped) left as-is** — `fraud_signals` is the new *polymorphic* risk store that extends coverage to users/identity/membership without mutating `RiskFlag`'s non-null `OrgId` FK (the two coexist; the dossier's "extend RiskFlag" is realised as the additive `fraud_signals` rather than a risky FK change).
- **Signal *generation* is the data layer, deferred:** the scoring + enforcement framework is complete and manual/admin signals + blacklist work today; automated producers (device fingerprinting, velocity counters, duplicate-account graph, disposable-email detection) are follow-ups that simply call `RecordSignalAsync`.
- Admin endpoints (`/v1/admin/blacklist`, `/v1/admin/fraud-signals`) gated by `VerificationReviewer`.

**Why:** verification proves *who you are*; fraud prevention decides *whether we still trust you*. Making `fraudClear` live and blocklist-backed means a suspension, blacklist, or risk spike immediately strips the ability to run paid events or receive payouts — the last safety layer over the whole trust model.
**Verification:** `dotnet build` clean; `dotnet test` **166/166** (+5 `FraudTests`: blacklisted phone → loses paid-organizing live, high risk score → loses paid-organizing, blacklisted org name → `org_blacklisted`, admin blacklist add/list/remove, non-reviewer → 403 — all real HTTP against `kurx_test`). 68 → 70 tables.

## D-055 · Affiliation + proof is attached at event creation (not a standalone "create/manage org" flow)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-15). ⚠️ Partly SUPERSEDED — see [D-074](#), [D-267](#), [D-268](#).** Its
event-first instinct survives; its mechanics do not. D-074 replaced implicit org creation + `Owner` with an
admin-approved representation request. **D-268 retired the "personal org" this entry introduced as a
user-facing concept entirely** — a user representing themselves is `Representing = Personal`, and the
`IsPersonal` row is a persistence detail that appears in no API, DTO, route, label or document.

Product-model clarification of how an organizer proves they may run an event on behalf of an institution. Supersedes the earlier framing (`docs/history/architecture/TRUST_MODEL_VS_BUILT.md`) that assumed a standalone create-organization + registry-management surface.

**The model (as directed):**
- There is **no separate "create/manage an organization" area.** The user never administers an org as its own thing.
- **Free / private (no money)** event → needs only the **creator's own identity**. No org, no proof. *(The org-less personal-event path is an open sub-decision — see below.)*
- **Money involved / public institutional** event → the creator attaches an **affiliation** ("this event is for **NSRIT College**, a College") **plus proof of belonging** (letterhead / ID / official doc) **at event-creation time.**
- Proof is **remembered per organization** (uploaded once, **reused** across that org's future events) — **not** re-uploaded per event.
- **An admin verifies the proof first** (call/email the institution). **Nothing auto-publishes** off a self-service upload; events stay non-live until the affiliation is verified, and paid events remain gated by the existing publish/review flow (D-047).

**Chose (reuse the built trust engine — M4/M5/M6/M8/M12 — surfaced inside event creation):**
- The institution is still an **`organizations` row**, but **created implicitly** from what the organizer types (name + `OrganizationType`) via the existing `POST /v1/orgs` (which makes them Owner) — **no standalone create-org form, no registry-management dashboard** as primary destinations. Search (`GET /v1/orgs/search`) is used only to dedup against an existing institution.
- "Proof you belong" = existing **`verification_documents`** (letterhead) + **`membership_claims`** (person↔org, M6) + the **org verification lifecycle** (M5). Collected **in one step of the event-creation flow**, not as separate screens.
- Call/email → the **existing admin review queues** (`/v1/admin/orgs/pending` + `.../verification/review`, `/v1/admin/membership-claims/pending` + `.../review`), which have **no UI yet** — the admin app is the largest remaining surface.
- **One new backend keystone:** an **org-scoped media presign** — `POST /v1/orgs/{orgId}/media/presign` — so a letterhead can be uploaded **before any event exists** and **at org level** (an org credential must outlive any single event and be uploadable when affiliating with an existing org). Reusing the event-scoped presign (`.../events/{eventId}/media/presign`) was **rejected**: it needs an event to exist and stores the credential under `events/{id}/media/*`, which breaks the "remembered per org, reused across events" requirement. `IMediaService.PresignOrgDocAsync` mirrors `PresignUploadAsync` exactly (Owner/Manager/Admin; 404-not-403), keys under `orgs/{orgId}/verification/*`.

**[Just me] org-less personal event — RESOLVED (2026-07-15): auto-personal-org.** The no-org event-creation step now offers **[Just me]** vs **[An organization]**. **[Just me]** silently creates a lightweight personal org (`type: other`, named after the user) via `createPersonalOrgAction` so **`Event.OrgId` stays non-null — no org-scoped-query ripple** (the alternative, nullable `OrgId`, was rejected for its large blast radius). The personal org is **never submitted for verification**, so it can only ever run **free** events (paid still requires a verified real org — D-047).

**G6 registry-search pollution — RESOLVED (2026-07-15): explicit `IsPersonal` flag.** A personal org must not surface in `GET /v1/orgs/search`. The **rejected** first attempt filtered on "verified-or-has-events" — but a freshly-created *real* institution is *also* Unverified with no events (that's the exact dedup case registry search exists for, and the `OrgRegistryTests` prove it), so status/activity can't discriminate. Added a single **`Organization.IsPersonal` boolean** (additive migration `AddOrganizationIsPersonal`, `NOT NULL DEFAULT false` — a tiny, safe change, unrelated to the nullable-`OrgId` ripple that was rejected). `createOrg(personal: true)` sets it on the [Just me] path; search filters `!IsPersonal`. Covered by two new CI tests (personal hidden; unverified-real still findable).

**Why:** the whole "College → letterhead → verify the person belongs → grant permission → paid needs approval" engine already exists (D-039…D-052); this is a **UX re-shape + one small endpoint**, not a re-architecture. Reference: `docs/history/architecture/TRUST_MODEL_VS_BUILT.md`.

**Verification:** ✅ **CI green (PR #1, 2026-07-15)** — backend build + full suite **170 passed** against Postgres 17 + `kurx_test` (run `29380768624`); the `AddOrganizationIsPersonal` migration applied cleanly and the two new G6 tests passed. Web + admin CI green too. **Follow-up landed (G1):** the presign now has **3 dedicated tests** (owner 200 + org-key prefix; non-member 404; Staff 403) and its authz was **hardened to 404-not-403** for non-members (D-018), matching its sibling `verification/submit` — the earlier 403 leaked org existence. Frontend slices verified in the browser.

## D-056 · Staff & role management (admin console — first M12 client slice)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-15).** First operational module of the dedicated `admin/` console (see `admin/ADMIN_AUDIT_AND_ROADMAP.md`). The `platform_roles` table + `IPlatformRoleService` (grant/revoke/read-live) already existed from M2 (D-040) — this exposes them over HTTP and in the admin UI. No new persistence.

**The model:**
- **"Staff" == holding a platform role.** There is no separate staff-account entity. Making someone staff = granting them a `PlatformRole`; removing them = revoking every role. This reuses the existing live-per-request authority (D-040) — a grant/revoke takes effect on the target's **next request**, nothing is baked into a JWT.
- **Grant is by phone**, normalized with the same `AuthService.NormalizePhone` as login, and **the target must already be a registered user** (they log in once via OTP first) — `user_not_found` (404) otherwise. **No provisioning of unknown phones** here (unlike org `AddMemberAsync`, D-015): granting platform power to a phantom account is a footgun; requiring a real prior sign-in is the safer default. Provisioning can be added later if onboarding needs it.
- **SuperAdmin-only.** All `/v1/admin/staff` routes use `RequireAuthorization("SuperAdmin")` (live policy). Managing who holds platform power is the most privileged action, so it sits above the reviewer/finance/support split.
- **Last-SuperAdmin guard.** Revoking `SuperAdmin` is refused (`cannot_revoke_last_superadmin`, 409) when it would drop the platform to zero active SuperAdmins — prevents self-lockout / total lockout. Any other revoke (including a SuperAdmin revoking their *own* role while another exists) is allowed.

**Endpoints (new `AdminStaffEndpoints`):**
- `GET /v1/admin/staff?q=&role=` — everyone with ≥1 active platform role, grouped to one row per user (`user_id, name, phone, username, roles[]`). `q` matches name/phone/username; `role` filters. In-memory grouping over the tiny staff set (documented; add a query-side rollup only if staff ever grows large).
- `POST /v1/admin/staff/grant { phone, role, expiresAt? }` — resolve phone→user, grant (idempotent upsert via `IPlatformRoleService.GrantAsync`, `GrantedBy` = caller). `invalid_role` / `phone_required` / `user_not_found`.
- `DELETE /v1/admin/staff/{userId}/roles/{role}` — revoke (with the last-SuperAdmin guard). `invalid_role`.

**`GET /v1/me` now returns `platform_roles: string[]`** (the live active roles), so the admin app's `deriveRoles` resolves the full RBAC instead of only `VerificationReviewer` via `is_platform_reviewer` (which is retained, now `SuperAdmin`-inclusive). This unblocks role-based nav across the whole console.

**Roles unchanged — `RiskTeam`/`Moderator` deferred.** The `PlatformRole` enum stays at the 5 that have live capability wiring (`SuperAdmin, VerificationReviewer, FinanceOps, Support, ReadOnlyAuditor`). The audit-requested `RiskTeam`/`Moderator` are a **decorative role with no gate** until a module actually authorizes on them; adding them is a one-line enum + migration when that module lands (YAGNI — don't ship roles nothing checks).

**Why:** the highest-value, lowest-risk first admin slice — the data layer was done, so this is a thin endpoint + UI, and it unblocks every other role-gated console page by making `platform_roles` real end-to-end.

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required.** Backend builds clean (`dotnet build`, 0 warnings); **backend integration tests cannot run on this dev host** (Windows Application Control blocks the test host, `0x800711C7`) — the grant/revoke/last-SuperAdmin/`user_not_found` branches need a CI run (`kurx_test`) to be considered green. Admin app typechecks clean. **PII note:** `GET /v1/admin/staff` returns staff names/phones to SuperAdmin only — acceptable (SuperAdmin manages staff); a security review sign-off is still owed before merge per CLAUDE.md §7.

## D-057 · Admin event-approval queue (completes the M8 flow's admin surface)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-15).** M8 (D-047) built the event-approval *logic* — a paid event can't self-publish; it goes `Draft → submit_review → InReview`, and a platform reviewer publishes it. But there was **no admin surface to find events awaiting review** — the transition endpoint is org-scoped and a reviewer would have to already know each event id. This adds the missing queue.

**The model:**
- **One new read endpoint** — `GET /v1/admin/events/pending` (VerificationReviewer): every event currently `InReview` across all orgs, oldest-first, with its org name (`IEventService.ListInReviewAsync` → `PendingEventView`). That's the entire new backend surface.
- **Approve/reject reuse the existing transition** — `POST /v1/orgs/{orgId}/events/{eventId}/transition` with `action: "publish"` (approve) or `"reject"`. `TransitionAsync` already takes `isReviewer` and lets a reviewer drive **any** org's event (the events group is `RequireAuthorization()` with per-action authz in the service, M8). So **no dedicated admin action endpoint was added** — that would duplicate a working, tested path. The queue returns `org_id` per row precisely so the client can address the transition.
- **The gate is re-checked live on transition**, never trusted from the queue snapshot: publish re-verifies org-verified + organizer paid-capable, so a stale queue can't push an unqualified event live.

**Deliberately deferred — a full event-detail review view.** The queue shows title + org + dates, not the event's full content (tickets/pricing/description). The M8 approval gate is about **org/organizer trust** (already confirmed in the Verification queue), not event-content moderation (that's Reports, a separate Tier-B module). A read-only `GET /v1/admin/events/{id}` review view is a documented follow-up; note that a non-SuperAdmin reviewer currently can't load an InReview event via the public `/v1/events/{slug}` (it 404s for non-members, and `isAdmin` = SuperAdmin only), so that view needs its own reviewer-scoped endpoint when built.

**Why:** the approval engine already existed and is CI-tested; the only real gap was *discoverability* of the queue. A single list endpoint + a reviewer UI closes it without touching the tested transition path — the laziest complete fix.

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required.** Backend builds clean; admin `next build` clean (`/events/pending`). `AdminEventQueueTests` (lists an InReview event, drops it after approve-via-transition, non-reviewer 403) **compiles** but runs only in CI (local test host blocked, `0x800711C7`).

## D-058 · Admin dashboard summary (makes the console landing page real)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-15).** The console landing page shipped with placeholder tiles (all `—`) because there was no `GET /v1/admin/dashboard/summary`. This adds it with the counts that have real data today.

**The model:**
- **One read endpoint** — `GET /v1/admin/dashboard/summary` → live COUNTs: `pending_org_verifications`, `pending_membership_claims`, `pending_events`, `blacklist_entries`, `staff_count`, `new_users_24h`, `total_users`, `total_orgs`, `total_events`.
- **Reuses the queues' exact "pending" definitions** (org `VerificationStatus == PendingReview && DeletedAt == null`; claim status ∈ {Submitted, UnderReview, OfficialContactVerification}; event `Status == InReview`) so a tile can never disagree with the queue it links to. Cheap `CountAsync`es, computed live — no rollup table (YAGNI at current scale; add one only if it's ever slow).
- **Any-staff gated, not reviewer-only.** Every staff role lands on this dashboard, and the numbers are non-PII aggregates, so the gate is "holds ≥1 platform role" — enforced inline via `IPlatformRoleService.GetRolesAsync` (returns `forbidden` for a role-less user) rather than a per-role policy or a new "AnyStaff" policy. A plain authenticated user gets 403.
- **Only real data is surfaced.** Revenue / payouts / refunds / open-reports tiles are deliberately absent — that data doesn't exist yet (Tier-C Finance + Reports). The frontend labels them as arriving later rather than faking a number.

**Why:** the landing page is every staff member's first screen; it was inert. Cheap counts over data that already exists turn it into a real operations view, and reusing the queue predicates keeps it honest. Closes the second of the two `admin/STATUS.md` §5 backend gaps (the first, `platform_roles` on `/v1/me`, closed in D-056).

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required.** Backend builds clean; admin `next build` clean. `AdminDashboardTests` (a Support user — lowest-privilege staff — sees the summary with all 9 keys ≥ 0; a role-less user 403s) **compiles**, runs in CI (`0x800711C7` blocks the local test host).

## D-059 · Content moderation reports (C-5 — first moderation module)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-15).** The `reports` table existed (polymorphic `EntityType`/`EntityId`, `Status` open/resolved/dismissed, `ResolvedBy`/`ResolvedAt`) with **no service or endpoints**. This wires the full report → triage → resolve loop.

**The model:**
- **Create is any authenticated user** — `POST /v1/reports { entityType, entityId, reason, details? }`. `entityType` ∈ {event, review, chat_message, user, org} (`invalid_entity_type` otherwise); `reason` required. **One open report per (reporter, entity)** — a second open report of the same subject by the same user is `already_reported` (409), so one user can't flood the queue. (The create endpoint has no admin-app UI — it's for the web/mobile clients where content is viewed; the admin app only triages.)
- **Triage is Moderation staff** — new `Moderation` authorization policy = `SuperAdmin | VerificationReviewer | Support` (matches the RBAC matrix's Reports row; Support handles complaints, reviewers handle trust). `GET /v1/admin/reports?status=`, `POST /v1/admin/reports/{id}/{resolve|dismiss}`.
- **Resolve/dismiss are terminal + audited** — a closed report can't be re-closed (`already_closed`, 409); each resolution appends an `audit_log` row (`report.resolve`/`report.dismiss`, actor + entity). `resolve` = action taken, `dismiss` = no action; both just close the report (taking the *actual* action on the reported content — hide/ban — is a follow-up that ties into user/event moderation, Tier-C).
- **Business logic lives in `IReportService`** (Infrastructure), not the endpoint — validation, dedup, state transition, and the audit write are all in the service (CLAUDE.md §2: Api never does business logic).

**Deliberately deferred:** acting on the reported content (hide event / ban user / delete message) — that needs the Tier-C user/event-management endpoints; for now triage records the decision + audit trail. Reporter-name enrichment on the queue (a join) is also skipped — the raw `reporter_id`/`entity_id` are shown; add the join when reviewers ask for it.

**Why:** moderation is a launch-blocking safety capability (C-5, P1) and the table already existed — a thin service + two endpoint groups + a triage UI closes it. New `Moderation` policy is the one genuinely-new primitive (reviewers *and* support both triage, which no existing single-role policy expresses).

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required.** Backend builds clean; admin `next build` clean (`/reports`). `ModerationTests` (file a report; duplicate → `already_reported`; `invalid_entity_type`; Support lists + resolves once then `already_closed`; plain user triage 403) **compiles**, runs in CI (`0x800711C7`).

## D-060 · User administration + account moderation (first Tier-C module)
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-17). ⚠️ SECURITY REVIEW REQUIRED before merge** (auth-path + PII change, CLAUDE.md §10). First Tier-C admin module — unlike Tier-A/B (which wired existing backend), this adds **new schema + an auth-enforcement change**.

**The model:**
- **Two holds on `users` (additive nullable columns):** `SuspendedAt` (reversible hold), `BannedAt` (hard block), `ModerationReason` (shown to staff). Both null = active. Migration `AddUserModeration`.
- **Enforcement is at authentication** (`AuthService`), which is the single choke point that matters: a suspended/banned account **can't obtain a token** — `VerifyOtpAsync` refuses with `account_suspended`/`account_banned` (401), and `RefreshAsync` refuses + revokes. On suspend/ban the service also **revokes all refresh tokens immediately** (the same `ExecuteUpdateAsync` reuse-revokes-all path as phone-change, D-038), so a live session dies at its next refresh. `unban` clears both holds.
- **Suspend vs ban** today enforce **identically** (both block login/refresh) — the difference is **severity/intent + which flag**, surfaced in the UI + audit. Kept deliberately simple; a divergent enforcement (e.g. suspend = lose capabilities but can still attend) can be added later without a schema change.
- **Gate = the `Moderation` policy** (SuperAdmin / VerificationReviewer / Support, from D-059) on `GET /v1/admin/users` + `POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/{suspend|ban|unban}`. **Guards:** a staff member can't moderate **themselves** (`cannot_moderate_self`) or a **SuperAdmin** (`cannot_moderate_superadmin`) — protects trusted accounts from lockout/abuse. Every action writes `audit_log` (`user.suspend|ban|unban`, actor + reason).
- **Search** requires a term (phone/name/username ILIKE); **empty search returns only the currently-moderated accounts**, never a full-table dump (privacy + perf).

**Known limitation (documented, not a bug):** a suspended user's **already-issued access token stays valid until it expires** (≤ access-token TTL, ~1h) — enforcement is at token *issuance/refresh*, not per-request. For the high-impact actions (organizing/payments) capabilities are already read live (M7), and sessions are revoked so no renewal is possible; a per-request suspension check (or shorter TTL) is the follow-up if immediate hard cut-off is ever needed.

**Deferred:** user **merge** (needs its own `D-NNN` — non-trivial FK repoint); a rich user **detail view** (tickets/events/payments/verification) — the list shows core fields + moderation state, the activity view is a follow-up; live capability-layer suspension (above).

**Migration note — hand-authored.** `dotnet ef migrations add` **cannot run on this dev host** (the EF design-time host loads the app, which pulls `StackExchange.Redis.dll` — blocked by Windows Application Control, `0x800711C7`). The migration was written by hand (additive nullable columns only, lowest-risk shape) with an inline `[Migration]` attribute so `MigrateAsync()` discovers + applies it exactly like a scaffolded one, and `KurxDbContextModelSnapshot` was updated so the next tooling-generated migration diffs correctly. **CI must confirm it applies cleanly on `kurx_test`** (both tests and prod run `MigrateAsync()` at boot).

**Why:** moderation (D-059) could only *record* decisions; suspend/ban is how staff actually act on an abusive account, and it closes the loop. The account already flows through one auth choke point, so enforcing there is the smallest correct change.

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required** (and security review owed). Backend builds clean; admin `next build` clean (`/users`). `UserModerationTests` (suspend blocks fresh login + unban clears; suspended account can't refresh; ban → `account_banned`; non-moderator 403; can't moderate a SuperAdmin or self) **compiles**, runs only in CI (`0x800711C7`). The hand-written migration is **unverified locally** — CI is the first real apply.

## D-061 · Global event management (admin) — no new schema
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-17).** Platform-wide event admin, built entirely on columns that already exist (`Event.IsFeatured`, `DeletedAt`, `Status`, `PublishedAt`) — **no migration**.

- **Search** — `GET /v1/admin/events?q=&status=` (`IEventService.ListForAdminAsync`): every non-deleted event across all orgs and **all statuses** (the public `SearchAsync` is Published-only), newest first, with org name + featured flag. Reviewer-gated.
- **Feature / unfeature** — `POST /v1/admin/events/{id}/{feature|unfeature}` toggles the existing `IsFeatured` (the public discovery signal). Admin curation.
- **Force publish / unpublish** — **reuse the org-scoped transition** (reviewer-capable, M8), same as event approval; the client calls it with the `org_id` the list returns. No duplicate endpoint.
- **Deferred (documented):** *suspend/hide* as a distinct state — it would need a new column **and** changes to every public event read path (search/detail/featured/trending) to honour it; "unpublish" already removes an event from public, so suspend is deferred until a genuine "hidden but not unpublished" need appears. Also deferred: **pin** (needs a `PinnedAt` column + ordering), **transfer-ownership**, admin **edit**, and hard **delete** (soft-delete via `DeletedAt` exists but isn't surfaced — destructive, wants its own decision).

**Why:** the highest-value event-admin actions (find any event, curate featured, force publish/unpublish) all ride existing columns + the tested transition — a search endpoint + a feature toggle is the whole new surface.

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required.** Backend builds clean; admin `next build` clean (`/events`). `AdminEventQueueTests` gains coverage (admin search lists an event; feature/unfeature toggles `is_featured`; non-reviewer 403) — **compiles**, runs in CI (`0x800711C7`).

## D-062 · Admin audit-log viewer — read-only
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-17).** A read view over the `audit_log` the platform already writes — no new schema, no writes.

- `GET /v1/admin/audit?actor=&entity=&action=&limit=` — newest-first audit rows (actor, action, entity, details, time). Gated by a new **`Audit` policy** (`SuperAdmin | ReadOnlyAuditor`) — the first use of the read-only auditor role. Read-only, so the query lives in the endpoint (not a service).
- **Coverage caveat (documented):** the viewer is only as complete as what *writes* `audit_log`. Today that's auth (`auth.login`, phone-change, token-reuse), event lifecycle (`event.create`), moderation (`report.resolve|dismiss`), and user moderation (`user.suspend|ban|unban`). A **uniform audit-write interceptor** on every admin mutation (so org verification, blacklist, staff grants, event feature, etc. all land here) is the follow-up that makes this the complete "nothing happens without an audit log" surface the audit envisioned.

**Why:** the auditor role + the `audit_log` table both already existed with no way to read them; a single filtered read endpoint activates both. Broadening what gets written is incremental and doesn't block the viewer.

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required.** Backend builds clean; admin `next build` clean (`/audit`). (No dedicated test this pass — pure read over an existing table gated by an authorization policy; the policy wiring mirrors the CI-tested Moderation/VerificationReviewer gates.)

## D-063 · Platform analytics — read-only growth aggregates, no revenue
**Status: ACCEPTED (2026-07-17).** `GET /v1/admin/analytics?days=` over the real users/orgs/events data: `signups_by_day`, `events_by_day`, `events_by_status`, `top_organizers` (by published-event count), `top_events` (by views), plus headline totals. Any-staff gated (non-PII aggregates), same inline role check as the dashboard summary (D-058). No new schema; enum→string and date→string formatting happen in memory (EF can't translate them).

**Deliberately excludes revenue / conversion / ticket-sales metrics** — money doesn't move yet (Razorpay is `MockPaymentGateway`, no captured payments), so those numbers would be fabricated. They arrive with the Finance module once real payments flow. Showing only what's real (growth, activity) keeps the page honest — the same principle as the dashboard's absent revenue tiles.

**Why:** growth analytics over data that already exists is genuinely useful and needs no backend it doesn't have. Chosen over the other "missing" modules precisely because it's *real*: a feature-flags/settings table nothing reads, or a finance console over zero transactions, would be decorative — this isn't.

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required.** Backend builds clean; admin `next build` clean (`/analytics`). (No dedicated test — read-only aggregation behind the same any-staff gate as D-058; correctness of the GROUP BY translations is confirmed by the CI run against `kurx_test`.)

## D-064 · Complete the scaffolded non-provider features (Category A)
**Status: IN PROGRESS (2026-07-17).** Umbrella decision for finishing the "unfinished scaffolding" (D-018) that needs **no real provider** — tables/entities existed with no service or endpoints. Built in CI-validated batches. **Excludes** anything gated on real providers (Razorpay/SES/WhatsApp/FCM/S3/DigiLocker) or the money flow (refunds, payouts, cancellation) — those wait for go-live.

**EF discipline for the whole batch** (a CI-caught trap in D-061): never call `enum.ToString()` inside a LINQ-to-SQL projection, and never `ORDER BY` a property of a *constructor*-projected record. Order by columns / anonymous-type properties, then map to records + stringify enums **in memory** after materialization.

**Shipped so far:**
- **A1 — Saved events + org follows** (`ISocialService`): `POST/DELETE /v1/events/{id}/save`, `GET /v1/me/saved`; `POST/DELETE /v1/orgs/{id}/follow`, `GET /v1/me/following`. Idempotent; save requires a visible Published+Public event (else `not_found`). Over `saved_events` / `organization_followers`.
- **A2 — Event reviews / ratings** (`IEventReviewService`): `POST /v1/events/{id}/reviews` (upsert = edit), `GET .../reviews` (public, paginated + avg/count summary), `DELETE .../reviews/mine`. Eligibility = the caller holds an issued ticket for the event (`Ticket.EventId`+`UserId` are denormalized → one `AnyAsync`); `review_requires_ticket` (403) otherwise, `invalid_rating` (1–5). Over `event_reviews`.
- **A5 — Org invitations** (`IOrgInvitationService`): invite a teammate by phone → they accept a token to join. `POST/GET /v1/orgs/{id}/invitations`, `DELETE …/{id}`, `GET /v1/me/org-invitations`, `POST /v1/org-invitations/{token}/{accept|decline}`. Owner invites any role, Manager Staff-only (D-015); **accept creates the membership** + audit row. Possession of the token is *not* enough — the accepting account's phone / invited-user-id must match (a leaked token can't be redeemed by someone else). Over `org_invitations`.
- **A4 — Event assignments** (`IEventAssignmentService`): Owner/Manager assign a user to a role (14 standard + Custom) at an event; invitee accepts/declines their own. `POST/GET/DELETE /v1/orgs/{o}/events/{e}/assignments[/{id}]`, `POST /v1/assignments/{id}/{accept|decline}`, `GET /v1/me/assignments`. `invalid_role`/`custom_role_required`/`user_not_found`; idempotent per (event, user, role). Over `event_assignments`.

- **A6 — In-app notifications + device registration** (endpoints over the previously-*dead* `NotificationService`, which was fully implemented but never registered in DI nor exposed): `GET /v1/me/notifications` (`{ items, unread_count }`), `POST .../{id}/read`, `POST .../read-all`, `POST/DELETE /v1/me/devices[/{id}]`. The FCM push **send** stays deferred (provider); the in-app feed + token registration are pure DB and ship now. Registered `INotificationService` in DI.
- **A8 — Certificate roster** (`ICertificateService.ListForEventAsync`): `GET /v1/events/{eventId}/certificates` (Owner/Manager/Admin) — who holds a certificate, verify code, kind, revocation state. Closes the "could generate but not list/revoke per event" gap.

- **A3 — Waitlist** (`IWaitlistService`): `POST/DELETE /v1/events/{e}/ticket-types/{tt}/waitlist`, `GET /v1/me/waitlist`. Join only when sold out (`Sold >= Quantity`, else `tickets_available`); FIFO `Position`; `already_waitlisted`. Over `ticket_waitlist`. **Auto-promotion deferred** — it needs a capacity-freeing trigger (refund/cancel) that doesn't exist yet; the `ExpireWaitlistOffersJob` is already in place for the offer window.
- **A7 (free/paid filter — the no-schema half)**: `GET /v1/events?price=free|paid` — `free` = no priced ticket type (EXISTS subquery), `paid` = at least one. Added as an optional `EventListFilter.Price` (no caller breakage).
- **A7 online/hybrid `EventMode`**: `EventMode { Offline, Online, Hybrid }` + `Event.OnlineUrl`, migration `AddEventMode` (text NOT NULL default 'Offline' + nullable url; enums store as text via the `OnModelCreating` convention). Threaded through the core event flow — `CreateEventBody`/`UpdateEventBody` → `CreateEventInput`/`UpdateEventInput` (added as **optional trailing params** so nothing breaks) → `EventService` create/update → entity → `EventDetail`. Validation: Online/Hybrid ⇒ `online_url_required`. Search gains `?mode=offline|online|hybrid`. (Venue validation left unchanged — an online event still carries placeholder venue text; making venue optional-for-online is a small follow-up.)

**Remaining in this umbrella:** only **A9 client wiring** (web + mobile) — the whole non-provider backend backlog (A1–A8) is now built.

**Verification:** ⚠️ **CI-verification-required.** Backend + test project compile clean; `EngagementTests` (save/list/unsave, follow/list/unfollow, save-404, ticket-holder-reviews-but-stranger-403, invalid-rating) runs in CI against `kurx_test` (local host blocked, 0x800711C7).
## D-065 · Mobile design system — Stitch warm palette replaces GitHub-dark/coral (2026-07-16)
**Status: ACCEPTED.**

The Flutter `design_tokens.dart` previously used a GitHub-dark / coral accent palette (`#FF5A3C` dark, `#CF4225` light), matching the web surface. The mobile Stitch design brief (kurx-stitch-prompts.md Part 0) specifies a distinct warm-event palette: orange primary `#F0762B`, teal secondary `#1F6B5C`, cream card surface `#FFF8F0`, screen background `#FFFCF8`, and a peach→mint gradient behind phone frames. These are irreconcilable without a choice.

**Chose:** the Stitch warm palette wins on mobile. Rationale: mobile is an attendee-first surface (concerts, festivals); the warm palette reads "event" while the GitHub-dark/coral reads "developer tool". The web and admin surfaces retain the existing palette unchanged — three surfaces, two visual registers.

**Changes:** `design_tokens.dart` gains a `teal` semantic token (`#1F6B5C` light / `#2A8B78` dark), warms all background/card/border tokens; `app_theme.dart` updates card radius to 24 px (was 16), button height to 56 px pill shape (was 52 px `KRadius.md`), cards drop the border in favour of a soft shadow; Plus Jakarta Sans loaded via `google_fonts` package; `kurx_button.dart` primary variant uses `KRadius.pill`; `kurx_card.dart` uses `KRadius.xl` + shadow. Every existing screen inherits via `context.kurx.*` — no per-screen colour literals changed.
**Why:** smallest token-layer swap; no business logic touched; web/admin unaffected.

The Stitch style guide specifies 5 tabs (Home / Browse / Tickets / Profile / Saved) in a floating pill/rounded bar with an orange circle highlight on the active tab — a layout the stock `NavigationBar` widget cannot render without custom wrapping.
