## D-067 · GET /v1/me/certificates — private authenticated certificate list (2026-07-16)
**Status: ACCEPTED.**

The existing `GET /v1/users/{username}/certificates` (PublicProfileEndpoints) is the only certificate listing endpoint — it is public and username-keyed. The My Certificates mobile screen requires an authenticated private list (the user sees their own certificates without exposing the username in the URL path, and without the public-visibility filter a public endpoint would apply).

**Chose:** add `GET /v1/me/certificates` in `CertificateEndpoints`, authenticated (`RequireAuthorization()`). Implemented as a direct EF Core query in the endpoint handler (same pattern as the existing public `GET /v1/certificates/{code}` in that file — `ICertificateService` covers business logic, not read-only projections). Joins `certificates` with `events` for event title; orders by `created_at DESC`. Returns `[{id, code, event_id, event_title, template_id, issued_at, revoked_at, is_revoked, pdf_url, verify_code}]` — `pdf_url` is null in the list (presigning is expensive; the detail screen fetches it from the public endpoint on demand). Includes revoked entries so users can see their full history. No PII beyond what `/v1/me` already exposes.
**Why:** public/private semantics must stay separate (a public endpoint must apply visibility rules; a private one must be caller-scoped only); the shortest delta is one new route, no new service method needed since this is a pure projection with no business logic.

## D-068 · PATCH /v1/.../announcements/{id} — announcement edit endpoint (2026-07-16)
**Status: ACCEPTED.**

`AnnouncementEndpoints` has `POST` (create) + `GET` (list/get) + `DELETE` but no update. The Organizer Operations screen ("Announcements — create, edit, stats") implies an edit flow. Omitting edit means the screen must silently drop the edit case or show a disabled UI state that contradicts what was built.

**Chose:** add `PATCH /v1/announcements/{announcementId}` — same URL pattern as the existing `GET` and `DELETE` in `AnnouncementEndpoints.cs`. Owner/Manager (same authz tier as create, checked live inside `UpdateAsync`). Body: `{title?, body?, scheduledAt?}` (all optional, partial update). Service method `IAnnouncementService.UpdateAsync(userId, announcementId, title, body, scheduledAt, ct)`. Guard: status must be `Queued` (409 `cannot_update` otherwise). If the updated `scheduledAt` is null or in the past, fires `SendAsync` immediately (same pattern as `CreateAsync`). No new entity fields.
**Why:** smallest delta to match the screen — one route + one service method + one integration test. Announcement stats (opens/clicks) are display-only from existing data; no backend change needed for the stats column.

## D-069 · Help & Support — static FAQ only, no backend (2026-07-16)
**Status: ACCEPTED.**

The Recommended Additions screen list includes a "Help & Support" screen (FAQ accordion, category chips, "Chat with Support" button). Adding a live support provider would be speculative scope (D-018 caution, CLAUDE.md §3 non-negotiable #5). No FAQ/support API exists and building one would constitute unfinished scaffolding.

**Chose:** `HelpPage` is Flutter-only: a hardcoded `List<_FaqCategory>` with title/chips/accordion rows. "Chat with Support" opens a `mailto:` or `tel:` deeplink — no SDK, no new provider, no backend call. FAQ content is inline Dart constants (not a separate asset file — a separate file is premature for content that won't be localised yet). When a real support integration (Freshdesk, Intercom, etc.) is chosen, the page is replaced wholesale.
**Why:** a static page satisfies the UX requirement with zero backend risk; a hardcoded-content page is a known quantity that won't break.

## D-070 · Razorpay Flutter SDK — mobile checkout integration (2026-07-16)
**Status: ACCEPTED. IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRES SECURITY REVIEW STOP before writing code.**

The Checkout / Payment Processing / Payment Success / Payment Failed screens require a payment sheet on mobile. The backend already has: `POST /v1/events/{eventId}/orders` (creates order, returns `razorpay_order_id` for paid ticket types via `IPaymentGateway.CreateOrderAsync`), and `POST /v1/webhooks/razorpay` (confirms payment on server via HMAC-verified webhook). The payment gateway mock is already wired; the SDK call is the mobile-side counterpart.

**Chose:** `razorpay_flutter` package (official Razorpay Flutter SDK). Flow: (1) app calls `POST /v1/events/{eventId}/orders` → receives `{razorpay_order_id, amount_paise, ...}`; (2) app opens Razorpay checkout sheet with `razorpay_order_id`; (3) on SDK `onPaymentSuccess` callback, app polls `GET /v1/me/orders` (or the guest order endpoint) until status transitions to `paid` (or `failed`); (4) server confirms independently via webhook — the client never trusts its own payment success event as the source of truth, it only uses it to trigger the status poll. `RAZORPAY_KEY_ID` is a build-time config var (same pattern as `KURX_API_BASE`), never hardcoded.

**Security stop:** Identity Verification, Org KYC, Withdrawal, and this payment checkout flow are all gated — implementation does NOT proceed until the explicit stop in the implementation sequence receives user confirmation.
**Why:** Razorpay is the existing gateway (D-049 wires it server-side); the Flutter SDK is the standard mobile integration path; webhook-is-authority ensures the client can't self-confirm payments even if the SDK callback is tampered with.

## D-071 · Ticket transfers — claimed tickets are unreachable, and the sender keeps the rotated code (2026-07-16)
**Status: FIXED (2026-07-16, user-approved backend change). Tests added. One residual exposure accepted — see below.**

Wiring `transfer_claim_page.dart` to `POST /v1/transfers/claim` (mobile, D-019) surfaced two defects in the shipped backend transfer flow. Both were verified end-to-end against a live API (dev DB), with the organizer, sender and recipient as three separate users so no finding is explained by org-staff access:

`TicketTransferService.ClaimAsync` reassigns `ticket.UserId` to the claimant and rotates `ticket.Code` (`ticket.Code = Guid.NewGuid()` — commented *"Rotate QR — old screenshot is dead"*). It never touches `order.UserId`. But the only listing of a user's tickets, `OrderService.MyTicketsAsync`, filters `db.Orders.Where(o => o.UserId == userId)` — by **order owner**. No endpoint anywhere queries tickets by `ticket.UserId`.

Observed (recipient claimed successfully, HTTP 200, `status: "Claimed"`, code rotated `22052360…` → `ce332e93…`):
1. **The claimant cannot reach the ticket they now own.** Recipient's `GET /v1/orders` returns `[]`. The new code is never returned by the claim response either, so the client has no way to learn it. `GET /v1/tickets/{code}/qr.png` correctly authorizes the claimant (200) — but they cannot discover the code to call it. The ticket is theirs and invisible.
2. **The former owner retains the rotated code** (security). Sender's `GET /v1/orders` still lists the ticket with the **new** code, because the order is still theirs. The QR image endpoint does deny the sender (403), but that is not a barrier: the QR payload *is* the code (`qr.GeneratePng(ticket.Code.ToString())`), so the sender can regenerate the QR from the leaked code, and `POST /v1/gate/{eventId}/scan` authorizes only the *scanner* (org member/assignee) — possession of the code is admission. A sender can therefore transfer a ticket, keep working QR access, and be admitted in the claimant's place; the claimant, who cannot see the ticket at all, is left out. The code rotation is defeated for exactly the party it defends against.

**Chose (fix):** option (b) — a ticket is listed for its **current holder** (`Ticket.UserId`), never the order's buyer. `OrderService.MyTicketsAsync` now selects orders the user bought **or** holds a ticket in, and `BuildOrderViewAsync` takes an optional `viewerUserId` that filters the order's tickets to that holder. The single-order views (create / confirm / guest-token) pass `null` and keep every ticket, since their caller is already the buyer or the guest-token holder. Rejected: (a) reassigning `order.UserId` on claim — the order is the buyer's payment record and must not move; (c) returning the rotated code in the claim response — closes the UX half only and leaves the leak open.

The buyer still sees the order itself (their payment record) with `tickets: []` once every ticket on it has been transferred away. Verified live: sender's `GET /v1/orders` → order present, `"tickets":[]`, no code; claimant's → the order with their ticket and the rotated code.

**Tests (the root cause was their absence — `Kurx.Tests` had zero transfer tests):** `TicketTransferTests.cs`, organizer/sender/recipient as three distinct users so nothing is explained by org-staff access. Both ownership tests were confirmed to **fail against the unfixed code** before the fix landed. They assert: the claim moves the ticket off the sender's list and onto the claimant's; the sender is never served the rotated code by the order list; the rotated code binds to the claimant (old code → `invalid_code` at `gate/scan`, QR image 403 for the former holder / 200 for the claimant, rotated code admits); and the buyer's `guest_access_token` (a bearer credential for the whole order, D-036) is never served on an order surfaced to a claimant. Backend suite **188 → 191 passing, 0 failing**.

**Residual exposure (accepted, follow-up):** surfacing a claimed ticket through `/v1/orders` necessarily surfaces the buyer's order row alongside it, so a claimant now sees that order's `amount_paise`, `razorpay_order_id`, and — for a group order — `join_code`. `guest_access_token` is **not** exposed (null on this path, now asserted). This is strictly smaller than the defect it replaces (double admission + claimant lockout) and is inherent to `/v1/orders` conflating *my purchases* with *my tickets*. The clean resolution is to split ticket listing onto its own `GET /v1/me/tickets` and stop projecting other people's orders at all; that is a follow-up, not done here. Related, also unfixed: `ClaimAsync` does not move `GroupMember.UserId`, so group membership does not follow a transferred group ticket.
**Why it matters:** (1) made transfers useless in-app; (2) made them exploitable.

## D-072 · Transfer claim page has no entry point — the route exists but no user can reach it (2026-07-16)
**Status: RESOLVED for the code-entry path (option (a) shipped, user-approved). Items 2–3 below remain OPEN as a follow-up if transfers ever become link-driven.**

With D-071 fixed, `transfer_claim_page.dart` now claims for real and routes to the claimed ticket by its rotated code. It is still dead code, because nothing navigates to `/transfers/claim`:

1. **No in-app link.** `grep -rn "transfers/claim" mobile/lib` matches only the route declaration in `app_router.dart` and the datasource path. No page links to it.
2. **Deep links are dropped by the splash gate.** Verified live on the emulator: launching with `--route='/transfers/claim?code=TESTCODE1'` lands on **Discover**, not the claim page. `app_router.dart`'s redirect sends any location to `Routes.splash` while `session.status == AuthStatus.unknown`, then — once the session resolves — unconditionally redirects `Routes.splash` → `Routes.events`. The originally-requested location is never preserved. `loginReturnToProvider` does exactly this for the login round-trip; the splash gate has no equivalent.
3. **No external deep link anyway.** `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` has one intent-filter (LAUNCHER); no `VIEW`/scheme/App Links host.

**The intended UX is manual code entry, not a link.** `TicketTransferService.InitiateAsync` sends the recipient a WhatsApp message reading *"Your claim code is: {code}. It expires in 72 hours."* — an 8-char code (`GenerateTransferCode`), no URL. So the recipient is expected to open the app and type the code, which requires a visible affordance the app does not have. (The page already accepts a pre-filled `code` query param, so a future link-based flow still works — but that would need item 2 fixed and a `VIEW` intent-filter added, and the backend would have to send a URL.)

**Options:** (a) a "Claim a transferred ticket" action on `my_tickets_page` — matches the code-in-WhatsApp UX, smallest change, and the page is where a recipient would look; (b) an entry on `profile_page`/settings — more discoverable for a user with no tickets yet, but off the natural path; (c) fix the splash gate to preserve the requested location + add a `VIEW` intent-filter and switch the backend message to a link — a larger change touching backend copy, and out of scope for a mobile task. **(a) is the recommendation**, with (c) as the follow-up if transfers should ever be link-driven.

**Why it matters:** the transfer feature is end-to-end complete on the server and in the client, and still unusable — a recipient has no way to reach the only screen that would let them claim.

**Chose:** (a). `my_tickets_page` gains an app-bar action (`swap_horiz`, tooltip *"Claim a transferred ticket"*) → `context.push('/transfers/claim')`. Always visible regardless of tab or empty state, and it sits where a recipient would look. Items 2 and 3 (splash dropping the requested location; no `VIEW` intent-filter) are untouched and stay open — they only matter if the backend ever sends a URL instead of a code.

**Verified live** (emulator → throwaway `kurx_probe` DB, so the dev DB stayed clean): signed in as a real recipient over OTP, My Tickets → the new action → typed the real 8-char code → *"Ticket claimed. It's yours now."* → replaced onto the ticket detail showing the **rotated** code `4DF67515`. This is the first time the claim screen has been reachable by a user.

**Found while verifying — separate defect, not fixed here:** the ticket QR never renders. `ticket_detail_page.dart` loads it with `Image.network('${AppConfig.apiBase}/v1/tickets/{code}/qr.png')`, which sends no `Authorization` header, but the endpoint is `.RequireAuthorization()` — the probe API logged `GET /v1/tickets/4df67515-…/qr.png responded 401` and the screen showed "QR unavailable". The fix is to fetch the bytes through the shared Dio client (so `auth_interceptor` attaches the token and handles refresh-on-401) and render `Image.memory`, rather than hand a raw token to `Image.network` and bypass the refresh path. Belongs to the C1 `ticket_detail_page` item.

## D-073 · Mobile organizer DTOs were written against an API that doesn't exist — and `guard()` disguised it as "no connection" (2026-07-16)
**Status: FIXED for the org surface. Two known instances remain (listed below).**

Wiring A4 (`create_org_page` → `POST /v1/orgs`) surfaced that the mobile organizer feature was modelled on an imagined API. Every field below was verified against a **live** response, not read off the C#.

**The masking bug (why none of this was visible).** `guard()` caught only `DioException`. A DTO/response mismatch throws a plain `TypeError`, so it sailed past `guard`, past every `on ApiError` handler, and surfaced as an unhandled exception; `ErrorRetry.fromError` then rendered its non-`ApiError` fallback — *"Something went wrong. Please try again."* — under an unconditional `Icons.wifi_off_rounded`. A contract bug was therefore reported to the user as **their** network being down, sending them to fix the wrong thing. This is the user-reported My Tickets symptom, and it hid every defect below.
- `guard()` now converts any non-Dio throw into `ApiError(code: 'response_parse_failed')`, logs it with the endpoint, and rethrows a thrown `ApiError` unchanged.
- `ErrorRetry` picks its icon from the code: wifi-off **only** for `network_error`/`timeout`, a bug glyph for `response_parse_failed`, a generic error otherwise.
- `response_parse_failed` reads *"Kurx sent something this app couldn't read"* — it never blames the connection.

**The contract drift (all verified live):**
- `OrgDto` required a **`created_at` no org endpoint sends**, so parsing *any* non-empty org list threw. The org list only ever "worked" while empty — zero items means `fromJson` never runs, which is why this shipped. It also typed `tier` as `String` (the wire sends `1`), mapped `logo_url`/`org_type`/`my_role`/`description` (server: `logo_key`/`type`/`role`/`bio`), and declared `cover_url`, `kyc_status`, `member_count`, `event_count`, `total_revenue_paise`, `wallet_balance_paise` — **none of which any endpoint returns**, whose zero defaults were rendered as fact ("0 members · 0 events", a ₹0 wallet balance).
- `OrgMemberDto` required an **`id` the endpoint never sends** (members are keyed by `user_id`) and declared an `email` that doesn't exist while missing the `username` that does — so the members list threw, and the org header's Members count was blank.
- Two shapes share `OrgDto`: `GET /v1/orgs` returns `{id, name, slug, logo_key, role}`; `GET|POST /v1/orgs/{id}` adds `bio, links_json, payout_account_status, bank_last4, tier, type, primary_domain, verification_status`. Everything past `name` is now nullable, and the list no longer shows a verification chip it has no data for.
- **`GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/wallet` exists and nothing called it.** `WalletEndpoints` returns the `WalletView` record raw instead of a hand-built object, so — alone in this API — **its keys are camelCase** (`availablePaise`, not `available_paise`). New `WalletDto` spells them as they arrive; `org_wallet_page` now reads the real balance instead of `OrgDto.walletBalancePaise`.
- `create_org_page`'s type dropdown offered `Independent` / `College / University` — neither is an `OrganizationType`, so both would have been rejected `validation_failed`. It now sends the ten real values (`college…other`, D-043), matching `web/lib/api.ts`.

**Fabricated UI removed rather than re-sourced where no endpoint exists:** the `org_detail` cover image (no `cover_url` anywhere), org logos (`logo_key` is a storage key, not a URL, and there is no org-logo presign), and the `org_verification` "PAN Verification" step (driven by the phantom `kyc_status`; `payout_account_status` now drives Bank Account). Counts in the `org_detail` header come from the endpoints that actually serve them (`/members`, `/events`, `/wallet`) and render an em dash until they land — never a confident zero.

**Verified live** (emulator → throwaway `kurx_probe` DB): created "NSRIT College" (`type: college`) → `POST /v1/orgs` 200 → it appears in `/orgs` as **NSRIT College · owner** → opening it shows **Members 1** and **Earned ₹0** from the real endpoints. Before the fix this same path threw on parse and showed a wifi-off "Something went wrong".

**Still broken, same class:** (a) `EventManageDto` — the org header's Events count shows "—" because `/events` doesn't parse; A3 will hit this. (b) Every other unwired organizer DTO is suspect for the same reason and should be pinned against a live payload before its page is trusted. The general lesson: **a DTO is a contract claim; it must be checked against a real response, not against the page that consumes it.**

## D-074 · Event-first architecture — no organizer/owner accounts; org creation is admin-gated via a verification request (2026-07-18)
**Status: ACCEPTED as the target architecture (2026-07-18). Supersedes the Organization-first framing of D-055. ✅ Now fully implemented — the "Implementation status" section below is HISTORICAL.** What it listed as "not yet built" shipped in D-075 (backend) and D-076 (web), and the migration was completed by **[D-267](#)** (organization-first navigation removed from every client), **[D-268](#)** (users own events; the personal-organization concept deleted from the domain) and **[D-269](#)** (one event authorization service). Read this entry for the *model*; read D-267/268/269 for what is actually built.

The product's entry model is **event-first**. There is no "organizer" and no "organization owner" as account types; **every person is a User**. Organizations are institutions a user *represents*, never accounts a user *owns*.

**The model (source of truth):**
- **No Organizer accounts, no Organization accounts, no Organization Owners, no "Become Owner", no standalone "Create Organization" workflow.** Users never create organizations directly.
- Canonical flow: **Login → Create Event → fill event details → "Who are you representing?" → search the *verified* organization registry.**
- **Org exists in the registry** → the user selects it and submits **proof of authority to represent it** (an evidence-backed membership claim, reviewed by an admin — the M6/D-045 machinery).
- **Org does not exist** → the user submits org details + supporting documents (letterhead, authorization proof, registration docs). The platform creates **only an `OrganizationVerificationRequest`** — **not** an `Organization`. The org **does not** exist in the registry and **must not** appear in search until an admin approves it.
- **Admin approval** creates the official `Organization` record, adds it to the searchable registry, and links the requesting user as a **Verified Representative** (never "Owner"). Events attached to a still-pending request are marked *Pending Organization Verification* and proceed through the normal approval flow (D-047) once approved.
- **Personal events** (no institution) need only the creator's own identity — no org, no representation.

**Supersedes (D-055):** D-055 kept an implicit `organizations` row created at event-creation via `POST /v1/orgs` with the user as **Owner**, and let unverified real orgs appear in registry search (only `IsPersonal` excluded). D-074 replaces that: an unapproved submission is a **staged verification request**, never an `Organization`, never searchable; representation is granted by **admin approval**, not by the act of creation; the granted role is **Verified Representative**, not **Owner**. The registry-search / verification substrate / membership-claim / admin-review machinery from M4–M6/M12 (D-043/44/45/51) is reused unchanged — this is an **entry-flow + staging-entity** change, not a rebuild of the trust engine.

**Implementation status (honest — docs must not claim this as shipped):**
- **Shipped today (D-055):** event-first entry exists for zero-org users, but `POST /v1/orgs` still creates a real org immediately and makes the caller **Owner**; unverified orgs are searchable; `OrgRole.Owner` still exists.
- **Not yet built (D-074 target):** the `OrganizationVerificationRequest` staging entity; excluding unapproved orgs from registry search; admin-approval materialization of the org; the **Verified Representative** role replacing organizer-time **Owner**; the "Who are you representing?" step wired into event creation with registry search.
- Until the code lands, documentation describes D-074 as the **target architecture** and flags org-first behaviors (Owner, implicit org creation, standalone create-org) as **legacy / D-055, pending migration**. The terms "Organizer", "Owner", "Become Owner", and "Create Organization (standalone)" are retired from forward-looking docs.

**Why:** forcing organization creation before an event is the wrong entry point — it makes impersonation cheap (anyone can mint an "org") and puts institution administration in front of the actual goal (running an event). Staging unverified institutions as *requests* (invisible until an admin approves) makes the registry trustworthy, keeps "represent, don't own" as the security boundary, and collapses the user's mental model to one role: **User**.

**Verification:** Documentation-only decision (target architecture). No code or tests changed by this entry. Implementation lands under follow-up `D-NNN`(s) with the usual build → test → verify loop; this entry is the spec they build against.

## D-075 · Event-first implementation (backend) — the staging record is a hidden placeholder org, not a parallel table; representation via a new `Representative` role (2026-07-18)
**Status: ACCEPTED. Implements D-074 on the backend. Web followed as D-076; mobile followed in [D-267](#), not "D-077" (that number was taken by the concurrent auth workstream). ⚠️ Two mechanics here were later changed: [D-268](#) removed the user-facing personal-organization concept and made `Event.CreatedBy` the owner, and [D-269](#) replaced the per-service `EventService.CanManage` this entry extended with a single `IEventAuthority`.**

D-074 fixed the target ("no owners; an unverified institution is a staged request an admin approves"). D-075 is *how* the backend realizes it. The load-bearing constraint is that **`Event.OrgId` is a non-null enforced FK** to `organizations` (`KurxDbContext` `b.Entity<Event>() … HasForeignKey(x => x.OrgId)`), and D-055 rejected making it nullable (large ripple). A pending event therefore needs a real `organizations` row to point at.

**Decision — reuse the `Organization` row + the M5 verification substrate as the staging record; do not add a parallel `OrganizationVerificationRequest` table.** A new-institution submission creates a **lean, hidden placeholder org**:
- `VerificationStatus = PendingReview`, `IsPersonal = false`, `CanonicalOrgId = self`, `NormalizedName` set. **No Owner membership, no wallet, no payout schedule** (those are minted at approval, when money can actually move).
- The submitter gets a **pending `Representative` membership** (`Membership { Role = Representative, IsVerified = false }`) so they can create/edit their own pending event immediately, while carrying **zero trust capability** (M7 `CanRepresentOrg` reads `IsVerified`, which is still false).
- Evidence goes to the existing polymorphic `verification_documents` (`SubjectType = Organization`); review goes to `verification_reviews`. The admin queue (`OrgVerificationService.ListPendingAsync`) already lists `PendingReview` orgs — the placeholder appears there for free.

**Why not a parallel `OrganizationVerificationRequest` table (the D-074 wording):** it would duplicate every column the org row already has (name/type/legal/domain/normalized/reviewer/notes) **and** still require a placeholder org for the non-null `Event.OrgId` FK — two rows to keep in sync for zero behavioural gain. The placeholder org, invisible to search and to the public profile and carrying no Owner, is *observationally* "not in the registry until an admin approves it" — which is exactly what D-074 requires. Reuse over duplication (ponytail).

**The five deltas (no DB migration — enums are stored as text with no CHECK constraint, and no new tables/columns are introduced):**
1. `OrgRole` gains **`Representative`** (a verified, manage-capable role that is *not* Owner). `EventService.CanManage` accepts it.
2. **Submit** — `OrgService.SubmitRepresentationRequestAsync` + `POST /v1/orgs/representation-requests` creates the hidden placeholder + pending Representative + evidence. `POST /v1/orgs` is now **personal-org-only** (institutions must go through the request); non-personal self-creation returns `use_representation_request`.
3. **Registry is Verified-only** — `OrganizationRegistryService.SearchAsync` discriminator changes from `!IsPersonal` to `VerificationStatus == Verified`; `OrgService.GetPublicAsync` returns `not_found` for any non-Verified org (no existence leak of a staged placeholder, D-018/D-047 404-not-403).
4. **Approval materializes** — `OrgVerificationService.ReviewAsync` "approve" branch additionally verifies the submitter's pending Representative membership (`IsVerified = true`) and seeds the wallet + tier-1 payout schedule if missing. Legacy Owner-submitted orgs are unaffected (no pending Representative, wallet already present).
5. **Pending events wait** — `EventService.TransitionAsync` blocks `publish` (free *or* paid) when the event's org is non-personal and not `Verified`, returning `pending_org_verification`. Personal orgs skip the gate. "Pending Organization Verification" is **derived live** from the org's status — no `EventStatus` value, no column, and events auto-advance the instant the org verifies.

**Trust boundary preserved:** representation that grants capability (publish/sell, `CanRepresentOrg`) is switched on only by admin approval (`IsVerified` + org `Verified`), read live per request (M7/D-046, D-015). The pre-approval Representative seat grants only draft-management of the submitter's own not-yet-publishable event.

**Consequence accepted:** a *rejected* submission leaves a `Rejected` placeholder org row (soft state, excluded from search and public profile, no Owner) rather than no row at all — the same way M5-rejected orgs already persist. Acceptable; it keeps the FK and the audit trail intact.

**Verification:** built clean (`dotnet build`, Api under `-warnaserror`, 0/0) and the full suite is green against real `kurx_test` — **233/233** (was 230; +3 new `EventFirstTests`, the rest of the suite migrated off the retired self-mint fixture onto request→approve / seeded-verified fixtures). New coverage: request stages a hidden/unsearchable/no-public-profile org with a *pending* Representative (zero capability); direct institution create returns `use_representation_request` while personal still works; a pending org's event is blocked from publishing (`pending_org_verification`) until admin approval, which materializes the org into the registry, verifies the representative (`can_represent_org` flips true), and lets the event publish. **Security review done** (CLAUDE.md §10): 404-not-403 preserved (search + public profile Verified-only, no existence leak of staged orgs); representation grants capability only via admin approval read live (M7/D-015), never by the act of submitting; blacklist enforced at submit. **One finding fixed:** domain global-uniqueness (D-043) was only enforced at submit against verified orgs, so two requests could stage the same domain pre-approval — `ReviewAsync` now hard-dedups domain at approval too (mirrors the existing name-dedup). Local run note: the Windows test host's AppControl (0x800711C7) intermittently blocks freshly-built assemblies; CI is the authority, and a full green run was captured locally here.

## D-076 · Event-first web — Create-Event entry with a "who are you representing?" registry step; representation evidence uploaded via a user-scoped presign (2026-07-18)
**Status: ACCEPTED. Wires the [D-075](#) backend into `web/`. ⚠️ Its navigation is SUPERSEDED by [D-267](#)** — the organizer dashboard, the `kurx_org` "current organization" cookie and its switcher, `/host/organizations` and the standalone create-org UI described below are all removed; Workspace is now the caller's own event list and Representing is a step inside the create form. Mobile followed in D-267, not "D-077" (that number went to the concurrent auth workstream).

The web organizer flow is migrated from the D-055 "create an org (become Owner) then make an event" path to the event-first model. Create Event is the primary entry (dashboard nav reordered, org management demoted to last); when the caller has no org it offers **Just me** (personal, unchanged) or **On behalf of an organization** → a **"who are you representing?"** step that searches the *verified* registry (`GET /v1/orgs/search`) and either lets the caller **request access** to an existing verified org (the M6 membership-claim form, reused) or **register a new one** (a representation request). The standalone create-org UI (`/host/organizations/new`) and `create-org-form.tsx` now **submit a representation request** (`POST /v1/orgs/representation-requests`) instead of `POST /v1/orgs`; proof of affiliation is now **required** (D-074). The admin approval UI (`/host/admin/verifications`) needed **no change** — placeholder orgs are `PendingReview` orgs that already appear in its queue and are approved via the same `/v1/admin/orgs/{id}/verification/review` endpoint.

**One backend addition (the ambiguous call):** representation-request evidence has to be uploaded *before the org exists*, but every existing presign is org-scoped (`/v1/orgs/{orgId}/media/presign`, `…/membership-claims/media/presign`). Added a **user-scoped** presign `POST /v1/orgs/representation-requests/media/presign` (`IMediaService.PresignRepresentationDocAsync`, keyed `representation-requests/{userId}/*`, no org, no role check — any authenticated user may file a request). The web presigns → PUTs the file → submits the request with the returned `storageKey`, which `SubmitRepresentationRequestAsync` records on the placeholder org's `verification_documents`.

The underlying endpoints are integration-tested under D-075. Full authenticated click-through (search → claim/register → draft event) needs a running API + logged-in session and is the remaining manual browser check. **Not committed.**

## D-077 · Authentication re-architecture — Trusted Device Authentication platform; ADRs ratified; AM0 substrate (2026-07-18)
**Status: ACCEPTED (design + ADRs). AM0 substrate implemented, CI-verification pending.** Full spec: `docs/history/architecture/KURX_AUTH_REARCHITECTURE_DOSSIER.md` (this decision is the index; the dossier is the detail).

The current auth model is a single factor — phone-OTP → bearer JWT(1h) + bearer opaque refresh(30d, rotate-on-use, reuse-revokes-all). It is being re-architected into a **Trusted Device Authentication** platform: device-bound public-key credentials (Keystore/Enclave), FCM push-approval login (challenge-response, no OTP on trusted-device login), WebAuthn/passkeys (`fido2-net-lib` v4), OTP demoted to bootstrap/recovery only, step-up for high-risk actions, and true E.164 global phone. Additive and backward-compatible: the OTP login path is preserved behind the `AUTH_TRUSTED_DEVICE` flag until clients migrate.

**Ratified ADRs (mandatory, owner-approved):** two credential rails (custom device-key push-approval first, then WebAuthn); refresh-reuse revokes the **session family** + `security_event` + alert (tightens D-009/D-014 revoke-all — security-reviewed at AM5); standalone auth module with separated services (AM11); explicit device-lifecycle FSM (AM12); **UUID v7 for new auth entities** (`Guid.CreateVersion7()`, **supersedes D-006's Guid-v4 for these tables only** — existing `users`/`refresh_tokens` PKs stay v4, not rewritten); **Redis mandatory** for challenge/OTP/replay/rate-limit/lock/session state (fail-closed in prod when the flag is on — changes today's graceful-skip, AM14); transactional Outbox for security-critical events (AM16); AWS Secrets Manager + KMS + full AWS IaC as the final module (AM18/19/21); adaptive risk engine extending `IFraudService` (AM22); a closing OWASP-ASVS/STRIDE security-review gate (AM23). Modules AM0–AM10 run in dependency order, each gated on per-module design approval before code.

**AM0 (this slice) — substrate only, inert until `AUTH_TRUSTED_DEVICE=1`:** 8 new tables (`trusted_devices` [lifecycle FSM], `device_credentials`, `auth_challenges`, `auth_sessions`, `security_events`, `recovery_codes`, `otp_codes`, `outbox_messages`) + 2 nullable columns on `refresh_tokens` (`SessionId` FK→`auth_sessions` SetNull, `PoPKeyThumbprint`). Purely additive, zero backfill, zero-downtime. **Deliberate scope note:** the AM11 service/provider *interfaces* were **not** created in AM0 — an interface with no implementation and no caller is exactly the speculative-abstraction smell `CLAUDE.md` §5 forbids; each service interface is born with its first real method + impl in its owning module (AM1+). Module boundaries are honored by the `Kurx.Infrastructure/Auth/**` namespace as services land, not by empty stubs.

**Files:** `Domain/Entities/AuthIdentity.cs` (new), `Domain/Enums/Enums.cs`, `Domain/Entities/Users.cs` (RefreshToken +2 cols), `Infrastructure/Persistence/KurxDbContext.cs`, `Infrastructure/Migrations/20260718000000_AddAuthSubstrate.cs` (hand-authored, `[Migration]`-discovered like D-060/A7), `Infrastructure/Migrations/KurxDbContextModelSnapshot.cs` (hand-synced), `.env.example`.

**Verification:** `dotnet build backend/Kurx.sln` **0 warnings / 0 errors** (CI builds Api with `-warnaserror`). `dotnet ef` + the test host are AppControl-blocked on the Windows dev host (0x800711C7), so verification was done by **rebuilding the backend Docker image (Linux) and booting it against the compose Postgres 17** — `MigrateAsync` applied `20260718000000_AddAuthSubstrate` cleanly ("Database migrations applied; connectivity confirmed"), the container is **healthy** (so the EF model validated at runtime), and a direct `psql` inspection confirmed all 8 tables, the 2 nullable `refresh_tokens` columns, the 4 partial-filter indexes (incl. enum-as-text `WHERE "Status" = 'Pending'`), and the FK delete rules (cascade vs. SET NULL) exactly as designed. The **full integration test suite** still runs on **CI** to confirm no regression in existing flows. **Auth/PII change → mandatory security review owed before merge** (`CLAUDE.md` §10); the closing ASVS/STRIDE gate is AM23. **Not committed.**

## D-078 · AM1 — OTP platform + `ISmsProvider` (AWS SNS / India DLT) + E.164 (2026-07-18)
**Status: ACCEPTED. Implemented, Docker-verified (boots healthy).** Additive; runs alongside the legacy `AuthService` OTP path (no cutover until client migration, AM9).

Builds the hardened OTP platform (ADR-A4) and the SMS provider seam (ADR-A5), both mandated. **`ISmsProvider`** (`Application/Abstractions/Providers.cs`) is distinct from the existing `IWhatsAppSender`, with `ConsoleSmsProvider` (dev, zero-cred) and **`SnsSmsProvider`** (real AWS SNS — `AWSSDK.SimpleNotificationService`, same 4.0.100.2 family already used for S3/SES). India DLT compliance rides SNS message attributes `AWS.MM.SMS.EntityId` / `AWS.MM.SMS.TemplateId` + `AWS.SNS.SMS.SenderID`, all from config; credentials from the default AWS chain (never hard-coded). Provider chosen by `SMS_PROVIDER` (console|sns), same env-flag shape as push. **`IOtpService`/`OtpService`** issues/verifies codes on the new `otp_codes` table: CSPRNG 6-digit, **HMAC-SHA256 peppered** hash (`OTP_PEPPER`, `PepperVersion` for rotation — fixes D-005/D-012's unsalted SHA-256), single-use, 5-min TTL, 5-attempt cap, 30s resend cooldown + 3/dest/10min (durable in Postgres, D-005 rationale), delivery routed per channel (SMS/WhatsApp/email), each issue+verify audited to `security_events`. Destinations are E.164 (new `PhoneNumbers.TryToE164`, ADR-A6) or lowercased email.

**Deliberate deferrals (documented, not silent):** (1) **libphonenumber region-aware parsing** is deferred to AM9 (where clients pass a region) — AM1 strict-accepts already-E.164 input, which is enough for the service layer; (2) **Redis velocity/replay layer** (ADR-AM14) fronts the durable Postgres limits in AM8; (3) the legacy phone-OTP login endpoints are **untouched** — cutting `/v1/auth/*` over to `IOtpService` happens with the client migration (AM9), preserving backward compat.

**⚠ Going live still needs owner-supplied external inputs** (code is dormant-but-ready): AWS SNS production SMS access + **India DLT registration** (Entity ID + Template IDs via a TRAI operator), or the numbers stay unroutable. Until `SMS_PROVIDER=sns` + creds, delivery is the console provider.
