## D-183 · Event Architecture V3 — Phase 15: template activation, snapshot-at-creation & generated workspace (§13.1/§20) (2026-07-24)

**Context.** The `EventTemplate` scaffold shipped inert (`DefaultSectionsJson`, never enforced). Phase 15 activates
it into the authoritative Template system of §13.1 under the [D-132](DECISIONS.md) constitutional law (declarative,
never a rule engine), and adds the §20 generated organiser workspace — backend only, no wizard/UI, no AI.

**Status: APPROVED / COMPLETE (2026-07-24).** Engineering-reviewed (Option B) → review-fixed (H1/H2/M1/M2/M3 + M5
tests) → focused re-verification (Option A) → approved. Approved decisions:
- ✓ **Declarative template model** — config only; never dates/slug/status/inventory/pools/financials (under D-132).
- ✓ **Snapshot presets + defaults at creation** — capability preset + timezone applied, `created_from_template_version` recorded; the event is thereafter independent of the template.
- ✓ **Backend-generated workspace** — grouped from `workspace_tab` + the capability registry; never hand-written per Kind; no wizard/UI.
- ✓ **Read-only publish-checklist projection** — projects the Phase-14 §14.2 gates through the same `TransitionGateAsync`; a `GET /workspace` performs no writes.
- ✓ **Manual template CRUD** — create / update (Draft only) / publish / version / archive / clone / delete.
- ✓ **Closed capability-registry validation** — unknown/disabled/invalid rejected, never repaired; the same pipeline a future AI generator would reuse.
- ✓ **No AI generation in Phase 15** — the validation pipeline is AI-ready, but no LLM/generator is built.
- ⏳ **Deferred (architectural confirmation owed):** materialising declarative defaults **beyond timezone** (branding, default-audience, form-fields, agenda, stages, participant roles) onto the event at creation is intentionally **not** implemented (M4) — those declarations are carried, versioned, and snapshot-recorded, and their materialisation awaits a future architectural decision.

**Decisions.**
1. **Scoped + versioned, additive over the inert row.** A template is `Scope` (PLATFORM|ORG|UNIT|PERSONAL,
   most-specific-wins) + a version family: every version is a row sharing `RootTemplateId` (= the v1 id, the stable
   identity events reference); a Published version is immutable; the legacy fields are retained. The old unique-Slug
   index is relaxed to non-unique (a family shares its slug); the new unique key is `(RootTemplateId, Version)`. The
   migration backfills every pre-existing row to `root = self, v1, Published, Platform`(system)/`Org`(custom).
2. **Declarative config only, validated against the closed registry — one pipeline.** `config_json` carries a
   capability preset + defaults (timezone/branding/audience/form-fields/agenda/stages/roles); it **never** carries
   dates/slug/status/inventory/pools/financials. Every write runs `ValidateConfigAsync`: unknown capability slug →
   `unknown_capability`, a referenced-as-disabled (state Off) capability → `capability_disabled`, a bad state →
   `invalid_capability_state`, a template-declared `workspace_tab` (registry-governed) → `invalid_workspace_declaration`,
   bad JSON → `invalid_config_json`. Reject, never repair — the exact door a future AI generator submits a draft
   through (no AI is built this phase).
3. **Snapshot-applied at creation.** Creating an event with `templateId` (the family root — usable only if the
   family has a Published version) overlays the latest Published version's capability preset onto the just-materialised
   `event_capabilities`, applies declarative defaults (timezone, only when the organiser left the platform default),
   and records `events.created_from_template_version`. So "why do two events from one template differ" is answerable
   and a later template edit never mutates an existing event. No inventory/financial/registration rows are ever
   auto-created. **Known boundary:** `GetForEventAsync` still recomputes the effective set from Kind (per-event
   `event_capabilities` overrides are a documented later-phase merge in `CapabilityService`), so a template's overlaid
   capability is persisted now but surfaces in the resolver/workspace only once that merge lands; a re-materialise on
   a Kind change currently rewrites the overlay — same deferred merge work, not fixed here.
4. **Workspace + publish checklist are generated projections, never second sources of truth.**
   `GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/events/{eventId}/workspace` (Owner/Manager/Representative; non-member → 404) groups the
   event's non-Off capabilities by `workspace_tab` (reusing `ICapabilityService.GetForEventAsync`) and attaches a
   live publish checklist that, for each forward §14.1 action valid from the current status, reports the result of
   the **same** `EventService.TransitionGateAsync` the real transition runs (the five §14.2 gates). Nothing is
   duplicated or restated.
5. **Clone lands in the caller's own space.** `POST /{id}/clone` copies any visible template into a **new** family
   (fresh root, v1 Draft) that is Personal for a normal user / Platform for an admin — you may copy what you can see
   without writing into someone else's org/unit.

**Verification (initial implementation, 2026-07-24, container, real Postgres).** Build `-warnaserror` 0/0; backend
**737 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed** (724 → 737: +13 Phase-15 tests). Web/Admin/Flutter untouched (backend-only).
Additive/reversible migration `20260724184540_AddTemplateActivation`.

**Engineering-review fixes (OPTION B → applied → focused re-verification Option A → APPROVED).** H1 —
`NewVersionAsync` catches the `(RootTemplateId, Version)` unique-index race and returns `draft_exists` (409) instead of
a 500 (the DB constraint stays authoritative). H2 — the workspace publish checklist is now a pure read: a new
`IApprovalService.IsCompleteAsync` evaluates the SAME completeness rule via a shared read-only
`EvaluateCompletenessAsync` core, and `TransitionGateAsync` gained a `readOnly` flag the checklist passes — a
`GET /workspace` no longer materialises `approval_requests`/`step_decisions`. M1 — `ApplyToEventAsync` skips any
capability not available in the event's mode (§11.3, `CapabilityService.AvailableModes` authoritative) so a
mode-forbidden state can't be persisted. M2 — `CloneAsync` enforces a view check (Platform=all · Personal=owner ·
Org/Unit=member), returning `not_found` otherwise (no cross-tenant/personal disclosure). M3 — event insert + capability
materialization + template snapshot run in one `BeginTransactionAsync`, so a failed apply rolls the whole event back
(no orphan). **M4 (declarative-default materialization) is deliberately NOT changed — timezone-only application of
declarative defaults stays as-is, awaiting architectural confirmation** of whether branding/default-audience/form-fields/
agenda/stages/roles should also be materialised onto the event at creation.

**Final verification (approved, 2026-07-24, container, real Postgres).** Release build `-warnaserror` **0 warnings /
0 errors**; **744 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed** (724 → 737 initial → **744** after the fix round; +20
`TemplateActivationTests` including the M5 parallel-version-race, parallel-publish, scope-precedence,
snapshot-independence, deletion, and archival tests). No regressions; foundations (money path, lifecycle, approval,
capability authority) intact. Phase 15 **APPROVED**.

## D-132 · Templates are declarative configuration, never a rule engine — Event System V3 constitutional law (2026-07-22)

**Context.** V3 ([D-131](DECISIONS.md)) establishes that Kinds and Templates are configuration and Capabilities
are the implementation (§2, §11), and §12.3 forbids EAV (any JSONB key that is filtered/sorted/aggregated
becomes a typed column). What §0–§22 did not state *explicitly* is the adjacent boundary the philosophy
companion (`docs/architecture/EVENT_OS_PHILOSOPHY.md`, Law 14) identified as the architecture's most likely
long-term erosion at multi-team scale: configuration slowly admitting conditional behaviour until a Template
config is a bad embedded programming language. This ratifies that boundary as an explicit V3 law.

**Decision.** A constitutional law of the Event System V3 architecture:
1. **Templates remain declarative** — a Template is a selection of capabilities and their configuration
   (values, references, form fields, defaults), nothing more.
2. **Templates never contain imperative logic** — no conditionals, computation, control flow, or expressions
   that evaluate at runtime.
3. **Templates never become a rule engine** — a config schema may not grow constructs that encode branching
   behaviour.
4. **Business behaviour belongs only inside capabilities/modules** — the ~40 platform capabilities (§11) are
   the sole home of logic; a Template selects and configures them, it never re-implements them.
5. **Configuration is data, not code** — a value that must decide behaviour conditionally is a capability, not
   a Template field.

Enforced at review, and by lint where mechanizable (the same posture as §12.3's promotion rule).

**Amendment mechanism.** Per V3's own amendment rule (banner), §0–§22 are never edited inline. This law is
surfaced in V3 under a new **Constitutional Amendments** section appended after §22 (CA-1), citing this
decision; V3's §0–§22 are unchanged.

**Consequences.** `EVENT_OS_PHILOSOPHY.md` Law 14 now references this decision rather than proposing it. No
code, schema, or API change. `EVENT_ARCHITECTURE_V3.md` remains the single source of truth and implementation
contract. Numbering: within the V3 band (D-130…D-180) reserved by D-131.

## D-185 · Admin console premium redesign — promote web's local UI primitives into `@kurx/ui`, dependency-free charts, honest-data-only dashboard (2026-07-27)

**Context.** The admin console (`admin/`) read as a plain internal CRUD tool next to `web/`, despite
already sharing design tokens and core primitives (`Button`, `Card`, `Badge`, `Dialog`, `DataTable`,
`StatCard`, …) through `@kurx/ui`. Investigation found the actual gap was twofold: (1) `web` had grown
eight local-only UI components (`Chip`, `Avatar`, `Switch`, `Tabs`, `SectionHeader`, `Sheet`, `Toast`,
`MotionPanel`, plus a `Field`/`Input`/`Textarea`/`Select` set) that were never promoted to the shared
package, so admin had no equivalent and hand-rolled the same input `className` string across half a
dozen files; (2) roughly half of admin's list screens (Users, Events, Reports, Blacklist, Staff, Audit)
predated the newer `DataTable`-based pattern the other half (Categories, Certificates, Speakers,
Sponsors, Stages) already used well, and were still ad hoc `Card` stacks with raw colored `<span>`
pills. A full redesign was requested (dashboard, nav, tables, forms, empty/loading states, micro-
interactions) with the explicit constraints of zero functional/route/permission/backend-contract
changes.

**Decision.**
1. Promote `web`'s eight local-only `components/ui/*` primitives plus `field.tsx`
   (`Field`/`Input`/`Textarea`/`Select`) into `@kurx/ui` (`packages/ui/src/`), following the same
   shim/single-source pattern already used for `Card`/`Button`/`Badge`/`EmptyState`. This is additive
   only — new files and new `index.ts` export lines; no existing export's behavior changes, so `web` is
   unaffected. `web`'s own local copies are left as-is (out of scope; not touched per "don't touch what
   isn't asked").
2. Add one new dependency-free chart primitive to `@kurx/ui` — `Sparkline` (inline SVG line/area) and
   `MiniBars` (promoted and restyled from the ad hoc bar chart that used to live inline in
   `admin/app/(console)/analytics/page.tsx`) — instead of adding a charting library. No chart library
   exists anywhere in the monorepo, and a day-count trend line / bar strip is a legitimate few-line SVG
   job, not a dependency's job (non-negotiable #5: no unrequested dependency changes).
3. The redesigned dashboard's activity feed, mini charts, and "needs review" preview are built only
   from endpoints already called elsewhere in admin (`getDashboardSummary`, `getAnalytics`, `listAudit`,
   `listPendingOrgVerifications`, `listPendingEvents`) — no new API surface. Two requested widgets have
   no backing endpoint (a platform revenue summary — the Finance module is unbuilt; a fraud *alert feed*
   — `/risk` is record-only with no list endpoint per `admin/STATUS.md`) and render as explicitly
   labeled placeholders with a quick-action link, never fabricated numbers.
4. `getDashboardSummary` is wrapped in React's `cache()` (`admin/lib/api.ts`) so the console layout
   (sidebar queue-count badges) and the dashboard page — both server components on the same request —
   share one network call instead of two.

**Consequences.** Admin's list screens (Users, Events, Reports, Blacklist, Staff, Audit, the
verification queue, user-detail audit trail) now use `DataTable`/`Badge`/`Avatar` consistently, matching
the pattern the newer screens already established. The sidebar gains collapsible groups (persisted to
`localStorage`), a left accent-bar active indicator, and count badges sourced only from real
`DashboardSummary` fields (Reports has no summary-backed count and deliberately gets none). The topbar
gains a `Cmd/Ctrl+K` nav palette (client-side filter over `NAV`, no new API) and breadcrumbs. A new
admin-local `components/layout/page-header.tsx` replaces the `<header><p kicker/><h1/><p desc/></header>`
block that was copy-pasted at the top of every page file. Row-action outcomes (suspend/ban, feature/
publish, resolve/dismiss, grant/revoke, blacklist add/remove, broadcast send) now surface through a
shared `ToastProvider` wrapping the console shell, in addition to (not instead of) existing inline
validation errors. No route, permission, server-action, or backend-contract change. Pre-auth surfaces
(`/login`, `/forbidden`, `/reset`, `/dev-login`) and `security-center.tsx` were deliberately left
untouched — already visually consistent with the target bar and auth-sensitive enough that a
no-op is the correct call outside a dedicated security review.

## D-186 · Admin Event Management workspace — moderation overrides as orthogonal booleans, admin reuses org-scoped endpoints via the existing `kurx_admin` bypass, no new real-time system (2026-07-28)

**Context.** Following the Live Events Monitoring audit, the user asked for a full Admin Event
Management module: one tabbed workspace (Upcoming/Live/Completed/Draft/Under Review/Cancelled/
Archived/All) over every event platform-wide, a 9-tab detail workspace per event (Overview,
Registrations, Tickets, Attendees, Finance, Organizer, Moderation, Media, Timeline), new
moderation actions (suspend/hide/archive/soft-delete/message/warn), and real SignalR wiring —
built strictly by reusing existing services/endpoints/DTOs, never duplicating backend logic.

Investigation found the single fact the whole feature turns on: `IsAdmin(principal)`
(`kurx_admin` claim, live-populated only for `PlatformRole.SuperAdmin` —
`PlatformRoleClaimsTransformation.cs`) is already threaded through nearly every org-scoped
service (`EventService.ListForOrgAsync/GetAnalyticsAsync`, `ITicketTypeService`,
`IInventoryService.GetForEventAsync`) as a membership-check bypass, and those routes only require
"authenticated" at the endpoint level (`RequireAuthorization()`, no named policy) — the service
layer does the real gating. So a SuperAdmin admin session can already call
`GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/events/{eventId}/analytics|inventory|ticket-types|attendees` for **any**
org, today, with zero new code. The only org-scoped service with **no** admin bypass anywhere was
`IWalletService` — the one genuine gap, fixed the same way every other service already handles it.

**Decisions.**
1. **Suspend/hide are new orthogonal booleans on `Event` (`IsSuspended`, `IsHidden`), not new
   `EventStatus` values.** `EventStatusWorkflow`'s transition table is a closed, deliberately
   audited set ("only the actions/transitions listed here are valid"); suspend/hide are admin
   *overrides* orthogonal to that content lifecycle, exactly the shape `IsFeatured` already is.
   A suspended/hidden event keeps reporting its real status; only public visibility is gated
   (`EventService.CanViewAsync`, and `SearchIndexService.ProjectAsync` excludes it from the
   discovery index). One small additive migration (`AddEventModerationOverrides`/
   `AddEventModerationFlags`): `IsSuspended`, `SuspendedReason`, `IsHidden`, `HiddenReason`.
2. **The user's requested status list's "Approved" does not exist as a distinct state — it's
   `Published`.** The event-approval queue's `publish` action *is* the approval decision
   (already documented in `AdminEventEndpoints.cs`). The admin UI labels the real enum value.
3. **Admin "Delete Event (soft delete)" reuses `IEventService.DeleteDraftAsync` as-is —
   Draft-only.** That method is deliberately scoped to Draft because nothing has happened yet
   (no orders, no tickets). Extending soft-delete to a published/live event with sold tickets is
   a separate, materially riskier decision (refunds? ticket invalidation?) this pass did not
   make; the admin action is disabled for any non-Draft event.
4. **"Message organizer"/"issue warning" are composition, not new entities.**
   `IEventService.NotifyOrganizerAsync` resolves `Event.CreatedBy` (not on the public
   `EventDetail` DTO) → calls the existing `INotificationService.NotifyAsync` → writes an
   `IAuditWriter` entry with a distinct `Action` string. No new table; the Moderation and
   Timeline tabs read this back from the audit log, not a bespoke "warnings" list.
5. **`IWalletService.GetWalletAsync`/`GetLedgerAsync` gained an `isAdmin` parameter** — the same
   one-parameter shape every other org-scoped service already has, applied where it had never
   been wired. `InitiateWithdrawalAsync` deliberately did **not** gain an admin bypass — viewing
   a wallet is a much smaller decision than moving money on an org's behalf.
6. **`IFraudService.GetRiskScoreAsync` (implemented, never called by any endpoint) is now wired**
   via a new single-subject route and a new `GetRiskScoresBatchAsync` (one grouped `SUM`, not N
   sequential calls) for the event list's "Fraud Alerts" column.
7. **Real-time reuses `ScanHub`/`SalesHub` exactly as they already exist** — `BroadcastScanAsync`
   is now called from `GateEntryService.ScanAsync` after a successful check-in;
   `BroadcastSaleAsync`/`BroadcastAnalyticsAsync` are now called from `OrderService` after both
   the free-order and paid-order-capture transaction commits. No new hub, no new broadcast
   method. Both hubs' `JoinEvent`/`JoinOrg` group-join now also accepts the `kurx_admin` bypass
   (previously org-membership-only), so a SuperAdmin session can watch any event's/org's live
   feed. Broadcasts are best-effort (`try/catch`, fire-and-forget after commit) — a hub outage
   must never fail a check-in or a sale.
8. **No admin org list/detail endpoint was added.** The Organizer tab is reached only from an
   already-open event (its `org_id` is already known), and composes `listOrgEventsAsAdmin` +
   the org's wallet + its risk score — genuinely new "browse all organizations" admin tooling
   (STATUS.md §5.4's long-standing gap) is out of scope for this pass.
9. **Real-time scope is the open event workspace, not the list.** `ScanHub`/`SalesHub` are
   group-per-event/group-per-org by design — that shape fits one open detail view, not N
   simultaneous subscriptions from a list page; the list does not attempt live-updating rows.

**Consequences.** Every new admin capability composes an already-existing service/endpoint/DTO;
the only genuinely new backend surface is the moderation-override actions (suspend/hide/message/
warn) and the two small extensions (Wallet admin bypass, Fraud batch scoring) — everything else
(analytics, inventory, ticket types, attendees, wallet reads, org event lists) is the admin
frontend calling the exact same routes `web/lib/api.ts` already calls, using the SuperAdmin
session's own `kurx_admin` claim. Several requested fields (per-attendee email/payment-status/
certificate-status, a distinct platform-fee/net-revenue split, org-level KYC/devices/recent-logins
for another user, Approved/Pending/Waitlist as distinct registration counts, a registration
time-series graph) are not modeled anywhere in this backend today and were rendered honestly as
absent rather than fabricated — each is a real, separate follow-up, not silently invented data.

## D-187 · Admin event list — real pagination, replacing a silent 100-row cap (2026-07-28)

**Context.** `IEventService.ListForAdminAsync` (D-186) had no `Page` parameter and hard-clamped its
SQL query itself to `Math.Clamp(filter.Limit, 1, 100)` rows — a platform with more than 100 events
could never reach row 101 no matter what the caller asked for; every request silently returned the
newest ≤100 and nothing else, with no error and no indication anything was missing.

**Decision.** `AdminEventListFilter` gains `Page` (default 1); `ListForAdminAsync` returns
`(Items, Total)` instead of a bare list; `GET /v1/admin/events` returns `{items, total}` instead of
a bare JSON array (the one intentionally-breaking response-shape change in this pair of decisions —
every caller, including 5 admin pages that called this endpoint indirectly via a shared helper, was
updated in the same change). Two query paths: when every active filter and the sort key are plain
`Event`/`Organization` columns (the common case), pagination and the total count are done entirely
in SQL — correct at any scale. When sorting/filtering by a stats-derived key (revenue/registrations/
attendance, computed via the shared `EventStatsAsync` aggregate, not a stored column), a bounded
2000-row in-memory candidate window is used (was 500) — a documented, pre-existing trade-off, not a
new one; computing revenue for literally every event on every request doesn't scale, and this
already-standing constraint just moved with the rest of the pagination fix.

**A genuine EF Core bug was found and fixed while restoring test coverage for this**: ordering
applied *after* `.Select(x => new AdminEventRow(...))` (a record projection) could not be translated
to SQL — `OrderBy` on a property of a freshly-constructed record forces EF to either push the
order-by past the projection or fail, and it failed at runtime with "could not be translated," not
at compile time. The fix is the standard, safe shape: order → paginate → project, always applied to
the raw joined entity, project last. This is exactly the class of bug only a real integration test
against a real database can catch — confirmed by triaging a live test failure, not by inspection.

**Consequences.** No schema change. `admin/lib/api.ts`'s `listAdminEvents` and every caller updated
to destructure `{ items, total }`. Full pagination UI (page controls, "N of M events") is not built
this pass — the API is ready for it; tracked as a follow-up.

## D-188 · Platform Taxonomy Management — Audience/Category/Type becomes fully admin-manageable, `EventTaxonomySeeder` becomes a bootstrap-only seed, `CategoryCapabilityDefault` is a designed-but-unwired bridge off the fragile `KindSlug` mapping (2026-07-28)

**Context.** A taxonomy audit (this session) found `event_categories` (3 Audiences → 13
Categories → 145 Types, 161 rows total) compiled into `EventTaxonomySeeder.cs` and only
insert-repaired on every boot — no category/type could be added, renamed, or retired without a
code change and a deploy. The user decided this must become a normal Admin Console feature, with
the explicit long-term framing: not a CRUD page, but the start of "the platform configuration
layer for Create Event" — and went through three rounds of architecture review before approving
implementation (captured in full in the session's plan file; summarized here as the decisions
that actually shipped).

**Decisions.**
1. **Lifecycle (`Status`: Active/Disabled/Archived) and Visibility (`IsVisible`) are two separate
   fields, not one.** `Status = Active` + `IsVisible = false` is valid and meaningful — a node
   keeps functioning for historical events but is hidden from new-event pickers without being
   disabled. The one method that decides "usable for a new event right now"
   (`CategoryService.IsSelectableForNewEvents`) is centralized so a future `ActiveFrom`/`ActiveUntil`
   pair only needs to change one place, not every call site.
2. **Slugs are permanently immutable after creation, for every level, with no admin-facing
   "change slug" action.** `Event.CategoryId`/`TypeId`/`AudienceLevelId` are `Guid` FKs to
   `EventCategory.Id`, never to `Slug` — rename, disable, archive, or hide never touches a
   historical event's reference. A slug-change escape hatch was deliberately not built (it would
   need a redirect/alias mechanism nothing here requires yet); the existing zero-usage delete path
   is the fix for a genuinely wrong slug.
3. **Rich metadata gets real typed columns; `MetadataJson` is a one-time escape hatch, not a
   dumping ground.** `Description`, `IconKey` (a storage key, matching Speaker/Sponsor's
   `photo_key`/`logo_key` — no upload widget exists anywhere in `admin/` to extend, so this stays
   a pasted key), `Color`, `Badge`, `SearchKeywords` are columns. `MetadataJson` exists only for
   fields nobody has asked for yet; the day a second concrete field is requested it becomes a real
   column in a follow-up migration.
4. **Delete stays hard-delete, gated strictly on zero usage AND zero children** — unchanged from
   the pre-existing `CategoryService.DeleteAsync` (`category_in_use`/`category_has_children`
   guards), now with the audit write it was missing. Disable/Archive/Hide are the everyday tools;
   physical delete is the rare exception. Archived restores to Disabled, never straight to Active —
   a deliberate two-step.
5. **Import is merge-only — there is no "replace" mode anywhere in the API.**
   `PreviewImportAsync` matches incoming nodes to existing rows by slug (create/update/conflict/
   error), `ApplyImportAsync` refuses to run at all if the preview reported any hard errors, and
   even on success only ever creates missing-slug rows or updates existing-slug metadata — it
   never deletes a row absent from the import file and never touches `Status`/`IsVisible`. Export
   is the same tree keyed by slug (portable across environments), with a plain download/upload UI,
   not a polished diff viewer.
6. **A real usage count and a real reorder endpoint, not manual number-editing.**
   `UsageCountsAsync` is one grouped query per FK column (`CategoryId`/`TypeId`/`AudienceLevelId`),
   never per-row — the same batch-aggregate shape as this session's `EventService.EventStatsAsync`.
   `POST /v1/categories/reorder` takes `{parent_id, order[]}` (`parent_id` nullable — reorders the
   top-level Audience rows), validates every id shares that parent, and updates `Sort` in one
   transaction. The admin UI renders this as Move Up/Down; real drag-and-drop is a frontend-only
   follow-up the API already supports.
7. **Every mutation is audited with a full-row snapshot, not a partial diff.** `CategoryService`
   had zero `IAuditWriter` calls before this; every create/update/disable/enable/archive/restore/
   duplicate/reorder/delete/import/capability-change now writes one, with `Before`/`After` carrying
   every column, not just what changed — the deliberate discipline that makes a future
   "view/compare/rollback previous versions" screen a pure read over `audit_logs` later, not a new
   table now. A cheap, real `Version int` (bumped on every mutation) ships today as a
   change-detection signal; a whole-tree numbered "Taxonomy Version N" concept was evaluated and
   declined — it implies undecided product semantics (per-field vs. per-batch, draft/publish) that
   nothing in this pass asked for.
8. **`CategoryCapabilityDefault(Id, CategoryNodeId, CapabilitySlug, State)` reuses the existing V3
   Capability catalog (~45 slugs — `teams`, `certificates`, `scoring`, `check-in`, `paid`,
   `seat-map`, `waitlist`, `sub-events`, `sponsors`, …) rather than inventing new capability names,
   and is deliberately keyed by a real FK to `EventCategory.Id` — not DB-constrained to Type level —
   instead of the fragile mechanism the platform already has for this. Investigation found
   `Event.KindSlug` (a plain string, not a FK) is resolved at event-create time by matching a
   Type's exact `Name` against a hardcoded 145-entry C# dictionary
   (`KindCatalog.TypeNameToKind`) into one of 20 fixed `EventKind` rows, which then map to
   `KindCapabilityDefault(KindSlug, CapabilitySlug)` — seeded once at boot, never reacting to a
   taxonomy edit, with no admin UI anywhere. `CategoryCapabilityDefault` is the designed target for
   a **future** pass to change `CapabilityService.GetForEventAsync`/`ResolveStates` to resolve
   through `TypeId` directly and retire `EventKind`/`KindAlias`/`KindCatalog` — this pass does not
   make that resolution change (materially riskier, touches live event-creation code), only ships
   the schema + admin CRUD (`GET`/`PUT /v1/categories/{id}/capabilities`, Type-level only) so the
   data exists and is real the moment a future pass wants it. Because the table isn't Type-only at
   the DB level, a later capability-*inheritance* pass (Audience → Category → Type cascading
   defaults, considered and explicitly declined as premature this pass — zero live consumers yet)
   needs a new resolution algorithm on this same table, not a migration.
9. **Reuses the existing `KurxAdmin` policy — no new permission system.** Every mutation is
   already its own endpoint (disable/archive/duplicate/reorder/import/export/capabilities, never
   one mega-PATCH), so a future narrower `TaxonomyManager` role is a one-line policy change per
   route later, not a redesign; inventing a bespoke fine-grained permission scheme used nowhere
   else in this console would have been inconsistent, not safer.
10. **`EventTaxonomySeeder` is bootstrap-only.** `SeedAsync` now starts with
    `if (await db.EventCategories.AnyAsync(ct)) return;` — the per-slug `Ensure`/reconciliation
    loop (which existed only to support "the code array is the permanent source of truth") is
    gone. A fresh database gets one bulk insert of the same 161-node starter content; any database
    that already has rows — from this seeder or an admin — is never touched again. The Admin
    Console is the source of truth from first boot onward.
11. **The old flat `/categories` screen was retired only after the new one reached and exceeded
    parity** — the review pass caught two real gaps before deletion (no search/filter box, and no
    way to toggle Visibility from the edit view at all), both fixed, before `categories-manager.tsx`
    and its page were deleted and the `"Catalog" → "Categories"` nav entry removed in the same
    change as adding `"Platform" → "Event Taxonomy"`.

**Backend.** `EventCategory` gains (all additive — nothing dropped): `Status`, `Description`,
`IconKey`, `Color`, `Badge`, `SearchKeywords`, `MetadataJson`, `Version`, `CreatedAt`/`UpdatedAt`,
`CreatedBy`/`UpdatedBy`. New `CategoryCapabilityDefault` table. One migration
(`AddPlatformTaxonomyManagement`), verified to preserve all 161 existing rows with a correct
`Status`/`Version`/`CreatedAt` backfill. `CategoryService` grows from 4 methods to ~18
(create/update/delete/disable/enable/archive/restore/set-visible/duplicate/reorder/list/
list-for-admin/usage-counts/export/preview-import/apply-import/get-capabilities/set-capabilities)
— one cohesive bounded context, the same shape `EventService` already has in this codebase for
event lifecycle. New `GET /v1/admin/categories` (enriched, `KurxAdmin`) alongside the unchanged
public `GET /v1/categories` — mirrors the `AdminEventView`/`EventSummary` split from D-186.

**Frontend.** New `admin/app/(console)/platform/event-taxonomy/` (page + stats panel),
`admin/components/admin/taxonomy/` (`taxonomy-workspace.tsx` — tabbed Audience/Category/Type
`DataTable` with search and Move Up/Down reorder; `taxonomy-detail-sheet.tsx` — create/edit/
lifecycle/duplicate/delete/capabilities in one `Sheet`; `taxonomy-import-export.tsx` — the
Preview→Apply merge flow). `admin/lib/api.ts`/`admin-actions.ts` extended with the full new
surface. Verified additive and backward-compatible against both real consumers: Flutter's
`EventCategoryDto` (`freezed`/`json_serializable`) only parses the fields it explicitly declares
(confirmed it doesn't even read `slug`/`sort` today) so new JSON fields are safe by construction;
`web/lib/api.ts`'s `categorySchema` (Zod, not `.strict()`) is the same. `web/`'s Create Event
wizard needed no code change — it already fetched categories/types live on every load; only the
backend's default filter (now `Status == Active && IsVisible`, was `IsVisible` only) changed
underneath it.

**Verification.** Full container `dotnet build -warnaserror` (0 errors) and `dotnet test`
(container sharing `kurx-postgres`'s reachable network so `KurxApiFactory`'s hardcoded
`Host=localhost` resolves correctly — a real environment issue hit and fixed this session, not a
code defect); `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint`, `next build` clean on `admin/` and `web/`. New
`PlatformTaxonomyManagementTests.cs` covers create/audit-snapshot, slug immutability, the full
lifecycle state machine, public-vs-admin visibility filtering, Type-only duplicate, reorder
(including the null-parent Audience case and parent-mismatch rejection), delete blocked by
usage/children and allowed when neither, real usage counts against seeded events, Type-only
capabilities reusing the real registry, export→reimport round-trip, an unresolvable-parent import
correctly erroring and refusing to apply, a genuinely new node importing via merge, and every
write route rejecting a non-admin.

**System-impact audit follow-up (post-approval, same day).** A 35-point whole-platform dependency
trace found one real gap and fixed it in this same decision's scope: `EventService.CreateAsync`/
`UpdateAsync` validated a submitted `CategoryId`/`TypeId`/`AudienceLevelId` by `Level` match only,
never by `Status` — so a client already holding a Disabled/Archived node's id could still submit
it for a new event, or re-select it on update, bypassing the "hidden from Create Event" intent
that was previously enforced only where the picker *reads* the list, not where the event-creation
*service* validates the write. Fixed: both blocks now also require `Status == Active`; the update
path only fires this check when a field is actually being *changed* (already guarded by the
existing `is not null` check), so an event that already references a since-disabled node is never
retroactively blocked from unrelated edits. Two regression tests added
(`Creating_an_event_against_a_disabled_category_is_refused`,
`An_event_already_using_a_since_disabled_category_can_still_be_edited_for_anything_else`).
Everything else traced (backend endpoints, EF/Dapper/AutoMapper/repository-layer — none of the
latter three exist in this codebase —, SignalR, notifications, background jobs, search, analytics,
recommendations, payments/ticketing, moderation, profile pages, event cards, Flutter/Web/Admin
API consumers) was confirmed unaffected by direct code inspection, not assumption.

**Deferred Improvements** (intentionally out of scope for this decision, not oversights — do not
let these block the next phase):
- Capability inheritance (Audience→Category→Type cascading defaults over `CategoryCapabilityDefault`).
- Wiring `CategoryCapabilityDefault` into live event-capability resolution
  (`CapabilityService.GetForEventAsync`/`ResolveStates`) — see the V3-conflict note below first.
- A real drag-and-drop reorder UI (the API already supports it; only Move Up/Down shipped).
- A polished import diff-viewer (today: a plain to-create/to-update/conflicts/errors list).
- An icon upload widget (`IconKey` is a pasted storage key today, matching Speaker/Sponsor's
  existing `photo_key`/`logo_key` pattern — no upload widget exists anywhere in `admin/` yet).
- Effective-dating (`ActiveFrom`/`ActiveUntil`) — the selectability check is centralized in one
  method (`CategoryService.IsSelectableForNewEvents`) specifically so this is a one-place change later.
- A whole-tree version/draft-publish/rollback UI (every mutation already writes a full-row audit
  snapshot, making this a read-only feature over `audit_logs` later, not a new table now).
- FluentValidation request validators for the new bodies (`ReorderBody`, `ImportBody`, etc.) — today's
  validation is real and enforced, just at the service layer rather than the FluentValidation pipeline
  other admin endpoints use.
- An index on `event_categories.ParentId` — inconsequential at 161 rows; add when the taxonomy
  approaches the "thousands of Types" scale this decision was explicitly designed to support.

**Architectural tension with the frozen V3 program (D-131), found after this decision shipped —
raised to the user and resolved same-day. See D-189 for the full reconciliation**: taxonomy is the
platform's admin-owned classification/config layer; Kind/Capability remains V3's internal
behavioral engine; the two are complementary systems with different jobs, not competing
implementations of the same thing. D-188 stands as built, not rolled back, not redesigned.

## D-189 · Taxonomy (D-188) and Kind/Capability (V3, D-131) are two coexisting systems with different jobs, not competing implementations of the same concept (2026-07-29)

**Context.** Before starting V3 Phase 16, a whole-platform impact audit for D-188 cross-checked it
against `docs/architecture/EVENT_ARCHITECTURE_V3.md` ("frozen, not to be redesigned") and found
apparent direct conflict: V3 §21.2's strangler migration says the legacy `CategoryId`/`TypeId`/
`AudienceLevelId` columns should become **"read-only shadows"** and eventually stop being written
at all (`legacy_*`, kept only as an audit trail); §21.3 Phase 0 called to **"freeze new type
additions"**; §14's elimination table lists **"Category (derive [from Kind])"** as a duplicate
concept to be removed, not grown. D-188 instead built a full CRUD/lifecycle/metadata/
capability-bridge admin surface *for* the legacy taxonomy — on its face, the opposite of freezing
it. Raised to the user rather than resolved unilaterally, since it's a product-ownership question,
not a technical one.

**Decision — the product clarification, not a technical compromise.** The platform taxonomy
(Audience/Category/Type) was never meant to be user-generated, before or after D-188. Organizers,
hosts, and every other non-admin caller only ever *select from* the platform-approved taxonomy when
creating an event — that was true of the pre-D-188 hardcoded seeder and remains true today; D-188
changed *who edits the taxonomy and how* (Platform Admin, live, via the console — no code change,
no deploy), not *who the taxonomy belongs to* (still the platform, never the organizer). Read that
way, D-188 is an **operational improvement to an already-platform-owned system**, not a reversal of
V3's ownership model.

**V3's "Category (derive [from Kind])" is about analytics/discovery grouping, not about who may
edit the taxonomy catalog.** Kind is V3's closed, ~20-value *behavioral* classification — it decides
what capabilities an event gets (Team Registration, Certificates, Judging, Check-in, Seat Map, …)
and is the primary dimension for search/discovery/analytics grouping once V3 Phases 16–17 ship.
Taxonomy (Audience/Category/Type) is the *administrative* classification an organizer picks from
in the Create Event form — the human-facing catalog, not the machine-facing behavior engine. These
answer different questions ("what should this event be filed under, for people to find it" vs.
"what should this event be able to do") and can coexist exactly as they already do today: a Type
selection resolves to a Kind via `KindAlias` at event-create time (unchanged by D-188), the Kind
then drives capability defaults (unchanged by D-188). D-188 did not touch, duplicate, or compete
with that resolution path — `CategoryCapabilityDefault` is a new, *separate* table, not a rewrite of
`KindCapabilityDefault`, explicitly not wired into live capability resolution (D-188's own text).

**Disposition:**
- D-188 stands exactly as built. Not rolled back. Not redesigned. Not rescoped.
- Platform Admins (SuperAdmin, `KurxAdmin` claim) own taxonomy management — unchanged, already true.
- Organizers/hosts/every non-admin caller cannot create, rename, delete, import, or export taxonomy
  — already true before D-188 (writes were always `KurxAdmin`-gated) and unchanged by it.
- Kind/Capability remains V3's frozen behavioral model — this decision does not touch, does not
  reinterpret, and does not deprecate `EventKind`/`KindAlias`/`Capability`/`KindCapabilityDefault`.
- **Future work that touches both must integrate, not replace.** Concretely: if/when a future pass
  wires `CategoryCapabilityDefault` into live capability resolution (already named as deferred work
  in D-188), it integrates *alongside* the existing Kind-based resolution — e.g. as an override layer
  or an eventual migration target — decided explicitly in its own D-NNN when that work is scoped, not
  assumed here. No future feature should build a second, parallel "what can this event do" system.
- `docs/architecture/EVENT_ARCHITECTURE_V3.md` is left untouched — it stays frozen, describing the
  Kind/Capability behavioral engine correctly. This decision is the taxonomy-ownership clarification
  that sits alongside it, not an edit to it.

**Consequences.** No code changes from this decision — it is a documentation/ownership clarification
only. V3 Phase 16 (Search & discovery) proceeds next per `docs/roadmap/README.md`, unblocked.

## D-190 · Event Architecture V3 — Phase 16 client completion: Web + Flutter discovery UI, closing the §12 backlog; sort-parameter regression found and fixed (2026-07-29)

**Context.** D-184 (2026-07-25) shipped Phase 16's backend — outbox-fed FTS+trigram index, deterministic
ranking, eligibility-aware `/for-you` feed — explicitly scoped "backend only," with client wiring tracked
as the roadmap's §12 Client Integration Backlog. This closes that backlog: Web and Flutter now consume
every filter D-184 added (kind, mode, price) plus the `/for-you` feed, with a UX pass (chips, active-filter
indicators, loading/empty/error states, quick-browse rails) reusing each platform's existing design system
(`Chip`/`Skeleton`/`ErrorState`/`Badge` on Web via `@kurx/ui`; `KurxChip`/`HomeSkeleton`/`ErrorRetry` on
Flutter) rather than inventing new visual language. Admin was confirmed out of scope — the only Admin
deliverable ever attributed to "Phase 16" was a taxonomy admin UI, already shipped by D-188.

**Decisions.**
1. Kind/Mode/Price filters added to both clients' existing search surfaces — Category/Kind stay dropdowns
   (cardinality: 13/20 values), Mode/Price become chip toggles (`Chip`/`ChoiceChip`, 3-4 values) — a
   deliberate cardinality-based split, not every dropdown converted to a chip.
2. Active-filter summary + one-tap individual removal on both platforms: plain server-rendered links on
   Web (preserving `/discover`'s existing URL-as-state architecture — no client JS added), controller
   calls on Flutter (`KurxChip.onDeleted`, a small, justified extension of the existing chip component).
3. `/for-you` recommended rail on both platforms, gated on signed-in state — Web's `/discover` already
   sits behind the app shell's `requireSession()`; Flutter reuses the existing `isGuest` check the same
   file already used for the sign-out button. Never called for a guest; confirmed server-side too (401
   without a token, live-tested).
4. New `KindChips` quick-browse rail (Web + Flutter), mirroring Flutter's pre-existing `CategoryChips`
   rail-into-filtered-search pattern.
5. Explicitly deferred, not built (named rather than silently skipped): proximity/location filtering (no
   geolocation package on Flutter — a new dependency plus a permissions flow); language picker (no UI
   source); recent searches / saved filters / search history (no backend persistence exists for any of
   them — would require backend work, out of this client-only phase); `Cache-Control` caching on
   `/v1/categories`/`/v1/kinds` (a real, cheap future lever — D-188's own plan already named it — not
   applied here to keep this phase backend-untouched); a dedicated category/kind browse page on Web
   (Flutter has one; a real net-new page, not a D-184 deliverable); Flutter i18n (none exists platform-wide
   today, not retrofit as a side effect); filter-usage analytics (needs new backend event tracking).
6. **Bug found and fixed during runtime integration verification** (explicitly requested as a final gate
   before approval): `SearchService.RankedIdsAsync` — D-184's "one canonical ranked query" (M4) — never
   read `EventListFilter.Sort` at all. Every `sort` value both clients already sent (pre-existing UI,
   unrelated to this phase) was silently ignored after D-184's cutover from the old `EventService`-based
   ordering; uncaught because `SearchDiscoveryTests.cs` never asserted `sort` behavior. Fixed:
   `date_asc`/`date_desc`/`newest` are now honored as literal `ORDER BY` overrides; `popular`/null/
   unrecognized keep the existing deterministic score-based default — no new sort value invented, no
   change to the ranking formula. New regression test `Sort_parameter_controls_result_order`.

**Verification.**
- Web: `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint`, `next build` — all clean.
- Flutter: `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` (new `KindDto` codegen), `flutter
  analyze` — 0 errors (5 pre-existing test fakes updated to implement the 2 new `EventsRepository`
  methods; 62 remaining info/warning-level issues are pre-existing, confirmed unrelated by file path).
- Backend: zero files touched by the client-wiring work itself; the one bug-fix file (`SearchService.cs`)
  verified by a fresh full container-suite run against real Postgres — **802 passed / 1 skipped / 0
  failed** (803 total; the skip is the pre-existing, unrelated `RefundLedgerTests` concurrency case).
- Live connectivity/contract check against the running `kurx-backend` container (curl, real responses):
  `/v1/kinds` and `/v1/categories` return real data matching both clients' schemas exactly (field-for-field,
  extra server fields safely ignored by non-strict Zod/json_serializable parsing); `/v1/events` with
  combined filters returns the correct `{items,total}` shape including the empty case; `/v1/events/for-you`
  returns 401 with no token, confirming server-side auth independent of client-side gating.
- Zero `backend/`/`admin/` files touched other than the one `SearchService.cs` sort fix.

**Status: APPROVED / COMPLETE (2026-07-29).** V3 Phase 16 (Search & discovery) is now complete end-to-end
— backend (D-184) and client (this decision). Phase 17 (Analytics rebuild) is next per the roadmap.

## D-191 · Admin Event Management production completion — moderation-not-mutation policy, Super Admin Emergency Edit as an exceptional path over the same update core, bulk operations, CSV export, pagination/audit-filter/reviewer-access gaps closed (2026-07-29)

**Context.** A production-readiness audit of D-186/D-187 found the module mostly real but not complete:
real backend pagination (D-187) was never adopted by the admin frontend (hardcoded `limit: 100`, `total`
discarded, no pager — the exact symptom D-187 fixed server-side was still visible client-side); the
table's column-sort was dead (`sortable: true` with no `onSortChange` wired); `GET /v1/admin/audit` had no
`entityId` filter, so the event Timeline tab scanned all `events`-entity rows client-side; a
`VerificationReviewer` without org membership 404'd on the event-detail route (`EventEndpoints.cs`'s
`IsAdmin()` checked only the `kurx_admin` claim); Suspend/Unsuspend/Hide/Unhide/Message/Warn had zero test
coverage; and bulk operations + CSV export never existed (already tracked, not new). Separately, the audit
surfaced a real architectural ambiguity: `EventService.UpdateAsync`'s `CanManage(isAdmin, role)` bypass let
any `kurx_admin` token edit any org's event content — with **no audit event written at all** for that path.

**Decision 1 — normal admin moderation never mutates organizer-owned content.** `ActionBar`
(`event-workspace-sheet.tsx`) is a deliberately-curated moderation toolkit (Approve/Reject/Suspend/Hide/
Archive/Delete-draft/Message/Warn) that never included Edit — consistent with D-186's own philosophy of
moderation as **orthogonal overrides**, never content mutation. `EventService.UpdateAsync`'s `isAdmin`
bypass is removed; content edit now requires a real per-org role (`OrgRole.Owner`/`Manager`/
`Representative` — the same set `CanManage` already granted, minus the admin bypass). The `isAdmin` bypass
remains valid, unchanged, for every genuinely admin-owned method (`SetFeaturedAsync`,
`SetModerationFlagAsync`, `NotifyOrganizerAsync`, `TransitionAsync`'s reviewer branch) — those are
moderation, not mutation, and were never in question.

**Decision 2 — a Super Admin Emergency Edit exists, as an exceptional path over the same update core, not
a second implementation.** Verified first that nothing like this existed anywhere in the platform. Built as
a thin wrapper, not a parallel code path: `UpdateAsync`'s entire body (material-change snapshot, field
validation, taxonomy/venue/mode validation, tag sync, capability re-materialization, reindex enqueue) was
extracted into one shared private core (`ApplyUpdateAsync`); `UpdateAsync` and the new
`EmergencyUpdateAsync` both call it. The only things that differ are exactly the four the review asked for:
**authorization** (real org role vs. `kurx_admin`/SuperAdmin only — the live-claim is already SuperAdmin-
exclusive, no new role plumbing), **required reason** (`EmergencyUpdateAsync` rejects an empty reason
before doing anything), **audit behavior** (`EmergencyUpdateAsync` writes one `admin.event.emergency_edit`
audit event with a full before/after row snapshot — replay-capable, matching D-188's `CategoryService`
snapshot-audit pattern; `UpdateAsync` itself still writes none, unchanged, matching every other
organizer-self-service write in this codebase), and **route entry point**
(`POST /v1/admin/events/{id}/emergency-edit`, separate from the organizer PATCH route). Future changes to
what "updating an event" means are made once, in `ApplyUpdateAsync`, and both paths inherit them —
there is no second update implementation to keep in sync.

**Decision 3 — the remaining gaps are closed as scoped fixes, not redesigns.** Reviewer detail-view 404:
`GetAsync`'s admin path recognizes `VerificationReviewer` (via `IPlatformRoleService`), not only
`kurx_admin`. Audit `entityId`: one additive filter param on `GET /v1/admin/audit`, replacing the client-
side `.filter()` scan in `page.tsx`'s `loadWorkspace`. Pagination: the admin frontend adopts the `page`/
`total` the backend has returned since D-187; no backend change. Column-sort: wired to the same `sort`
param the existing dropdown already controls (one state, not two). Bulk operations
(`POST /v1/admin/events/bulk`) loop the existing single-event moderation methods — never a second
moderation implementation — and require the same `reason` those methods already require for
suspend/hide/reject/archive. CSV export reuses `AdminEventListFilter` (no second filter parser) and the
`AnalyticsService.ExportEventAnalyticsCsvAsync` CSV-building convention (no second CSV approach).

**Verification.** Full container suite, real Postgres, final run: **824 passed / 1 skipped / 1 failed** (826
total). 19 new tests (`AdminEventManagementTests.cs`) cover every gap: suspend/unsuspend/hide/unhide/
message/warn mutation + audit; a mixed-batch bulk action (2 succeed, 1 not-found fails, reported
individually, **and asserted to leave the same `admin.event.suspend` audit rows the single-event route
would** — bulk is not a second, unaudited path); CSV export headers/rows; the audit `entityId` filter
(using a `SuperAdmin` token — the `Audit` policy is distinct from `VerificationReviewer`, a real fix over
this entry's first draft, which used the wrong persona and got an empty 403 body); **sorting**
(`sort=revenue` orders two VAR-seeded events highest-first — the pre-existing backend sort logic, confirmed
still correctly routed through `statsScopedSort`, not a plain-SQL fallback); **filtering survives
pagination** (a city filter narrows the same 3 matching events across two pages of a 4-event set, a
non-matching city never appears on either page); non-overlapping pagination pages; a Reviewer without org
membership viewing event detail; the tightened `UpdateAsync` policy (org-role succeeds, `kurx_admin` alone
now `forbidden`); Emergency Edit (missing reason `400`, non-SuperAdmin `403`, SuperAdmin + reason succeeds
with a real before/after audit snapshot containing both the original and new title).

**The one remaining failure, investigated fresh (not reasserted from memory).** `DevAuthTests.
Verified_organizer_scenario_grants_paid_capability` — `git status`/`git diff --stat`, checked at the moment
of this verification, show `DevAuthEndpoints.cs`/`DevAuthService.cs`/`DevRegistry.cs` **currently** modified
with 407 insertions / 100 deletions by a concurrent, separately-owned session, mid-flight on a legacy-to-
new auth-configuration migration — `DevAuthEndpoints.cs`'s own new comment reads *"Preset/Scenario are the
legacy string-key contract, kept only for..."* (truncated, in progress). `DevAuthTests.cs` (untouched by
this session) still calls the old `{scenario: "verified-organizer"}` contract, which 404s against the
in-progress replacement — the concurrent session's own transition state, not a D-191 or Phase 17 defect,
and not fixable here without editing code this session does not own mid-refactor. **Not fixed, isolated
and documented, exactly as instructed** — this is the one pre-existing, external, actively-owned exception
"0 unexpected failures" excludes by its own terms. The one skip
(`RefundLedgerTests.Concurrent_refunds_of_the_same_order_reverse_it_only_once`) carries its own
`[Fact(Skip = "...")]` reason citing D-103, unrelated and pre-existing, confirmed by reading the attribute
directly, not assumed.

Two real bugs were found and fixed by this same pass, not shipped broken: `OrgEventListTests`' revenue
fixture needed `ValueAllocationRecord` rows (it was seeding raw `Orders`, which Phase 17's VAR-based
revenue correctly no longer reads); the bulk endpoint's response was serializing camelCase by ASP.NET's

match (the frontend's `bulkActionResultSchema` already expected the correct snake_case shape, so this was a

`admin`: `tsc`, `next lint` both clean. Architecture review: `BulkActionResult`'s removal left zero dead
references; `CanManage` remains used, unchanged, at every other call site it always was — only
`UpdateAsync` lost the bypass, confirmed by a full-codebase grep, not asserted from memory. Runtime

real Postgres, real authorization middleware, not a mock — the standalone `kurx-backend`/`kurx-admin`
docker-compose containers were deliberately not rebuilt/redeployed this pass (a separate deploy step, not
