## D-192 · Event Architecture V3 — Phase 17: Analytics rebuild — read-time leaf-fact aggregation replaces the pre-computed rollup tables; two real bugs found and fixed by the mandated regression pass (2026-07-29)

**Context.** V3 §16/§9.5: `EventAnalyticsDaily`/`OrganizationAnalytics` were nightly-job pre-aggregated
tables — a second, derived copy of numbers already present in leaf-fact tables (`ValueAllocationRecord`,
`Registration`, `Ticket`, `EventView`, `Refund`), always as stale as the last job run. Phase 17 retires
both tables and the job that filled them (`DailyAnalyticsAggregationJob`), replacing them with **read-time
aggregation** over the leaf facts — one new seam, `IAnalyticsFactSource`/`LeafFactSource`
(`Kurx.Infrastructure/Analytics/AnalyticsFactSource.cs`), that `AnalyticsService` (public contract,
`IAnalyticsService`, unchanged in shape apart from the new `includeDescendantUnits` rollup flag) and
`EventService`'s own batch list-row stats both delegate to — one canonical computation for every number,
everywhere it's shown, matching §9.5's revenue/refund invariant ("VAR is the sole basis for revenue
reporting AND refunds — they can never diverge because they read the same rows").

**Decisions.**
1. `IAnalyticsFactSource`/`LeafFactSource` is `public`, not `internal`, only because C# requires a
   DI-constructed public class's constructor parameters to be at least as accessible as the class itself
   (`AnalyticsService`/`EventService` are both public) — by convention it is never referenced outside
   `Kurx.Infrastructure`.
2. Revenue is **gross** — VAR rows are never deleted or negated by a refund (`RefundService` only reads
   VAR to determine the refund amount). `RefundCountAsync`/the day-fact `RefundCount` column is the
   separate signal that a refund happened; nothing nets it against revenue. This is a deliberate design
   choice (gross sales and refunds reported as separate line items), not an oversight — verified by a new
   test asserting revenue is unchanged immediately after a refund, and that the refund amount matches the
   same VAR-sourced number revenue reads.
3. `RevenueForOrgAsync(orgId, includeDescendantUnits, ct)` — the dual-tree rollup toggle — has no
   product-facing way to exercise the "non-root" side yet: `IOrgUnitService` exposes only
   `EnsureRootAsync`/`ResolveOrgRoleAsync` this phase, so every event auto-binds the org's root unit and no
   API assigns one to a descendant. The new rollup test therefore seeds a child `OrgUnit` and re-points an
   event's `OrgUnitId` directly at the DB layer (the same pattern `OrgUnitTests` already uses for its own
   descendant-permission-walk test) to prove the query itself is correct ahead of that assignment
   capability existing — documented here explicitly rather than left as a silent gap.
4. `admin`/`web`/`mobile`: zero files touched. D-184's routes and DTOs were already the leaf-fact shape;
   this phase only changed how the numbers behind them are computed. Confirmed by a repo-wide grep for
   every removed type/method name — the only remaining hits are historical per-migration `.Designer.cs`
   snapshots (expected to keep describing the schema as it was at that point in time) and one doc comment.

**Two real bugs found and fixed by this phase's own new tests, not shipped broken.**
1. `RefundCountAsync` and `DailyFactsAsync`'s refund grouping filtered `Status == RefundStatus.Processed`
   — but `RefundService.RefundOrderAsync` always leaves a refund at `Initiated` ("the platform's books are
   reversed now, but the customer has not been paid back until a real gateway disburses it" — `Processed`
   is set nowhere in the codebase, that flip is deferred future work). Refund count would have silently
   read 0 for every refund that has ever happened. Fixed to filter `Status != RefundStatus.Failed` — an
   Initiated-or-Processed refund counts; a Failed attempt doesn't.
2. `ScopedEventIdsAsync`'s `includeDescendantUnits: false` branch scoped to "every event under the org"
   rather than "the root unit's own events" — making the rollup toggle a true no-op even in the scenario
   where an event genuinely was assigned to a descendant unit (decision 3's DB-seeded test scenario), not
   only in today's no-real-API-assigns-subunits case. Fixed: `false` now scopes to the root unit only
   (falling back to the org's whole event set only if the org somehow has no root yet); `true` widens via
   the materialised `OrgUnit.Path` prefix as before. Caught by the new
   `Org_revenue_rollup_includes_a_descendant_units_event_only_when_asked` test, which failed
   (`Expected: 10000, Actual: 35000`) before this fix.

**One pre-existing, unrelated test-flakiness bug found incidentally and fixed.**
`OrgEventListTests`' shared `NewEvent` helper generated `ShortCode` from 6 hex characters (~16.7M
keyspace); `Scales_to_a_thousand_events_without_loading_all_rows` seeds 1000 rows from it in one loop,
a real (~3%) birthday-collision chance against the real unique index on `events.ShortCode` — unrelated to
any Phase 17 change, just unlucky on this pass's regression run (`23505: duplicate key value violates
unique constraint "IX_events_ShortCode"`). Fixed by widening to 8 hex characters (negligible collision
risk at that scale); not a length Phase 17 or any production code relies on, purely internal test-fixture
uniqueness.

**Tooling finding, not a code bug.** `dotnet test` invoked without an explicit `-c Debug`/`--configuration
Debug` leaves `$(Configuration)` empty at the point `Directory.Build.props` evaluates its `DEV_AUTH`
compile-gate condition (`'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug' Or '$(EnableDevAuth)' == 'true'`) — `Directory.
Build.props` is imported before the SDK's own default-Configuration-to-Debug logic runs. The practical
effect: all 8 `DevAuthTests` (D-125) silently fail to compile and vanish from the run with no error, no
warning, just a lower total (818 instead of 829) — caught only because this pass cross-checked the total
against the previously-recorded D-191 baseline rather than accepting "0 failed" at face value. Every
`dotnet test` invocation for this backend must pass `-c Debug`/`--configuration Debug` explicitly.

**Verification — regression.** Full container suite, real Postgres, explicit `-c Debug`: **828 passed / 1
skipped / 0 failed** (829 total — 826 D-191 baseline + 3 new Phase 17 tests). The 1 skip carries its own
pre-existing D-103 `[Fact(Skip=...)]` reason, unrelated to this phase. **The one prior failure is now
genuinely fixed, not merely isolated:** re-investigating `DevAuthTests.
Verified_organizer_scenario_grants_paid_capability` down to the actual `DevRegistry.cs` source (rather than
re-stating the diffstat) found the concurrent session's in-flight D-125 cleanup had *already made a final,
coherent decision* — `"verified-organizer"` was removed from `LegacyScenarios` because it was a
byte-identical duplicate of the `LegacyPresets` entry of the same name ("one button kept, labeled by the
real OrgRole name," `DevRegistry.cs`'s own comment). The persona was never broken; only the JSON key the
test used to reach it was retired. Verified empirically (a throwaway probe test, deleted afterward) that
`{preset: "verified-organizer"}` returns 200 with `identity_verified`/`bank_verified`/`can_organize_paid`
all true, then updated the test itself — `DevAuthTests.cs` only, zero files owned by the concurrent
session touched — renamed to `Verified_organizer_preset_grants_paid_capability` and switched to the
current, still-supported key. 3 new tests (`RefundLedgerTests.
Refund_amount_matches_the_VAR_revenue_and_revenue_stays_gross_after_refund`,
`EventRegistrationTests.Distinct_checkin_count_dedupes_a_person_across_sub_events_of_the_same_parent`,
`OrgUnitTests.Org_revenue_rollup_includes_a_descendant_units_event_only_when_asked`) cover the three
genuinely-new Phase 17 capabilities that had no coverage.

**Verification — live runtime.** `docker compose build backend` from the current source (the standing
container was still running pre-Phase-17 code) + restart; startup log confirms `RemoveAnalyticsRollupTables`
applied cleanly against the real dev `kurx` database. Exercised end-to-end over real HTTP with real OTP
login (no dev-auth shortcut — the Release build doesn't compile `DEV_AUTH` by design, D-125's own layer-1
guarantee): created a live org owner session, published a free event, generated a real `EventView` (public
unauthenticated read) and a real `Registration` via a second buyer account. Confirmed live and correct:
`GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/analytics` (both `includeDescendantUnits=false/true` — identical, correctly, since
this event sits on the org's auto-bound root and no product API assigns non-root units yet); event sales
timeline, attendance, per-ticket-type revenue, and CSV export (`Date,Views,UniqueVisitors,...` header +
one real data row); `GET /v1/admin/analytics`'s `top_events` (the query rewritten off `events.ViewCount`
onto `EventViews` this phase) showing the live event with its real view count; both `GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/events`
and `GET /v1/admin/events`' batch stats rows (`tickets_sold`/`checked_in`/`revenue_paise`) — all sourced
through `EventService`'s delegation to `IAnalyticsFactSource`, matching the same numbers the dedicated
endpoints show. Every response shape matched what `admin`'s/`web`'s existing Zod schemas already expect,
confirmed field-for-field, live, not just by static contract reading. Refund-reverses-nothing and the
parent/sub-event distinct-attendance dedup were not separately re-exercised live (no product-facing HTTP
path creates a sub-event tree or a refund cheaply without a full paid+KYC+reviewer flow) — both are
covered by dedicated, real-Postgres integration tests instead, named above. All live test data (the event,
its ticket type/order/ticket/registration/view row, the throwaway buyer account, and a temporary
SuperAdmin grant used only to reach the admin endpoint) was deleted afterward; the dev database is back to
its pre-verification state.

**Verification — architecture.** Repo-wide grep confirms: zero references to `DailyAnalyticsAggregationJob`
anywhere; zero remaining `events.ViewCount++`/`+=` increments (D-130 already retired the inline increment
before this phase; Phase 17 only removed the nightly job that used to re-derive it, so `ViewCount` was
already frozen pre-existing, not newly staled by this work — confirmed by checking the deleted job's last
committed version, which never touched `ViewCount` either); every `IAnalyticsService` method has exactly
one real call site (its own endpoint) — no dead interface members; the one other `Sum(v =>
v.AllocatedPaise)`-style query outside `AnalyticsFactSource` (`AnalyticsService.GetEventRevenueAsync`'s
per-ticket-type breakdown) is a genuinely different dimension (grouped by `TicketTypeId`, not a duplicate
of the event/org-level sum) that `IAnalyticsFactSource`'s contract doesn't expose, reviewed and confirmed
legitimate rather than duplicate logic. API contracts unchanged — confirmed both statically (D-192's first
pass) and now live (this pass).

**Tooling documentation.** The `-c Debug` MSBuild finding is recorded in `.claude/memory/testing-standards.md`
— the repo's own designated owning file for backend testing conventions per `CLAUDE.md` §9 — not left in
a private note, so it survives across contributors and sessions.

**Status: APPROVED / COMPLETE (2026-07-29).** Every objective of this final verification gate is met: 0
unexpected regression failures (genuinely fixed, not isolated), live runtime verification against a
freshly rebuilt Release container passed on every analytics surface, architecture verification confirms
one source of truth for revenue/attendance/views with no legacy path and no dead code, and the tooling
finding is committed to the repo. V3 Phase 17 (Analytics rebuild) is complete. Every V3 wave (A–E) is now
✅ — Phase 17 was the last item in the 18-phase program (Phase 17→9,4 was its only hard-ordering
dependency, both long since complete). **Event Architecture V3 is complete.**

## D-193 · Independent review of D-185–D-192 — 6 discrepancies found, all fixed; no redesign (2026-07-29)

**Context.** A separate, concurrent Claude session (this repo's other standing workstream, see
[[kurx-concurrent-workstreams]] in the assistant's own memory) independently verified every claim in
D-185 through D-192 by reading the actual code — not trusting this log's prose — via three isolated
research passes plus a real `dotnet build`/`dotnet test` run in Docker against real Postgres. Result:
14/14 Platform Taxonomy claims confirmed, 13/13 Analytics-rebuild claims confirmed, the backend test
suite reproduced exactly (828 passed/1 skipped/0 failed, 829 total, `-c Debug`), `admin`'s `tsc --noEmit`
clean. Two areas had real, if minor, discrepancies between what was documented and what the code
actually did. Per the reviewing session's own mandate ("do not redesign or rebuild those features, fix
the review findings"), all six are closed here as scoped fixes, not a rework of D-186–D-192.

**Discrepancies found and fixed.**
1. **Moderation "reason" was optional everywhere despite D-191 reading "require... reason."**
   `ModerationActionBodyValidator` (single-event suspend/hide) had no `.NotEmpty()`; the bulk endpoint had
   no validator attached to `BulkEventActionBody` at all. Fixed: `ModerationActionBodyValidator.Reason` is
   now `.NotEmpty()` (applies to both suspend and hide, which share the validator); a new
   `BulkEventActionBodyValidator` requires `Reason` only `.When(x => x.Action is "suspend" or "hide")` —
   unsuspend/unhide/approve/reject/archive are untouched, since none of those routes to a method that
   stores a reason in the first place (approve/reject/archive go through `TransitionAsync`, which has no
   reason field at all — adding one is a separate, larger decision than this validation fix, not made
   here, not silently implied either). Both admin dialogs (`event-workspace-sheet.tsx`'s single-event
   `ReasonDialog`, `events-workspace.tsx`'s `BulkReasonDialog`) updated to mark the field required (and,
   for bulk, only required when the selected action is suspend/hide) rather than round-tripping to the
   server to discover it's missing.
2. **`AdminEventManagementTests.cs` has 13 `[Fact]`s, not the 19 D-191 claimed.** Documentation
   correction only — every named gap category genuinely has coverage; the count in D-191 was simply
   wrong. Not fixed by padding the suite with filler tests to hit a number.
3. **`web/components/ui/chip.tsx`'s `Chip` was a separate local implementation, not an import of
   `@kurx/ui`'s `Chip`** — the exact anti-pattern D-185 itself wrote into
   `.claude/memory/frontend-conventions.md` ("do not duplicate a primitive locally... promote it
   instead"). Root cause: `web`'s copy had grown a second export, `ChipLink` (a server-renderable `<Link>`
   variant `@kurx/ui`'s `Chip` didn't have — a real, legitimate gap, not a frivolous fork). Fixed by
   extending `@kurx/ui`'s `chip.tsx` with `chipClass` + `ChipLink` (matching the file `web` already had,
   verbatim) and turning `web/components/ui/chip.tsx` into a plain re-export shim — the same
   single-source pattern D-185 already used for `Badge`/`Card`/`EmptyState`. Zero call-site changes
   needed; every existing import of `Chip`/`ChipLink` from `@/components/ui/chip` still resolves.
4. **No `KindChips` component existed on the Web side** (D-190 claimed "New `KindChips` quick-browse
   rail (Web + Flutter)") — it was inline JSX in `discover/page.tsx`. Fixed by extracting a real
   `web/components/events/kind-chips.tsx`, mirroring Flutter's `KindChips` (both are now thin wrappers
   over their platform's shared chip primitive — `ChipLink` here, `KurxChip` there).
5. **`EventCard`'s `badge` prop was dead** — added, never passed by any of its 5 call sites across
   `web/`. Removed (deletion over speculative future use); `Badge`'s import dropped from `event-card.tsx`
   accordingly.
6. **D-190 cited `ErrorState`/`Badge` as reused in the discover flow; neither is actually wired in** —
   the error path is a legitimate hand-rolled retry link (`ErrorState` needs an `onRetry` callback,
   incompatible with a Server Component), and `Badge` was the dead prop just removed. Documentation
   overstatement only, recorded here rather than silently left for a future reader to trust at face
   value.

**Verification.** Full container rebuild + `dotnet test -c Debug` re-run after all fixes (see this
entry's own follow-up verification note below, filled in once that run completes); `admin`'s
`tsc --noEmit` re-run clean. No test required modification — every existing single-event and bulk
suspend/hide test call already passed a non-empty `reason`; the one bulk test with no reason
(`Bulk_endpoint_rejects_an_unknown_action_and_an_oversized_batch`) only asserts `400 Bad Request`, which
the new validator produces just as validly as the pre-existing batch-size check it was originally
targeting.

**Consequences.** D-186–D-192 stand exactly as built otherwise — this is a fix-in-place pass, not a
redesign, per instruction. No new backend surface, no new tables, no schema change. The one deliberately
NOT-fixed item (approve/reject/archive having no reason field at all) is named here as a real, scoped-out
gap rather than silently bundled into "reason is now required," so a future reader doesn't assume more
was enforced than actually was.

## D-194 · Admin-scoped organization list & detail — closes the standing "no admin org read" gap (2026-07-29)

**Context.** `admin/STATUS.md` §5.4 documented a long-standing gap, independently confirmed by D-186
point 8: no endpoint let a platform admin browse organizations. `GET /v1/orgs` returns only the
caller's own orgs; `GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}` 404s to non-members by design (D-018 anti-enumeration);
`GET /v1/orgs/search` excludes non-`Verified` orgs (it's the public discovery registry). The old
`admin/organizations` page could only act on an org whose GUID the operator already had — moderation
existed, browsing didn't.

**Decision.** Extend, don't duplicate, the exact pattern D-186 already established for events:
1. `IOrgService.GetAsync` gains `bool isAdmin = false` — the same one-parameter admin-bypass shape
   every other org-scoped service already has. When `true`, it skips the D-018 membership check;
   `ToDetail`'s `role` becomes `"admin"` rather than a fabricated real membership role.
2. New `IOrgService.ListForAdminAsync(AdminOrgListFilter, ct)` — paginated, searchable (name/slug/
   domain via `ILike`), filterable by verification status and org type, mirroring
   `IEventService.ListForAdminAsync`'s `(Items, Total)` shape (D-186/D-187). Member/event counts are
   two grouped queries over the current page only, never per-row.
3. `GET /v1/admin/orgs` (list) and `GET /v1/admin/orgs/{orgId}` (detail) added to the existing,
   already-`VerificationReviewer`-gated `/v1/admin/orgs` route group — no new policy invented.
4. The org detail workspace (`admin/components/admin/org-workspace/`) composes wallet/risk/events
   from functions D-186 already built for the event workspace's Organizer tab
   (`getOrgWalletAsAdmin`, `getFraudScore`, `listOrgEventsAsAdmin`) — these existed but had no entry
   point of their own until this pass. `OrgAdminTools` gained an optional `defaultOrgId`/`defaultOrgName`
   prop so opening an org from the list pre-fills moderation instead of requiring a re-typed GUID.
5. A real bug in `OrgEndpoints.cs` was caught and fixed by this change, not shipped broken: adding
   `isAdmin` as a new parameter before the existing trailing `ct` parameter would have silently broken
   the organizer-facing `GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}` route's positional-argument call (`ct` would bind to the
   new `bool` slot). Fixed with a named argument; a regression test
   (`Organizer_self_service_read_still_works_after_the_isAdmin_signature_change`) guards it.

**Verification.** 8 new tests (`AdminOrgManagementTests.cs`) — two initially failed on first run for
reasons in the *test code*, not the implementation, found and fixed during this same pass rather than
weakened: a search query that didn't actually appear as a substring of the seeded org names, and an
event-creation call missing the now-required `categoryId`. Full container suite after both fixes:
**836 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed** (837 total — 829 prior baseline + 8 new). `admin` `tsc --noEmit`
clean.

**Consequences.** Closes the exact gap named by two independent sources (D-186, `admin/STATUS.md`
§5.4) at two different times. No new permission model, no new backend service, no schema change.

## D-195 · Completing the Web → Admin trust/safety migration (org verification, membership claims, fraud/blacklist, org moderation, doc viewer)

**Context.** `web/app/(app)/host/admin/*` (org verification, membership claims, fraud blocklist, org
suspend/blacklist/merge, the evidence-document viewer) was never a second, permanently-coexisting
implementation — an 8-phase architectural investigation (this session, not repeated here) proved from
primary sources that it was always the temporary D-055 prototype the dedicated `admin/` console's
equivalents were explicitly built to **port** from and retire: D-051 (2026-07-13) itself calls the
admin console UI "Pending Stitch UI... deferred... generated + wired later"; the commit that first
built `admin/`'s UI (`832a9c4`, 2026-07-17) describes web's copy in its own message as "the D-055
prototype these admin pages port"; `admin/ADMIN_AUDIT_AND_ROADMAP.md` (07-15) planned the port
explicitly ("port it to `admin/`, don't rewrite"); and an independent later audit
(`docs/PLATFORM_AUDIT_M8.md`, 07-19) flagged the still-dual state as "worth consolidating." No roadmap
item, present or planned, was ever found to depend on web retaining these pages.

**Decision.** Complete the migration, preserving every capability, never deleting before redirecting:
1. The 5 web pages/routes (`verifications`, `claims`, `fraud`, `orgs`, `doc/[id]`) became thin
   `redirect()` shims to their admin equivalents (`/verification` — combined org+claims,
   `/blacklist`, `/organizations`, `/verification/doc/[id]`) via a new `NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_URL`
   (`web/lib/site.ts`'s `siteConfig.adminUrl`), rather than being deleted outright — an existing
   bookmark or the sidebar's `reviewerNav` (which now points straight at the absolute admin URL,
   avoiding an unnecessary bounce) both still land somewhere real.
2. `web/lib/dev-session-config.ts`'s `destinationFor()` — a genuine dependency found only during
   implementation, not the original investigation — special-cased `super-admin`/`moderator` to web's
   panel; it now falls through to the same "no web destination, land on `/profile`" bucket every
   other platform role already used, and testers needing the actual reviewer UI use admin's own
   `/dev-login` (confirmed to already carry `super-admin`/`moderator` legacy presets).
3. Only after redirects were verified live (real OTP login against the running `kurx-backend`
   container, a real `VerificationReviewer` grant, and a real cookie sent cross-app to `admin` on a
   different port — confirmed the same session is recognized, per the investigation's Phase 3 proof)
   were the now-dead `web/components/host/{review-form,blacklist-manager,org-admin-tools}.tsx`,
   `web/lib/admin-actions.ts` (deleted whole — every one of its 6 actions was this feature), and the
   12 duplicate `web/lib/api.ts` functions + their schemas (`pendingOrgSchema`, `verificationDocSchema`,
   `pendingClaimSchema`, `orgStatusSchema`, `blacklistEntrySchema`) removed. `membershipClaimSchema`
   and its two legitimate self-service functions (`getMyMembershipClaims`, `submitMembershipClaim` — a
   user's own claims, not the admin review queue) were kept; only the admin-only
   `reviewMembershipClaim` was removed, confirmed by checking every other call site first.
4. `is_platform_reviewer` (the `Me` field gating `reviewerNav`'s visibility) was **not** removed — it's
   not dead, it still correctly decides whether a signed-in web user sees the "jump to admin" nav links
   at all; only the links' destination changed.

**A real bug found and fixed during implementation, not shipped broken.** Two of the five redirects
(`verifications`, `claims`) initially returned `200 OK` with the real content never rendering, instead
of a clean redirect, discovered by live verification against the running Docker stack rather than
assumed from a green typecheck. Root cause: both routes still had a sibling `loading.tsx` (needed by
their old data-fetching pages, not by a page that now just calls `redirect()`), which wraps the route
in a Suspense boundary — Next.js 14's App Router commits to an HTTP 200 for the streamed shell before
the inner Server Component resolves, so the redirect was delivered only as a client-side RSC
instruction (correct in a real browser, but not a clean 307 for curl/crawlers/any non-JS caller, and
inconsistent with the other 3 routes). Fixed by deleting the two orphaned `loading.tsx` files; re-verified
clean 307s on all 5 routes afterward. A second, smaller gap found the same way: `web/Dockerfile` never
declared `NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_URL` as a build `ARG`, so it would have silently fallen back to its
hard-coded default in any environment — fixed by adding it alongside the existing
`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_LOGIN` args, in both `web/Dockerfile` and
`docker-compose.yml`.

**Verification.** Real OTP login against the live `kurx-backend` container (code read from its own
stdout log, not dev-auth — the Docker image is a Release build and doesn't compile `DEV_AUTH` by
design, D-125's own layer-1 guarantee); a real `VerificationReviewer` grant via direct DB insert into
`platform_roles` (cleaned up afterward); all 5 redirects confirmed 307 to the correct absolute admin
URL; all 4 real admin destination pages confirmed 200 for that session; the doc-viewer confirmed a
correct 404 for a nonexistent document id (not a crash); unauthenticated requests confirmed still
gated by web's own login, unchanged; `reviewerNav`'s rendered HTML confirmed to contain the correct
absolute admin URLs. `web` `tsc --noEmit` clean before and after every removal step; a repo-wide grep
confirmed zero remaining references to any deleted file. Backend, `admin/`, and Flutter: confirmed
untouched — this decision's only files are in `web/`, `.env.example`, `docker-compose.yml`, and this
log.

**Consequences.** One less place (`web/lib/api.ts` no longer redefines) to keep the org-verification/
membership-claim/fraud/blacklist contract in sync when the backend changes — the exact duplication
`docs/PLATFORM_AUDIT_M8.md` flagged in 2026-07-19 as "worth consolidating" is now closed.
`admin/STATUS.md`'s standing "worth consolidating" note is resolved by this entry.

**Deferred, not forgotten.** The redirect shims (`web/app/(app)/host/admin/*/page.tsx`,
`doc/[id]/route.ts`) are left in place rather than removed outright — they're cheap, harmless, and
exist precisely so a stale bookmark or an out-of-repo support link never 404s. Real production
domain/session topology for `web` vs. `admin` (whether cookies transfer the same way in whatever
actually deploys this, beyond this repo's own `docker-compose.yml`) remains unverified, as does any
out-of-repo support runbook that might reference the old URLs — both explicitly named as unproven
rather than assumed, in the original investigation and here.

## D-196 · Developer Mode production-readiness audit — no code changes; three real findings deferred (2026-07-29)

**Context.** A 12-phase audit of Developer Mode itself (D-125): inventory, architecture, feature/role/
scenario coverage, cross-platform comparison, real API validation, security/compile-guard verification,
real browser automation, code quality, future-readiness. Explicitly an audit, not a build — "do not
modify code unless explicitly approved after the audit."

**Method.** Native Debug backend (Linux container, Smart App Control workaround per
`kurx-container-test-runner`) + native web/admin dev servers. Real dev-login sessions minted and
confirmed live via `/v1/me` against real Postgres. Real Playwright (full `chromium-1228`, not the
headless-shell variant, which hangs) — 12 browser checks, 0 failed, across both apps' `/dev-login`.
API-level coverage: all 5 `PlatformRole`s, all 11 legacy presets, all 6 `UserState`s, 5 error/edge cases.

**Findings (all deferred — none previously approved for fixing in this pass).**
1. An orphaned `/v1/dev/auth/impersonate` route.
2. Flutter's dev-login preset list is not filtered to exclude platform-staff-only presets.
3. The global rate limiter (`Program.cs`'s `AddRateLimiter`, 60 req/min anonymous-IP) has no Developer
   Mode exemption — rapid automated QA against `/v1/dev/auth/*` can self-trigger 429s.
4. `DeveloperSeedService.EnsureOrgAsync` (`backend/Kurx.Infrastructure/Dev/DeveloperSeedService.cs:62-66`)
   branches only `College` vs. "everything else," so selecting **Community** representation in dev-login
   silently seeds/reuses the **Company** org rather than a distinct Community org. Confirmed live (identical
   org id returned for Community and Company configs) and in source. Compiled out of Release
   (`#if DEV_AUTH`), zero production impact — a QA-tooling bug, not fixed here (Low severity, not
   previously approved).

**Consequences.** No files changed. Developer Mode confirmed to mint real, DB-backed sessions via the
same `IAuthService` path as OTP login (refresh token present on every dev-minted response, same shape).

## D-197 · Full platform functional verification — no code changes; one real UI bug found, commerce path identified as untested (2026-07-29)

**Context.** Where D-196 verified Developer Mode itself, this pass used it as the entry point to verify
the platform it unlocks: every feature area named in the audit brief (auth, profile, identity/KYC, org
verification/claims/browsing, event lifecycle, taxonomy, discovery, wallet, certificates, announcements,
chat reachability, reports/fraud/blacklist/audit/analytics/bulk-ops), plus authorization boundaries.

**Method.** Same native Debug stack as D-196. ~55 of 349 backend routes driven live end-to-end — chosen
to cover every named feature area, not a random sample. A real Organization-Pending→Verified flow and a
real Membership-Claim submit→approve flow were driven through the actual API (`representation-requests`
→ `admin/orgs/pending` → `verification/review`), not dev-login shortcuts — closing the exact gap D-196's
scenario matrix couldn't reach (dev-login can't seed org-verification states; the real API can create
and approve them for real). A full event lifecycle (create→publish→edit→feature/suspend/hide→emergency-
edit→close→archive→delete) was driven for real, including the paid-event `submit_review`→reviewer-
`publish` gate. Discovery's outbox-fed index (`OutboxDispatchJob`, `Cron.Minutely()`, V3 §15/D-184) was
proven live: a published event was absent from `/v1/events` at t+0s and present at t+65s, then cleaned
up — confirmed working as designed, not a bug. 31 real Playwright checks across every built admin page
(`admin/STATUS.md`'s inventory) plus key web pages.

**Findings.**
1. **Real bug.** `admin/app/(console)/audit/page.tsx` and `admin/app/(console)/users/[id]/page.tsx` are
   Server Components that define a `columns` array containing `render: (r) => <JSX>` closures and pass it
   directly into `DataTable` (`@kurx/ui`, a Client Component) — Next.js throws "Functions cannot be passed
   directly to Client Components" 10-11 times per page load. Every one of the other 13 `DataTable`
   consumers in this codebase avoids this by wrapping columns+table in a `"use client"` component; these
   two pages are the only ones that skip that pattern. Medium severity (other columns still render, page
   doesn't crash) — not fixed this pass.
2. **Genuine, named gap identified rather than worked around**: the entire commercial event
   lifecycle — Orders, Payments, Refunds, Ticket purchase, Attendance, QR, Gate check-in — was not
   exercised. TicketType creation worked; driving a full order through `MockPaymentGateway` did not
   happen in this pass. Explicitly the trigger for D-198.
3. Two pre-existing Flutter widget-test failures (229/231 pass), unrelated to any change this session
   (zero mobile files touched) — likely stale test expectations (`home_dashboard_page_test.dart` expects
   exactly one "Trending" widget, finds two) rather than confirmed regressions; not chased to a full root
   cause.

**Consequences.** No files changed. Authorization held with zero privilege escalation across every
boundary tested. Verdict was explicitly "REMAINING FUNCTIONAL GAPS," not a pass — the commerce path gap
and the audit-page bug are both carried forward with exact evidence rather than papered over.

## D-198 · End-to-end commerce & event lifecycle verification — no code changes; Refund confirmed to have zero HTTP surface, certificate cold-start root-caused (2026-07-29)

**Context.** The one gap D-197 named on purpose: drive the full commercial workflow for real — organizer
setup through a real paid purchase, QR check-in, certificates, refund, moderation, authorization,
cross-application sync — using the native Debug backend + `MockPaymentGateway`.

**Method.** Real `Venue` entity (not inline event fields) → Draft event → a **paid** ticket type (₹500,
deliberately paid, not free, so money actually moves) → `submit_review`→reviewer-`publish` (the paid-event
gate found in D-197, now driven on purpose) → a second, distinct dev-seeded account discovers, opens, and
orders the ticket → real `razorpay_order_id` → real webhook (`VerifyWebhookSignature` always `true` in
dev) → order flips `Pending`→`Paid`. Real gate scan (admitted, ticket state `Issued`→`CheckedIn`) followed
by a duplicate scan (correctly rejected, `is_duplicate: true` with the original check-in time/staff name).
Certificate generation with a real checked-in attendee produced `{generated:1}` (vs. D-197's `{generated:0}`
with no attendees) — closing that PARTIAL. Moderation as SuperAdmin (hide→suspend→emergency-edit→
unhide/unsuspend→close→archive) with organizer-view and public-view checked at each step. Cross-application
sync confirmed by real Playwright rendering (not just API responses) in both admin (`/events`) and web
(`/host/events`, a *third*, independently dev-seeded organizer session) — both showed the identical event,
status, and ₹500 revenue.

**Findings.**
1. **Refund has no HTTP surface at all — confirmed, not assumed.** `IRefundService.RefundOrderAsync`
   (`backend/Kurx.Application/Abstractions/IRefundService.cs`) is fully implemented
   (`backend/Kurx.Infrastructure/Orders/RefundService.cs`, D-103: reverses the ledger, debits the wallet,
   voids tickets, replay-safe) but is wired to zero routes — grepped every `Kurx.Api/Endpoints/*.cs` file
   (zero "refund" matches) and live-probed two plausible routes (both 404). There is also no request/
   approve/reject queue model in the service at all — it's a direct one-shot action, not a workflow. This
   is the single reason D-198 could not return a clean verdict.
2. **Certificate generation's first call after a cold backend start takes ~26.7s; the second call in the
   same warm process takes ~293ms** — a ~91× difference, proving a one-time cold-start cost (almost
   certainly SkiaSharp/QuestPDF font-subsystem initialization,
   `backend/Kurx.Infrastructure/Providers/DocumentProviders.cs`'s `CertificateRenderer`) rather than a
   per-certificate scaling problem. Real production risk: whoever's request is first to hit a freshly-
   restarted backend eats ~27 seconds. Not fixed this pass (root-caused, not patched).
3. Email/WhatsApp delivery confirmed genuinely working via the explicit resend endpoint
   (`[email→console]`/`[whatsapp→console]` logged with real subject/recipient/attachment) — but nothing
   fires automatically on payment confirmation itself (`OrderService.ConfirmPaymentAsync` never calls the
   email/notification layer; only `ResendTicketAsync`/`ResendGuestOrderAsync` do). Flagged as a product-
   decision gap, not asserted as a bug.

**Consequences.** No files changed. Verdict was explicitly "REMAINING FUNCTIONAL GAPS." Both findings
(Refund's missing HTTP surface, certificate cold-start) are the named objectives of D-199.

## D-199 · Refund HTTP surface + certificate cold-start warm-up — the two D-198 findings closed (2026-07-29)

**Context.** D-198 found `IRefundService.RefundOrderAsync` (D-103) fully implemented but wired to zero HTTP
routes, and certificate generation's first call after a cold backend start taking ~26.7s (vs. ~293ms warm).
This entry implements both fixes — explicitly *not* another audit, not an architecture change.

**Decision — Refund API.** `RefundOrderAsync` itself is untouched, byte-for-byte (10+ existing integration-
test call sites in `Kurx.Tests` call it directly; changing its signature was avoidable and therefore not
done). `IRefundService` gained four additive members instead:
1. `RequestRefundAsync(orderId, reason, actorId, isFinanceStaff, ct)` — authorizes, then delegates to the
   unchanged `RefundOrderAsync`. Authorization mirrors `WalletService.HasFinancialAccess` exactly (org
   `Owner`/`Finance`, resolved from the order's event's org), with a `FinanceOps`/`SuperAdmin` platform
   override — no new permission model.
2. `GetForOrderAsync`, `MyRefundsAsync`, `ListForAdminAsync` — the read side the service never had, because
   nothing outside the test suite could reach it before.
`backend/Kurx.Api/Endpoints/RefundEndpoints.cs` (new) maps `POST`/`GET /v1/orders/{orderId}/refund`,
`GET /v1/refunds` (mirrors `GET /v1/orders`'s "my tickets"), and `GET /v1/admin/refunds` (`RequireAuthorization
("FinanceOps")`, the pre-existing policy — SuperAdmin or FinanceOps, unchanged). The attendee/buyer can read
their own refund but not initiate one; Support (platform role) is blocked from both, matching D-197/198's
established authorization-matrix discipline (only Owner/Finance/FinanceOps/SuperAdmin may move money).

**Decision — certificate cold-start.** Root-caused, not guessed: `ICertificateRenderer` is a DI singleton
(`services.AddSingleton<ICertificateRenderer, CertificateRenderer>()`), so the ~26.7s cost is paid once per
process, not per certificate — proven in D-198 by a second real call in the same warm process taking
~293ms (~91× faster), almost certainly SkiaSharp/QuestPDF's font-resolution path (`Fonts.Calibri`) doing
first-use native/font-cache initialization. Fix: `CertificateRendererWarmupService` (new, `IHostedService`,
`backend/Kurx.Infrastructure/Providers/DocumentProviders.cs`), registered via
`services.AddHostedService<CertificateRendererWarmupService>()`. Fires one throwaway `RenderAsync` call in
the background during app startup — fire-and-forget by design, so a slow (or even failing) warm-up never
delays the app from accepting traffic or becoming healthy; on failure, the first real request simply pays
the cost itself, exactly as before this fix. The certificate engine itself (`CertificateRenderer`,
`ComposeClassic`/`ComposeModern`) was not touched.

**Verification.**
- **Refund API**: `RefundEndpointsTests.cs` (new, 8 tests, real HTTP against real `kurx_test`) — Owner
  refunds successfully with wallet/ledger/ticket/audit all updating; a second refund of the same order
  is idempotent (`already_refunded`, wallet debited exactly once); org `Finance` role succeeds,
  `Representative` is blocked (403); the buyer cannot self-initiate (403) but can view their own refund
  once staff processes it, and it appears in `GET /v1/refunds`; `Support` is blocked from initiating,
  viewing, and the admin list (403 on all three); `FinanceOps` and `SuperAdmin` can refund any org's order;
  `GET /v1/admin/refunds` is FinanceOps-gated and 401s unauthenticated; refunding a nonexistent order 404s.
- **Certificate warm-up**: measured live on a freshly-started native Debug backend. Startup log:
  `"Certificate renderer warm-up completed in 26034ms"`. The first *real* HTTP call to
  `POST /v1/events/{id}/certificates/generate` afterward — the exact request a real user would make —
  completed in **720ms** (previously 26,678ms on an unwarmed process): a ~37× improvement, landing in the
  same range D-198 measured for an already-warm second call.
- **Regression**: full suite, same container recipe as every prior pass this session —
  **844 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed / 845 total** (837 prior baseline + 8 new). `admin`/`web` `tsc --noEmit`
  clean (no frontend files touched — this entry is backend-only). No other `IRefundService`/
  `ICertificateRenderer`/`IQrCodeGenerator` implementation or mock exists anywhere in the codebase, so
  neither change had a ripple effect to check for beyond the tests already covering both interfaces.

**Consequences.** `admin/STATUS.md`'s Refunds row updated: the backend gap is closed; only the admin
console's own `/refunds` page remains unbuilt (out of scope here — no UI work was requested or done).
`docs/api/README.md` gained the Refunds section. D-198's two open findings are both closed; nothing else
from D-196/197/198 was in scope for this entry (the orphaned impersonate route, Flutter's unfiltered
preset list, the rate-limiter's missing dev-mode exemption, the Community-org-aliasing bug, and the
audit-page/user-detail RSC violation all remain exactly as documented, untouched, not silently rolled in).

## D-201, D-202, D-203, D-205, D-206 · Professional Identity System — Allies, event/participation
dedup, source-agnostic Achievements, and the Verified-Identity kickoff reconciliation (2026-07-30)

**Context.** A product-architect directive to replace the thin public-profile page with a
"verified professional identity" system — explicitly not a social/vanity profile — built on real
platform data only. Full spec: `docs/architecture/PROFESSIONAL_IDENTITY_SPEC.md`. Backend already
had ~80% of this (`PublicProfileService`, the P1 draft named in `kurx-verified-identity`
memory/`VERIFIED_IDENTITY_KICKOFF_PROMPT.md`); this entry extends it in place rather than
building a parallel system.

**Decision — D-205, relationship to the Verified-Identity kickoff doc.**
`VERIFIED_IDENTITY_KICKOFF_PROMPT.md` (undated prior session, marked "APPROVED — do not
redesign") locks a heavier target architecture: an `IdentitySignal` append-only event index with
INGEST→COMPUTE→SERVE tiers, "no new source-of-truth tables" for the identity/projection layer,
and Allies-adjacent graph work explicitly deferred to a later phase gated on more V3 data. This
session's directive is more direct: extend `PublicProfileService` in place, add schema only where
data doesn't already exist. Reconciliation: **Allies is not part of the Identity-Signal
projection layer** — it's a new first-class relationship (the same category as `Membership` or
`OrganizationFollower`, D-064), not a derived projection of existing V3 facts, so a new
`AllyConnection` table does not violate the kickoff doc's "no new source-of-truth tables for the
identity layer" rule (that rule governs the read/aggregation layer, which still owns zero tables
of its own). The new aggregation logic in `PublicProfileService` is written as separable
per-source methods so it could be lifted behind an `IdentitySignal` pull-adapter later — but no
signal contract is built now.

**Decision — D-201, Allies domain model & privacy.** New `AllyConnection` entity/table: one row
per **unordered** user pair for its entire lifetime (`UserLowId < UserHighId`, DB unique index +
`ck_ally_connections_pair_order` check constraint — structurally forbids self-allying too).
State machine `Pending → Accepted/Declined/Revoked`; re-request after Decline/Revoke reactivates
the same row; a crossed mutual request (both sides ask before either responds) auto-accepts
(`ConnectedVia = "mutual_request"`). Non-party caller on a mutation → `not_found` (404, the
hidden-resource convention — never confirm a connection exists to a non-participant); a party
attempting an invalid transition for the current state → `invalid_state` (409). Privacy:
`User.ShowAllies` (new column, default `true`, same convention as `ShowAttended`/
`ShowCertificates`); an ally appears on someone else's public page only if **both** parties have
`ProfilePublic = true` and the connection's own `Visibility = Public` — the one genuinely
non-obvious call, because the relationship being mutual doesn't override the other party's own
privacy choice. `FirstSharedEventId` is computed best-effort at Accept time (earliest public
event both users have real involvement in) and left null rather than fabricated when none is
found. `MutualEventCount` is deliberately **not** a stored column (repo convention: prefer
computed values over stored counters) — it's computed live on read. `LastInteractionAt` is a
reserved, currently-unwritten column — no existing subsystem defines "interaction" yet, so this
entry doesn't invent one. New endpoints: `POST /v1/allies/requests`, `.../{id}/accept`,
`.../{id}/decline`, `DELETE /v1/allies/{id}`, `GET /v1/allies/requests/{incoming,outgoing}`,
`GET /v1/me/allies`, `GET /v1/public/users/{username}/allies`.

**Decision — D-202, event-participant role vocabulary.** The product's 11-word role vocabulary
(Participant/Competitor/Volunteer/Staff/Coordinator/Organizer/Host/Speaker/Judge/Mentor/Sponsor)
maps onto the existing 29 `ParticipantRole` slugs with a pure display-label dictionary — zero new
seed rows. The one non-obvious pair: **Host → `owner`** (whose event it legally is), **Organizer
→ `manager`** (the operational runner) — cheaper than adding a new seeded slug and updating every
place that assumes 29. Slugs outside the 11-word vocabulary still count and render, as a
humanized fallback chip rather than being hidden.

**Decision — D-203, Achievements is source-agnostic, not certificate-tied.** Explicit direction:
achievements must not be tightly coupled to certificate storage, so future sources (e.g. an
organizer-awarded recognition table, if ever built) can be added without redesigning the shape.
Implemented as a merge of two independently-swappable methods returning the same
`AchievementCard{Name, Description, IconKey, EarnedAt, Source, EventTitle?, EventSlug?, OrgName?}`
shape: certificates with `Kind ∈ {Winner, RunnerUp, Finalist, Appreciation}` (`Source =
"certificate"`), and `UserBadge`/`Badge` platform gamification (`Source = "badge"`) — kept
distinguishable rather than merged indistinguishably, because a badge proves engagement, not
competitive recognition. `ProfileStats.Achievements` counts the certificate-backed source only;
badges are still surfaced in the list, just not folded into that headline number.

**Decision — D-206, organization role labels.** `Membership` carries two independent axes —
`OrgRole` (platform RBAC: Owner/Manager/Staff/Finance/Representative) and, when verified via a
claim, `MembershipClaim.ClaimedRole` (the real affiliation: Student/Faculty/Employee/Alumni/
Founder/Director/Coordinator/Volunteer/ClubPresident/EventLead/Other). The product's org-role
vocabulary (Student/Employee/Organizer/Volunteer/Staff/Coordinator/Member) is the *affiliation*,
not the RBAC role, so the label rule is: show the claim's `ClaimedRole` label when
`SourceClaimId` is set, else fall back to the `OrgRole` label (`Representative` → "Organizer").
"Campus Ambassador" has no backing enum value anywhere — a real gap, not invented; it renders as
"Other" until a real claim type exists. **Correction to the original draft, caught in CI**:
`Membership` carries a DB-enforced unique constraint on `(UserId, OrgId)` — a person holds
exactly one membership row per org, ever (a role change updates that row in place). The org-card
"group by OrgId" logic still stands for forward-compatibility but degrades to a one-row group
under the current schema — `PublicProfileTests` proved this by hitting `23505` when the test
tried to seed two rows for one pair.

**Also shipped, no separate decision needed:** the event/participation/attendance dedup fix (an
event with 2 roles was counting as 2 events — `EventParticipant`'s unique constraint is on
`(EventId, SubjectType, SubjectId, RoleSlug)`, not `(EventId, SubjectType, SubjectId)`; a person
can also hold >1 checked-in ticket for one event). Every count/list now groups by `EventId`
first. `Membership.VerifiedAt` (new nullable column, set at the two existing `IsVerified = true`
call sites in `MembershipVerificationService`/`OrgVerificationService`) backs a new milestone
timeline (`org_joined`/`org_verified` lanes) and closes a real gap — a boolean alone couldn't
answer "verified since when."

**Schema.** One migration (`AddAllyConnectionsAndProfileFields`, generated via `dotnet ef` inside
the SDK container — this environment's `dotnet ef` now works per the updated
`kurx-container-test-runner` memory, retiring the hand-written-migration fallback for this
change): `ally_connections` (new table), `users.ShowAllies` (new column, default `true` —
corrected by hand after `dotnet ef` defaulted the migration's `AddColumn` to `false`, which would
have silently opted every existing user out), `memberships.VerifiedAt` (new nullable column).

## D-207, D-208, D-209 · Allies deep-integration pass — notification wiring, identity on every
real-user list, suggestions/search/mutual-detail (2026-07-30)

**Context.** A full repository gap analysis (Allies vs. mature networking platforms) followed by
a scope-confirmation exchange with the user, resolving to: wire notifications properly, extend
identity onto every existing person-list surface via backend DTO changes, ship a real (if
intentionally narrow) v1 of suggestions/search/mutual-detail, explicitly reject 1:1 chat as an
"integration," and build shared components once instead of page-specific UI. Full write-up:
`docs/architecture/PROFESSIONAL_IDENTITY_SPEC.md` §8.

**Decision — D-207, notification wiring + generic deep-link convention.** `AllyService` now calls
`INotificationService.NotifyAsync` (not a raw `db.Notifications.Add` — the distinction matters,
see the audit: only `NotifyAsync` gives SignalR + FCM for free) for request/accept/decline/an
accepted-connection-being-removed. Revoking a still-`Pending` request stays silent by design — the
addressee never engaged with it, so there's nothing to walk back noisily. New
`NotificationKinds` constants (`ally.requested/accepted/declined/removed`) — existing ad-hoc
`Kind` string call sites (12+) are left as they are, not retrofitted. Every ally notification's
`data` carries a generic `route` field; both web and mobile now follow `route` generically for
*any* notification kind, not just the chat-specific shape they special-cased before — closing a
gap that predates Allies entirely. `ally.requested` additionally carries `connectionId`, so its
notification card renders inline Accept/Decline (reusing the exact same accept/decline calls the
Allies page already uses) instead of only being a tap target.

**Decision — D-208, identity exposed on every real-user list, Sponsor deliberately excluded.**
`AssignmentView` (event Team/Volunteer/Judge/Coordinator/Organizer/Host), `OrgMember`, and
`AttendeeRow` all gained the identity fields (name/username/avatar, plus `IsVerified` for org
members) their underlying rows already had a real `UserId` for — a DTO gap, not a data gap.
`Speaker` gained a genuinely new nullable `UserId` (migration `AddSpeakerUserId`) so an organizer
can optionally link a speaker to a real account when one exists — the common case (a guest
speaker with no Kurx login) correctly shows no Connect affordance at all, never a fake one.
**`Sponsor` is not touched** — it is a brand/company record, not a person, and forcing Connect
onto it would be exactly the placeholder functionality this pass was told to avoid.

**Found and fixed as a direct consequence — a real, pre-existing bug on both clients.**
`AttendeeRow`'s wire format is camelCase — the one endpoint in this API that returns
`Results.Ok(record)` directly rather than a hand-built snake_case JSON object, so it picks up
ASP.NET's default `JsonSerializerDefaults.Web`. Web's `attendeeSchema` was snake_case and mobile's
`AttendeeDto` used field names (`id`/`name`/`email`/`checked_in`) that don't exist on the real
payload at all — both would have thrown or silently rendered nothing on every real load. Neither
had a test or verified integration proving otherwise. Fixed on both platforms in the same pass
that added the new identity fields to the same DTOs, rather than papering over it.

**Decision — D-209, suggestions v1 signals, batch status, mutual detail, search.** Suggestions
rank candidates by exactly two real signals — shared event co-participation and shared verified
organization membership — computed via a handful of set-based queries per request, never one
query per candidate; every other signal named in the original ask (college/company/competition/
speaker-panel/certificate-overlap) is named explicitly as deferred rather than faked, because
each needs data modeling Kurx doesn't have today. `POST /v1/me/allies/status-batch` is the one
call every person-list surface (attendees/team/org-members/speakers/search/suggestions) now uses
instead of a request per card. `GET /v1/me/allies/mutual/{otherUserId}` returns the real shared
events/orgs (reusing the existing intersection helpers), not just a count. `GET
/v1/public/users?q=` is a genuinely new endpoint — public-profile-only, 2-character floor, the
foundation people search/suggestions are built on.

**Explicitly rejected — 1:1 chat.** Kurx chat is deliberately event-room-scoped only (the mobile
code itself has a comment: *"There is deliberately no 'Direct' tab... the product does not have
this feature"*). "Message this ally" would reverse that standing design decision, not integrate
with something that exists. Not built; flagged rather than silently skipped.

**Shared components over page-specific UI.** Web reused the D-201 `UserCard`/`AllyConnectButton`
everywhere a person now renders. Mobile gained the primitive it was missing —
`KurxUserTile` (`mobile/lib/common/widgets/kurx_user_tile.dart`), mirroring `UserCard`
one-for-one — used across attendees, org members, search, and suggestions.

**Files.** Backend: `Kurx.Domain/Entities/EventManagement.cs` (`Speaker.UserId`), new migration
`AddSpeakerUserId`, `Kurx.Application/Abstractions/{IAllyService.cs, IAttendeeService.cs,
IEventAssignmentService.cs, IOrgService.cs, ISpeakerService.cs, IPublicProfileService.cs,
NotificationKinds.cs (new)}`, `Kurx.Infrastructure/{Users/AllyService.cs, Users/
PublicProfileService.cs, Events/{AttendeeService.cs, EventAssignmentService.cs,
SpeakerService.cs}, Orgs/OrgService.cs}`, `Kurx.Api/Endpoints/{AllyEndpoints.cs,
PublicProfileEndpoints.cs, EventAssignmentEndpoints.cs, SpeakerEndpoints.cs, OrgEndpoints.cs}`,
new `Kurx.Tests/PersonListIdentityTests.cs`, extended `AllyConnectionTests.cs`. Web:
`lib/api.ts`, `lib/social-actions.ts`, `lib/event-actions.ts`, new `lib/ally-status.ts`, new
`components/notifications/ally-notification-actions.tsx`, new `components/profile/
{people-search,suggestions-section,mutual-detail-sheet}.tsx`, reworked
`components/notifications/notifications-feed.tsx`, `components/host/{assignments-section,
event-sections}.tsx`, `app/(app)/host/team/page.tsx`, `app/(app)/host/events/[id]/
{team,attendees}/page.tsx`, `app/allies/page.tsx`. Mobile: new `common/widgets/
kurx_user_tile.dart`, new `features/public_profile/presentation/{pages/
people_search_page.dart, widgets/mutual_detail_sheet.dart}`, extended `data/models/
public_profile_dto.dart` + datasource + providers, reworked `features/organizer/
{presentation/pages/{attendees_page,org_members_page,speakers_page}.dart, data/models/
{event_manage_dto,org_dto,event_content_dto}.dart}`, `features/notifications/{domain/entities/
app_notification.dart, presentation/{providers/notifications_providers.dart, pages/

`PersonListIdentityTests`-equivalent DTO tests.

**Verification.** Backend: full suite green in the container runner (see the session's final

issues (2 *fewer* than the 60-issue baseline — no new issues), `flutter test` green with the same

new shapes with realistic payloads mirrored from the actual backend JSON projections.

**Consequences.** No Flutter equivalent of the web "Team" (`EventAssignment`) management screen
exists — a pre-existing mobile feature-parity gap, not something this pass introduced or was
asked to fix. The public event page and the public org page still show no speaker/sponsor/member
roster to anonymous visitors — unchanged, a separate product-surface decision not opened here.

## D-210 · Final repository-wide audit — group/team roster identity, a second camelCase-wire bug
in gamification, review-author profile links, chat sender deliberately deferred (2026-07-30)

**Context.** The user's own closing instruction for the Allies work required "one final
repository-wide audit... to ensure there are no remaining places where a user's avatar or name
appears without opening their professional profile or exposing the appropriate connection state,
except where privacy rules intentionally prevent it." A dedicated audit pass (10 candidate
surfaces: chat, group/team rosters, public event/org pages, leaderboard, certificate verify,
blacklist/audit, invited-by, reviews, judge-as-entity) found four real gaps; this decision covers
what was fixed and, as importantly, what was deliberately left open and why.

**Fixed — Group/Team rosters (web `app/(app)/groups/page.tsx`, mobile `group_detail_page.dart`).**
"Team pages" were explicitly named in the original audit scope, and `GroupMember` already carried
a real `UserId` on the wire — this was a pure DTO/UI gap, not a data gap. Extended
`GroupMemberView` (`IOrderService.cs`) with `Username`/`AvatarKey` (batch-loaded, `ProfilePublic`
users only, same convention as every other list touched in D-208) and wired the existing
`UserCard`/`AllyConnectButton` (web) and `KurxUserTile`/`AllyConnectButton` (mobile) — the exact
pattern already used for attendees/team/org-members/speakers, not a new one.

**Found and fixed — a second instance of the D-208 camelCase-wire bug, this time in gamification.**
`GamificationEndpoints.cs`'s `/leaderboards*`, `/me/points`, `/me/badges`, and `/referrals` all
return `Results.Ok(record)` directly with no snake_case mapping layer, same as `AttendeeRow`
before D-208. The mobile `LeaderboardEntryDto` requested `user_id` (snake_case) and a nonexistent
`avatar_url`; the actual field is `userId` (camelCase) and there was never a backend `avatarUrl` to
receive. Since a `required String userId` field with a missing key throws on parse, this endpoint
was broken for every caller. Fixed the one DTO now being touched (`LeaderboardEntryDto`): correct
casing, drop the phantom `avatarUrl`, add `username` for profile navigation. **Not fixed as part of
this pass:** `/me/points`, `/me/badges`, and `/referrals` show the identical symptom (same file,
same `Results.Ok(record)` pattern) but were not touched — doing so is a distinct, unrelated
gamification bugfix outside the Allies mandate; flagging it here rather than silently leaving it
undiscovered. Also closed a real, adjacent privacy gap while touching this code:
`GamificationService.GetGlobalLeaderboardAsync`/`GetEventLeaderboardAsync` exposed `Username`
unconditionally, without the `ProfilePublic` gate every other identity-bearing endpoint in this
project observes — now gated (`u.ProfilePublic ? u.Username : null`). The leaderboard's `Name`
field remains unconditionally visible, which is the pre-existing, unchanged product design for a
leaderboard (a name is the point of ranking); only the profile-linking `Username` is now gated. New
test: `PersonListIdentityTests.Event_leaderboard_exposes_username_camel_case_and_only_for_public_profiles`.
Web has no leaderboard UI; only mobile (`leaderboard_page.dart`) needed a tap-to-profile
`GestureDetector`/`onTap`, no `AllyConnectButton` — a ranked list is a display context, not a
"people list," so the lighter touch matches the audit's own stated intent (feature completeness,
not bloat).

**Fixed — event review author (web `app/e/[slug]/page.tsx`, `app/(app)/host/events/[id]/reviews/page.tsx`).**
`ReviewView`/`EventReviewService` gained `AuthorUsername`/`AuthorAvatarKey`, gated by **both**
`!IsAnonymous` and `ProfilePublic` — reviews already correctly suppressed `AuthorName` for
anonymous reviews (`x.IsAnonymous ? null : x.AuthorName`), so the new fields follow the exact same
gate rather than introducing a second one. Rendered as a plain profile link on the author's name;
no Connect button — an anonymous-option review list is not a people-directory surface.

**Deliberately deferred — chat sender identity (web `message-bubble.tsx`, mobile
`chat_message_bubble.dart`).** Every chat message shows a sender name/avatar with no profile link
today — a real gap by the audit's own definition. Not fixed: doing so would require changing the
chat message wire format on **both** the REST history endpoint and the live SignalR broadcast
payload (`ChatMessage` has no `senderUsername` field anywhere), which is materially larger and
riskier than a read-DTO extension, and touches a real-time contract this pass did not otherwise
touch. The user's own instruction to "skip 1:1 chat entirely" for Allies reinforces treating chat
as a drawn scope boundary here, not an oversight to rush under an audit deadline. Recorded as a
named, open gap for a dedicated future pass, not silently dropped.

**Non-issues confirmed by the audit (no action needed).** Public event/org pages show no
speaker/sponsor/member roster to anonymous visitors at all (nothing to link — a separate,
unchanged product decision). Certificate verify page (`/verify/[code]`) renders `issued_to` as
static text on a fully anonymous verification page — correctly no link. Blacklist/risk/audit
tooling lives only in `admin/` (D-195) or redirects there. "Invited-by" has no wired real data yet
(`invitation_rsvp_page.dart` is a pre-existing hardcoded placeholder, unrelated to this work).
"Judge" is a `ParticipantRole` slug on `EventAssignment`, not a separate person entity — already
covered by the D-208 Team/assignments work.

**Files.** Backend: `IOrderService.cs` (`GroupMemberView`), `Kurx.Infrastructure/Orders/
OrderService.cs`, `Kurx.Api/Endpoints/OrderEndpoints.cs`; `IGamificationService.cs` unchanged (already
had `Username`), `Kurx.Infrastructure/Gamification/GamificationService.cs`; `IEventReviewService.cs`
(`ReviewView`), `Kurx.Infrastructure/Social/EventReviewService.cs`, `Kurx.Api/Endpoints/
EventReviewEndpoints.cs`; extended `Kurx.Tests/PersonListIdentityTests.cs`. Web: `app/(app)/
groups/page.tsx`, `lib/api.ts` (`groupMemberSchema`, `eventReviewSchema`), `app/e/[slug]/page.tsx`,
`app/(app)/host/events/[id]/reviews/page.tsx`. Mobile: `features/orders/data/models/
order_dto.dart` (`GroupMemberDto`), `features/orders/presentation/pages/group_detail_page.dart`,
`features/gamification/data/models/gamification_dto.dart` (`LeaderboardEntryDto`),
`features/gamification/presentation/pages/leaderboard_page.dart`.

**Verification.** Backend: full suite green (864 passed, 1 pre-existing skip, 865 total — one net
new test). Web: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` green. Mobile: `flutter analyze` 58 issues (no
new issues vs. the established baseline), `flutter test` green.

**Consequences.** Chat sender profile-linking and the `/me/points`/`/me/badges`/`/referrals`
camelCase bug are now named, open, out-of-scope items for future work rather than undiscovered
gaps — the point of the audit was to make every remaining gap a decision, not to reach zero gaps
by construction.

## D-211 · Stabilization pass — closing the independent audit's findings (2026-07-30)

**Context.** An independent (if not disinterested — same agent, disclosed) release-readiness audit
of D-201..D-210 found three Blocking issues and several Medium/Low ones. This entry records the
disposition of every one of them: fixed, deferred-with-reason, or confirmed non-issue. Nothing here
redesigns Allies — every fix is a localized correction to code the audit specifically named.

**Blocking #1 — fixed. Mutual-detail no longer bypasses the target's privacy.**
`AllyService.GetMutualDetailAsync` previously computed shared events/orgs for *any* two user IDs,
checking only per-participation `Public` visibility, never the target's account-level
`ProfilePublic`, and never requiring any relationship between caller and target at all. It now
requires an **Accepted** `AllyConnection` between the two — matching the one place this is
actually surfaced in either shipped client (the "Shared history" toggle between existing allies).
Without one, it returns `{shared_events: [], shared_orgs: []}` — same 200, same shape, no new error
path, so nothing that inspects the response shape breaks; the endpoint just stops disclosing
anything to non-allies rather than 403/404'ing (consistent with D-018's hide-don't-error posture).
Tests: `AllyConnectionTests.Mutual_detail_returns_shared_events_and_orgs_for_an_accepted_ally`
(rewritten to actually accept a connection first — the old version passed by accident, never
exercising the privacy boundary) and the new
`Mutual_detail_is_empty_for_non_allies_regardless_of_the_targets_profile_visibility` (covers a
non-ally with a public profile, a non-ally with a private profile, and a nonexistent user ID — all
empty, none distinguishable from each other, so the endpoint isn't usable as an existence oracle
either).

**Blocking #2 — fixed. `status-batch` now bounds its input.**
`POST /v1/me/allies/status-batch` accepted an unbounded `userIds` array — the sibling
`/suggestions` endpoint already clamps its own `limit` in the same file, so this was a genuine,
self-inconsistent gap rather than a considered choice. Capped at 200 (matching
`AllyService.MaxPendingOutgoing`'s existing order of magnitude) at the endpoint layer only —
`AllyEndpoints.cs` rejects with `400 too_many_targets` above the cap before it ever reaches
`IAllyService`, so the service interface and every other caller are untouched. 200 legitimate
targets in one call is far beyond what any first-party page ever sends (a page of a list, tens of
items). Test: `AllyConnectionTests.Batch_status_rejects_an_oversized_target_list` (200 succeeds,
201 is rejected).

**Blocking #3 — fixed. Public user search now uses the codebase's own established pattern.**
`SearchUsersAsync`'s `ILIKE '%term%'` had no supporting index — `Username`'s existing index is a
plain unique btree (accelerates exact/prefix lookups, not a leading-wildcard substring scan), and
`Name` had none at all. Rather than invent a new search strategy, this reuses exactly what
`OrganizationRegistryService`/`KurxDbContext` already do for org name search: a `pg_trgm`
(`gin_trgm_ops`) GIN index — except applied directly to the existing `Name`/`Username` columns
rather than through a separately-maintained `Normalized*` column, since Users doesn't need the
dedup/canonicalization semantics `Organization.NormalizedName` exists for, just fast substring
search. A `gin_trgm_ops` GIN index natively accelerates `LIKE`/`ILIKE` pattern matching (a
documented, distinct pg_trgm capability from the `%`/`TrigramsAreSimilar` fuzzy-similarity operator
used for orgs) — so `SearchUsersAsync`'s query needed **no rewrite at all**, just the two new
indexes. Migration `AddUserNameSearchIndexes` (`ix_users_name_trgm`, `ix_users_username_trgm`).
One genuine hazard surfaced and is worth recording for future migration work: a second
`HasIndex(x => x.Username)` fluent call on the same property, given via the lambda-selector
overload, gets matched by EF Core to the *existing* unique btree index rather than creating a
distinct one — an early attempt at this fix nearly dropped the uniqueness constraint and tried to
create an invalid `UNIQUE GIN` index (Postgres doesn't support unique GIN indexes at all). Fixed by
using the explicit two-argument `HasIndex(propertyNames, indexName)` overload, which is matched by
name and coexists correctly with the property-expression-based index. `pageSize` was already
clamped to 50 (`PublicProfileEndpoints.cs`) — that bounds the response, not the scan cost, which is
what the new indexes actually fix.

**Medium — OrgMember vs. AttendeeRow/AssignmentView/Speaker/Leaderboard: documented, not changed.**
The audit found `OrgMember` exposes `Username`/`AvatarKey` unconditionally while the others gate on
`ProfilePublic`. The rule is now written down as **two intentional tiers**, not one
inconsistently-applied one: **membership rosters** (`OrgMember` — a `Membership` is itself an
ongoing, mutual organizational relationship; a colleague already knows you're on the team
regardless of your profile privacy) vs. **transactional/derived surfaces** (`AttendeeRow` — a
ticket buyer may have zero relationship with the org beyond one purchase; `AssignmentView`/
`Speaker`/`LeaderboardEntryView` — assignments and speaking slots can include people invited once,
not standing members). `OrgMember` is left as-is; this rule is now written down in
`PROFESSIONAL_IDENTITY_SPEC.md` §5 so the next surface has a rule to follow instead of a coin flip.

**Medium — mobile Speaker's wrong initial Connect state: fixed.**
`speakers_page.dart` hardcoded `initialRelation: AllyRelation.none` for every speaker regardless of
actual status — confirmed self-healing (the backend's idempotent `RequestAsync` corrects it on
first tap) but visibly wrong on load, unlike every sibling list. Fixed by computing real batch
status via `allyStatusBatchProvider` for both the "on this event" and "organisation catalogue"
lists (two separate batch calls, since the catalogue list resolves asynchronously behind its own
`AsyncValueView` and isn't known until the assigned list has already rendered). While already
touching this widget for the fix, also folded in the audit's separate Low finding that
`_SpeakerTile` hand-rolled a `ListTile`+`CircleAvatar` instead of reusing `KurxUserTile` like every
sibling list — same file, same change, no separate pass needed.

**Medium — web error handling / Flutter loading-error consistency: fixed for the surfaces the audit
named, not app-wide.** `web/app/(app)/groups/page.tsx` and `web/app/(app)/host/events/[id]/team/page.tsx`
swallowed a failed primary fetch into an empty list, indistinguishable from "genuinely nothing
here" — both now wrap the fetch in try/catch and render a real error message with
`apiErrorMessage(err)`, mirroring the pattern `host/team/page.tsx` already established (this pass
did not invent a new error-handling convention, it applied the existing one more consistently).
`getAllyStatusBatch`'s own soft-fail-to-`{}` was deliberately left alone in both files — that's an
enhancement, not primary content, and silently degrading to "no connect-state shown" is the correct
behavior for it, not a bug. **Explicitly not fixed**: the web app has zero `error.tsx` files
anywhere (a pre-existing, repository-wide gap predating this feature by a wide margin) — adding
error boundaries app-wide is out of scope for a stabilization pass scoped to this feature's own
files; named here so it isn't lost. Mobile: `allies_page.dart`'s Requests/Sent/Suggestions sections
now show a compact spinner while loading and a compact retry row on error instead of
`SizedBox.shrink()` for both states — while preserving their original "render nothing once
successfully confirmed empty" behavior, which was a deliberate, different design choice from
`_MineSection`'s always-visible `EmptyState`, not a bug.

**Medium — decline cooldown / no `Blocked` state: deferred, unchanged.** Confirmed still true:
`AllyStatus` has no `Blocked` value, and `RequestAsync` allows an immediate re-request after a
`Declined` or `Revoked` row. This was already named "Blocked (future)" in the original spec before
this stabilization pass began. Introducing a cooldown or a `Blocked` state is a genuine new
product/state-machine feature — explicitly out of scope for a pass whose mandate was fixing what
exists, not adding to it. Left as a named, prioritized future item, not silently dropped a second
time.

**Low — fixed where cheap.** Hardcoded `Colors.red` (`ally_connect_button.dart`) →
`context.kurx.danger`; hardcoded check-in icon colors (`attendees_page.dart`) →
`c.success`/`c.muted`; dead, unlabeled overflow `IconButton` (`group_detail_page.dart`, `onPressed:
(){}`, no tooltip) — removed rather than given a fake label, since the menu it implied doesn't
exist and building one is a new feature; inline Accept/Decline on ally notifications had no error
handling on **either** platform — both now catch and display a real error instead of leaving the
buttons silently re-enabled with no explanation.
**Low — reviewed, left as-is.** `org_members_page.dart`'s hardcoded Finance-role color
(`Color(0xFF5C6BC0)`) has no existing semantic token to substitute (the palette has `accent`/`teal`
for the other two roles and nothing for a fourth) — adding a new design-system token for one role
label is a larger change than this finding warrants; noted rather than force-fit to a
misleading existing token (e.g. `danger`, which would wrongly imply something is wrong with a
Finance-role member).

**Files.** Backend: `Kurx.Infrastructure/Users/AllyService.cs` (`GetMutualDetailAsync`),
`Kurx.Api/Endpoints/AllyEndpoints.cs` (batch cap), `Kurx.Infrastructure/Persistence/KurxDbContext.cs`
(two new indexes), new migration `AddUserNameSearchIndexes`, extended `Kurx.Tests/AllyConnectionTests.cs`.
Web: `app/(app)/groups/page.tsx`, `app/(app)/host/events/[id]/team/page.tsx`,
`components/notifications/ally-notification-actions.tsx`. Mobile:
`features/organizer/presentation/pages/speakers_page.dart` (rewritten), `features/public_profile/
presentation/pages/allies_page.dart`, `features/public_profile/presentation/widgets/
